# Awesome Semantic ID Generative Recommendation

> 181 papers on generative recommendation with Semantic IDs (SIDs), each placed by the problem it fixes and the pipeline stage it mainly changes.

## Core Files

- [README.md](README.md): Problem × Stage matrix and the full list of papers.
- [guides/glossary.md](guides/glossary.md): Definitions of every problem and Table 1 value.
- [pages/index/stages.md](pages/index/stages.md): Papers grouped by the stage they mainly change.
- [pages/index/code.md](pages/index/code.md): Papers that link to code.
- [pages/index/poi.md](pages/index/poi.md): Papers on POI and local-life recommendation.
- [data/vocab.yaml](data/vocab.yaml): Controlled vocabulary for problems, stages, and the six Table 1 columns.
- [schema/paper.schema.json](schema/paper.schema.json): JSON Schema for `data/papers/<id>.yaml`.

## ACERec

- Page: pages/papers/acerec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Ctr. + Aux.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: ACERec compresses long Semantic IDs into compact latent tokens with an Attentive Token Merger and adds an Intent Token with a dual-granularity objective, to keep long-ID expressiveness at short-ID cost.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Nine Amazon domains: Sports, Beauty, Toys, CDs, Office, Pets, Baby (2014 edition) and Science, Instruments (2023 edition); users with fewer than 5 interactions excluded; training histories truncated to the 50 most recent items. Sizes: Appendix Table 5 (not restated here).
  - Source: Nine Amazon domains and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#A1.SS3.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#A1.SS3.p2.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-last-out: last interaction for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-last-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (exact scoring over the entire item pool).
  - Source: Full candidate ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.SS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The cold-start analysis buckets test items by training frequency [0, 5] to [16, 20], mixing zero-frequency and low-frequency items; tokenizer exposure is not separated.
  - Source: Frequency buckets of test items in training: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS5.p1.
- **SID**: OPQ semantic IDs with m=32 orthogonal subspaces (8 to 64 tested), each with its own codebook of size M (value not restated); an Attentive Token Merger compresses the 32 tokens into 4 latent tokens for the sequence model. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: OPQ long semantic IDs m=32 with subspace codebooks: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.SS1.SSSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS3.p3; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: No beam search: per-subspace log-probabilities are computed once and every candidate is scored by gathering and summing its code log-probabilities (exact full-catalog scoring). Hardware, inference batch size, and measured latency: not reported in the main text.
  - Source: Parallel subspace matching and score gathering: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.SS3.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.SS3.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.SS3.p5.
- **Results from**: Tables 1-2 (six representative datasets versus ID-based and semantic-ID baselines; the other three in Appendix C.1; HGN, SASRec, S3-Rec, TIGER on Sports, Beauty, Toys copied from the TIGER paper, others reproduced); Figure 3 (semantic ID length); Figure 5 (cold-start buckets on Pets and Baby).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T2, scope stated in https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS2.p1; ID length: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.F3; cold start: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.F5; copied baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#A1.SS4.p1.

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: RPG predicts long OPQ IDs in parallel and decodes over an item graph; ACERec compresses the long IDs into a few latent tokens for sequence modeling and scores all items exactly.; where: ACERec v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p2; Tables 1-2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T2; ID-length comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS3.p3.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates short RQ-VAE IDs by beam search; ACERec uses long OPQ IDs with parallel scoring.; where: ACERec v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p2; Table 1 (numbers copied from TIGER): https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#A1.SS4.p1.
- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece merges feature tokens contextually; ACERec merges long OPQ codes into latent tokens with attention.; where: ACERec v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p2; Tables 1-2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T2.
- id: etegrec; relation: competitor; note: ETEGRec learns the tokenizer end to end; ACERec keeps fixed OPQ codes and compresses them.; where: ACERec v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p2; Tables 1-2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S3.T2.
- id: vq-rec; relation: predecessor; note: ACERec follows VQ-Rec and RPG in using OPQ-based semantic IDs and their evaluation protocol.; where: ACERec v2, Section 4.1 protocol follows Hou et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S4.SS1.p1; related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.13573v2#S2.p1.

## ActionPiece

- Page: pages/papers/actionpiece.md
- Venue: ICML’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: OPQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Ensemble
- TL;DR: ActionPiece represents each action as a set of item features and merges co-occurring feature patterns into new tokens, so identical actions get context-dependent tokens instead of fixed independent ones.
- [Code](https://github.com/google-deepmind/action_piece)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews: Sports and Outdoors, Beauty, and CDs and Vinyl. Users with fewer than 5 reviews are filtered; an item-frequency filter is not reported. Processed sizes (users / items / actions): Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 260,739; Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 176,139; CDs 75,258 / 64,443 / 1,022,334.
  - Source: Dataset categories: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p1; user filter and truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A6.p2; processed sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T3.
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-last-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, earlier items for training. Histories are truncated to 20 items for generative methods and 50 items for ID-based and feature-enhanced baselines.
  - Source: Leave-last-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p1; history truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A6.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists are produced by beam search.
  - Source: Evaluation settings name metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p3; top-K lists come from beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p4.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard leave-last-out protocol with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Each item is an unordered set of 4 OPQ codes x 256 codewords (sentence-t5-base text embeddings) plus 1 extra identification code to prevent conflicts. ActionPiece then merges co-occurring feature sets into a context-dependent vocabulary of 40,000 tokens (tuned over 5k-40k), so the same item can map to different tokens in different sequences.
  - Source: OPQ features, 256 codewords per digit, extra identification code: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A6.I1.i3.p1; vocabulary size 40,000 and tuning range: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A7.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 50; inference-time ensemble over q=5 set-permutation segmentations, with item scores averaged across the 5 ranking lists. Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Inference hardware, inference batch size, and measured latency: not reported (each model is trained on one 40GB NVIDIA A100; the paper states only that latency stays comparable when segments run in parallel).
  - Source: Beam size 50 and q=5 segmentations: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A7.T7; score averaging: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.SS3.SSS2.p1; GPU statement is for training: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p3; qualitative latency statement: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.SS4.p3.
- **Results from**: Table 4 (main comparison on Sports, Beauty, and CDs; averages over five seeds); Table 5 (ablations, including TIGER with varied vocabulary sizes); Figures 4-6 (vocabulary size, token utilization, and ensemble size). BERT4Rec, SASRec, FDSA, S3-Rec, TIGER, and LMIndexer numbers on Sports and Beauty are copied from earlier papers; other results are the authors' reimplementations.
  - Source: Main table: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS2.p1; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.T5; five seeds: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p3; copied baseline numbers: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER tokenizes each item independently into ordered RQ-VAE codes, whereas ActionPiece merges unordered feature sets into context-dependent tokens; both use the same encoder-decoder and beam search.; where: ActionPiece v3, Section 4.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p2; Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T4; same architecture statement: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A8.p2.
- id: vq-rec; relation: predecessor; note: ActionPiece follows VQ-Rec in quantizing sentence embeddings with OPQ into unordered codes, then builds a merged contextual vocabulary over those codes for generation.; where: ActionPiece v3, Appendix F follows Hou et al. (2023) for OPQ features: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#A6.I1.i3.p1; VQ-Rec is a Table 4 baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T4.
- id: lmindexer; relation: competitor; note: LMIndexer learns text-based semantic indexes item by item, while ActionPiece tokenizes whole action sequences with context-aware merges.; where: ActionPiece v3, Table 1 and Section 4.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S1.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p2; Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T4.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID builds item IDs by hierarchical clustering, independent of sequence context; ActionPiece's tokens depend on neighboring actions.; where: ActionPiece v3, Table 1 and Section 4.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S1.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S4.SS1.p2; Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.13581v3#S3.T4.

### Notes

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Existing generative recommendation (GR) models tokenize each action on its own, so an action gets the same tokens in every sequence (Abstract). The authors argue that the same action can mean different things in different contexts (Abstract). ActionPiece lets the surrounding actions decide how an action is tokenized.

> "However, existing GR models tokenize each action independently, assigning the same fixed tokens to identical actions across all sequences without considering contextual relationships." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Action sequences of feature sets") --> B["Count token pairs in a set and across adjacent sets"]
    B --> C["Weighted merges"]:::key
    C --> D("Context-dependent vocabulary")
    D --> E["Set permutation regularization"]
    E --> F("Several segmentations")
    F --> G["Enc-Dec generator"]
    G --> H("Ensembled ranking")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Actions as Feature Sets

Each action is an unordered set of item features, so a user history is a sequence of feature sets (Abstract).

#### Vocabulary Construction

Merges are counted both within individual sets and across adjacent sets (Abstract). The two kinds of token pairs receive different weights (Sec. 1).

> "Considering the structural differences between token pairs, e.g., whether they occur within a single set or between two adjacent sets, we assign different weights to different pairs." (Sec. 1)

#### Set Permutation Regularization

Because feature sets are unordered, set permutation regularization produces multiple segmentations of the same action sequence with the same semantics (Abstract). These segmentations augment the training data and are ensembled at inference (Sec. 3.2.2).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Vocabulary size: a larger vocabulary improves recommendation performance and reduces the normalized sequence length (NSL) (Sec. 4.4.1, Fig. 4). The authors describe vocabulary size as a trade-off between performance, sequence length, and memory efficiency (Sec. 4.4.1).
- Ablation: the gain does not come from vocabulary size alone (Sec. 4.3, Table 5).

  > "These results suggest that the performance improvement of ActionPiece is not simply due to scaling the vocabulary size up or down." (Sec. 4.3)

- Token usage: deriving different tokens for the same item from its neighbors improves token usage and acts as data augmentation (Sec. 4.3).
- Other analyses: the paper studies token usage (Sec. 4.4.2), the ensemble size (Fig. 6), and case examples (Sec. 4.5).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- Inference ranks several segmentations and averages the scores. This suggests that decoding cost grows with the ensemble size unless the segmentations run in parallel.
- VQ-Rec uses `OPQ` codes in an `Encoder` with `Scoring`; ActionPiece starts from the same kind of codes but generates merged tokens with an `Enc-Dec` generator.

## AdaSID

- Page: pages/papers/adasid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: AdaSID regulates Semantic ID overlaps during tokenizer training by relaxing repulsion for semantically compatible items and scaling the rest by local collision load, instead of fixed overlap regularization.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Offline: Amazon 2018 Reviews, Beauty and Toys and Games, with 5-core filtering of users and items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Toys 19,412 / 11,924 / 905,253; Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 1,048,296. Industrial: Kuaishou e-commerce short-video items with multimodal features (images, text, keyframes, audio transcripts); filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Amazon 2018 categories, 5-core filtering, leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T1; industrial setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Split**: Offline: leave-one-out into training, validation, and test; the exact validation/test position allocation is not reported beyond the leave-one-out label. Industrial: 4-day online A/B test on the retrieval model and a 4-day offline study on the ranking model.
  - Source: Leave-one-out named without position allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial test periods: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates).
  - Source: Metrics and backbone only: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: Offline: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Industrial ranking reports a cold-start CVR subset; generator/tokenizer visibility for those items is not reported.
  - Source: Offline protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial cold-start CVR subset without a visibility definition: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.I2.i2.p1.
- **SID**: 3 residual-quantization levels x 256 codes, 32-dimensional code embeddings, 768-dimensional input features. Collisions are reduced during tokenizer training by an adaptive overlap-repulsion loss; a post-hoc disambiguation suffix or other collision-resolution rule is not reported.
  - Source: SID length 3, 256 codes, 32-dimensional code embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1; collision handled by a training-time adaptive overlap loss, with no added suffix described: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S4.SS4.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Downstream generation uses the same TIGER configuration for all tokenizers; beam width, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. Recall and NDCG at K=3 and 5.
  - Source: Downstream TIGER configuration only: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1; no extra online cost claim: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S4.SS4.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (tokenizer comparison on Toys and Beauty under a shared TIGER backbone); Table 3 (Kuaishou online retrieval A/B and offline ranking AUC); Table 4 (ablations); Figure 3 (codebook statistics); Figure 4 (hyperparameter sensitivity on Beauty).
  - Source: Main offline table: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T2; industrial table: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T4; codebook statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.F3.

### Related

- id: quasid; relation: predecessor; note: QuaSID applies a fixed qualification-aware collision regularizer; AdaSID instantiates its collision term following QuaSID and makes the repulsion adaptive to semantic compatibility, local load, and training progress.; where: AdaSID v1, Section 4.1 follows Hu et al. (2026) for the collision term: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S4.SS1.p2; QuaSID is the collision-aware baseline in Section 5.1.3 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.T2.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER is the shared downstream generative backbone; AdaSID changes only how the SIDs are learned.; where: AdaSID v1, Section 5.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1; Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- id: hid-vae; relation: alternative; note: HiD-VAE suppresses SID overlaps with an explicit objective under a fixed standard, while AdaSID relaxes or strengthens repulsion adaptively.; where: AdaSID v1, Section 1 and Section 2.2 cite Fang et al. (2025) among static overlap-aware objectives: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S2.SS2.p1; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: etegrec; relation: alternative; note: ETEGRec aligns the tokenizer with downstream recommendation through end-to-end supervision, whereas AdaSID keeps a pre-trained tokenizer and regulates code overlaps adaptively.; where: AdaSID v1, Section 2.2 cites Liu et al. (2025) for end-to-end downstream supervision: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23522v1#S2.SS2.p1; not a baseline in Table 2.

## ADC-SID

- Page: pages/papers/adc-sid.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: MoE-VQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: ADC-SID adds collaborative information to Semantic ID quantization with alignment strength that adapts to collaborative noise and learned weights for behavioral IDs, instead of uniform alignment and equal weights.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial: Southeast Asian e-commerce advertising platform, October 2024 to May 2025, about 30 million users and 40 million ads (Table 1: 35,154,135 users, 48,106,880 items), average sequence length 128; filtering rules not reported. Public: Amazon Product Reviews Beauty (May 1996-September 2014); generative retrieval uses 5-core filtering of users and items, 22,363 users and 12,101 items; ranking uses the rating data with ratings above 3 as positives.
  - Source: Industrial data: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2; Beauty filtering and sequence construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3; sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T1.
- **Split**: Beauty generative retrieval: chronological sequences capped at 20 items; the train/validation/test allocation is not reported. Beauty ranking: chronological 90%/10% train/test split. Industrial offline split: not reported. Online: 5-day A/B test with 10% random user traffic.
  - Source: Beauty ranking split and retrieval sequence construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S5.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); retrieval uses Recall and NDCG at N=50 and 100.
  - Source: Retrieval metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The long-tail analysis stratifies items by 30-day impression counts (top 25% versus bottom 25%).
  - Source: No cold-start protocol; the popularity analysis groups items by 30-day impressions: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS5.p1.
- **SID**: Industrial: SID length 10 with codebook size printed as "3,00" (shared 2, text 2, visual 2, behavioral 4 codes for ADC-SID). Public: SID length 6 with codebook size 100 (shared 1, text 1, visual 1, behavioral 3). The online system uses an 8-token SID. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Codebook settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p3; online SID length: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S5.p1; no collision rule found in Sections 3-5.
- **Inference budget**: Generative retrieval uses the REG4REC encoder-decoder; ranking uses PPNet. Beam width, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Downstream backbones only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (generative retrieval and discriminative ranking on industrial data and Beauty, with quantization metrics); Table 3 (industrial ablation); Table 4 and Figure 5 (hyperparameters); Figure 6 (popular versus long-tail AUC); Table 5 (5-day online A/B test).
  - Source: Main table: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T3; hyperparameters: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T4; popularity: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.F6; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S5.T5.

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: The OPQ baseline is attributed to RPG's unordered content codes; ADC-SID builds hierarchical behavior-content codes instead.; where: ADC-SID v3, Section 4.1.2 describes the OPQ baseline as RPG: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.I3.i2.p1; Table 2 row OPQ: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: The behavioral weights are computed from the magnitude of a pre-trained collaborative embedding, so they depend on the quality of that embedding (Sec. 3.4.1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Semantic IDs (SIDs) quantize item content features so that items can share knowledge, and existing methods add collaborative information to them (Abstract). User-item interactions are highly skewed, so collaborative information is much weaker for long-tail items (Abstract). The authors identify two effects: indiscriminate alignment lets this noise corrupt the content representations of tail items, and equal weights hide which behavioral SIDs are informative (Abstract).

> "unlike relatively uniform content features, user-item interactions are highly skewed, resulting in a significant quality gap in collaborative information between popular and long-tail items." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Content features") --> M["Shared and specific experts"]
    B("Behavior features") --> M
    M --> C["Alignment strength controller"]:::key
    M --> D["Gate on L2 magnitude of CF embedding"]:::key
    C --> L1{{"Adaptive alignment loss"}}
    D --> W("Weighted behavioral SIDs")
    W --> E("SIDs")
    E --> G["Generator"]
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Behavior-Content Mixture-of-Quantization

Shared experts learn information common to behavior and content, and specific experts learn modality-specific information (Sec. 3.2).

#### Adaptive Behavior-Content Alignment

An alignment strength controller sets how strongly behavior and content are aligned for head and long-tail items (Sec. 3.3.1).

> "To adaptively align behavior and content information for head and long-tail items, the alignment strength controller is proposed to calculate the alignment strength." (Sec. 3.3.1)

#### Dynamic Behavioral Weighting

A gate learns an importance score for each behavioral SID from the L2 magnitude of the pre-trained collaborative embedding (Sec. 3.4.1, Eq. 22). A ReLU-based router with load balancing reduces training imbalance among the behavioral experts (Sec. 3.4.2, Eq. 23).

> "This gate suppresses noisy behavioral SIDs, improving the robustness of behavioral SIDs when incorporated with downstream recommendations." (Sec. 3.4.1)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Baseline families: behavior-content aligned SIDs such as RQ-Kmeans and LETTER outperform content-only SIDs such as RQ-VAE and OPQ on R@100, N@100, and AUC (Sec. 4.2, Table 2).
- Tasks: the SIDs are evaluated in both generative and discriminative tasks (Abstract).
- Behavioral weighting: the ablation compares learned weights with equal weights (Sec. 4.3.2).
- Popularity groups: with items split into popular (top 25%) and long-tail (bottom 25%) groups by impressions over the last 30 days, ADC-SID gains most on tail items (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 6).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- MME-SID uses the same three inputs with `MM-RQ` codes and a `Dec-Only` generator scored by `Scoring`; ADC-SID uses `MoE-VQ` codes with an `Enc-Dec` generator.

## Align3GR

- Page: pages/papers/align3gr.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Dual RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: Align3GR aligns an LLM recommender at three levels, with dual semantic and collaborative tokenization, bidirectional semantic alignment in behavior modeling, and progressive DPO from self-play and real-world feedback.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Instruments, Amazon Beauty, and Yelp; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered. Retained corpus sizes: not reported in the body. Industrial: internal data from a large-scale advertising recommendation platform; filtering not reported.
  - Source: Datasets, 5-interaction filter, leave-one-out, history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p1; industrial platform: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx3.p1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out into training, validation, and test; histories capped at the 20 most recent items. The exact position allocation is not reported beyond the leave-one-out label. Online: 10% of traffic (about 40+ million users) over multiple weeks.
  - Source: Leave-one-out and 20-item cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3; online traffic: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); industrial retrieval reports Recall@100.
  - Source: Metrics and beam width only: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard leave-one-out with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p1.
- **SID**: Item SCID: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over concatenated semantic (T5) and collaborative (DIN) embeddings; users receive their own SCIDs from a separate user RQ-VAE. Both are added to the LLM vocabulary. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codes of dimension 32, user and item SCIDs added to the vocabulary: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4; dual user/item tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.SSx2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.SSx2.p4.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam width 20 for generative methods (following EAGER-LLM); Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. All experiments use 4 NVIDIA GPUs (model not stated); inference batch size and latency: not reported. Backbone: Llama2-7B with LoRA.
  - Source: Beam width 20 following EAGER-LLM: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3; 4 GPUs for all experiments: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Instruments, Beauty, Yelp; averages over five seeds); Table 2 (industrial Recall@100 and online revenue versus a two-tower baseline and TIGER); Tables 3-5 and Figure 4 (tokenization, SFT-task, and DPO ablations).
  - Source: Main table: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.T1; industrial: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.T5; five seeds: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4.

### Related

- id: eager-llm; relation: competitor; note: EAGER-LLM aligns item tokens with collaborative signals; Align3GR also tokenizes users and adds progressive self-play and real-feedback DPO.; where: Align3GR v2, Experimental Settings baselines (13) and beam-width protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec aligns LLMs to item codes with auxiliary tasks; Align3GR adds dual user-item SCIDs and preference-level DPO on top of multi-task SFT.; where: Align3GR v2, baselines (11): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.T1.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER learns a regularized item tokenizer; Align3GR fuses semantic and collaborative features for both users and items through a U2I loss.; where: Align3GR v2, baselines (12): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.T1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER uses content-only RQ-VAE item codes with a small Transformer; Align3GR uses an LLM backbone with dual SCIDs and DPO.; where: Align3GR v2, baselines (10): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx3.T1; industrial Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.11255v2#Sx4.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On the public dataset, Align3GR reports +17.8% in Recall@10 and +20.2% in NDCG@10 over the strongest baseline (Abstract).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Turning a large language model (LLM) into a recommender meets semantic and behavioral misalignment (Abstract). Earlier LLM recommenders such as LC-Rec align item tokens through supervised tasks. Align3GR treats alignment as one problem across token, behavior modeling, and preference levels.

> "To bridge this gap, we propose Align3GR, a novel framework that unifies token-level, behavior modeling-level, and preference-level alignment." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Users and items") --> B["Dual SC encoders + RQ-VAE"]
    B --> C("User and item SCIDs")
    C --> D["Multi-task SFT"]
    D --> E["SP-DPO: Easy, Medium, Hard"]:::key
    E --> F["RF-DPO on real feedback"]:::key
    F --> G("Aligned LLM")
    L1{{"Four SFT tasks"}} -.-> D
    L2{{"Prefix n-gram curriculum"}} -.-> E
    L3{{"disliked / neutral / liked"}} -.-> F
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Token-Level Alignment

Dual semantic-collaborative (SC) encoders and RQ-VAEs build SCIDs for both users and items (Fig. 2 caption). The LLM vocabulary is expanded with these tokens.

> "Following previous work (Zheng et al. 2024), we first expand the LLM vocabulary to include the SCID tokens of the user and the item, thus avoiding out-of-vocabulary issues and ensuring smooth integration with autoregressive generation tasks." (Behavior Modeling-level Alignment)

#### Behavior Modeling-Level Alignment

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) follows LC-Rec with four tasks: sequential item prediction, asymmetric item prediction, item prediction based on user intention, and personalized preference inference (Multi-task SFT). The user's SCID token appears in every task prompt, and one task reconstructs the user profile text from the user SCID (Multi-task SFT).

#### Preference-Level Alignment

Self-play DPO (SP-DPO) runs in Easy, Medium, and Hard stages defined by prefix n-gram match over the hierarchical SCID (Preference-level Alignment). Real-feedback DPO (RF-DPO) then uses feedback labeled disliked, neutral, or liked (Preference-level Alignment).

> "Specifically, considering the hierarchical nature of SCID, we divide progressive SP-DPO learning into three stages: Easy, Medium, and Hard, using a prefix-ngram match metric (Zheng et al. 2025)" (Preference-level Alignment)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Industrial deployment: the authors report gains in online A/B tests and full-scale deployment on an industrial recommendation platform (Abstract).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The pipeline trains SCID tokenizers, multi-task SFT, and two DPO phases in sequence. This suggests that a catalog change requires repeating several stages.
- EAGER-LLM also feeds semantic and collaborative signals to a `Dec-Only` LLM, but with `Dual H-KM` codes; Align3GR uses `Dual RQ` codes and adds DPO.

## APAO

- Page: pages/papers/apao.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec / Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: APAO adds prefix-level losses and an adaptive worst-prefix strategy to training, so correct items survive beam-search pruning, closing the gap between token-level cross-entropy training and beam-search inference.
- [Code](https://github.com/yuyq18/APAO)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Office (4,905 users / 2,420 items), Grocery (14,681 / 8,713), Beauty (22,363 / 12,101), and Yelp (30,431 / 20,033), with 5-core filtering of users and items; histories truncated to the 20 most recent items.
  - Source: Datasets, 5-core, leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.T2.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (following LETTER and LC-Rec; allocation not restated beyond the label).
  - Source: Leave-one-out named: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K from beam search with Recall and NDCG at 10 and 20. Training losses use 100 uniformly sampled negatives; exclusion of history items for these negatives: not reported.
  - Source: Metrics; training negatives fixed at 100 uniform: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS3.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-K-means codes over Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct item embeddings; codebook size and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: 4-level RQ-K-means over Llama-3.1-8B embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; codebook size and collision rule not found.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 20 (scalability over K in Figure 6); TIGER encoder-decoder and Llama decoder backbones of about 0.01B parameters, trained on one NVIDIA A100-40GB. Inference batch size and latency: not reported (Table 4 reports training efficiency).
  - Source: Beam size 20 and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; beam scalability: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.F6; training efficiency: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.T4.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (four datasets, TIGER and Llama backbones, versus CE, MSL, DPO, DMPO, S-DPO losses); Table 3 (one-stage versus two-stage training); Table 4 (training efficiency); Figures 2-6 (ablations, prefix-level analysis, hyperparameters, beam size).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.T1; paradigms: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.T3; efficiency: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.02730v4#S5.T4.

## API

- Page: pages/papers/api.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: PID (P-SAE); Backbone: Enc-Dec / Dec-Only (AR); Non-AR (PR); Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank + Aux. / MTP + Rank + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam / Scoring
- TL;DR: API reuses feature indices of a pretrained sparse autoencoder as an interpretable Semantic ID vocabulary and trains an adapter to predict indices and strengths, instead of fitting a new vocabulary.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/API-C1F9/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports, and Toys as preprocessed in prior work (P5, GRID), keeping their splits; item text from title, brand, category, and price. Sizes: Appendix A (not restated here).
  - Source: Benchmark aligned with P5 and GRID: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p1.
- **Split**: The prior-work (P5 / GRID) splits and evaluation protocol are retained (allocation not restated); checkpoints selected by validation Recall@5.
  - Source: Inherited splits; PID statistics from training items only: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (complete test split, full catalog without sampled negatives).
  - Source: Full catalog without sampled negatives: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p4.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. PID selection statistics and activation calibration are estimated from training-item contents.
  - Source: PID statistics estimated from training-item contents; no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Pretrained Interpretable IDs: K in {4, 8, 16} feature indices selected by a priority rule from the 32 strongest of 24,576 labeled sparse-autoencoder features of a frozen GPT-2-small, plus their relative activation strengths, which separate items whose index sequences coincide. Collision-affected items at K=4: 15.16% on Beauty (77.37% with native SAE selection).
  - Source: PID from frozen GPT-2 SAE features with K tokens and activation strengths: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S4.SS1.p3; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.T3.
- **Inference budget**: Two decoders: parallel prediction (PR) with exact catalog scoring, and autoregressive (AR) with catalog-constrained beam search of width 50; T5- and GPT-2-style backbones trained from scratch. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Decoding settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.SS1.p4.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (full API versus sequential and generative recommenders); Table 2 (tokenizers under T5 and GPT-2 backbones with AR and PR decoding); Table 3 (collision rates by token budget); Table 4 (content alignment); Table 5 (preference and strength ablation); Figure 3 (cross-domain vocabulary reuse).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S4.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.36763v1#S5.F3.

## AtSpeed

- Page: pages/papers/atspeed.md
- Venue: ICLR’25
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Spec. Dec.
- TL;DR: AtSpeed aligns a draft model with the target LLM on top-K sequences and relaxes speculative-decoding verification, to speed up beam-search generation of top-K items in LLM-based generative recommendation.
- [Code](https://github.com/Linxyhaha/AtSpeed)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty and Games (main), plus MovieLens-1M and Goodreads in Appendix Table 6. Filtering rules: not restated; statistics in Appendix Table 2.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S4.SS1.p1; split and identifier length: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- **Split**: All interactions sorted by global timestamp and split 8:1:1 into training, validation, and test.
  - Source: Global-timestamp 8:1:1 split: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); top-K (K = 1, 3, 5, 10, 20) from beam search of the target LLM, evaluated by Recall and NDCG plus walltime speedup.
  - Source: Metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined (global temporal split, so test items may include items not seen in training, but this is not analyzed).
  - Source: Global temporal split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: RQ-VAE item identifiers following LC-Rec, length L=4; codebook size and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: RQ-VAE identifiers following LC-Rec, length 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Speculative beam decoding: LLaMA-68M draft model with draft length 4 and draft beam size N=40 verifying top-K beams (K up to 20) of a LLaMA-7B LC-Rec target with tree-based attention. Figure 1 measures LC-Rec inference time on one NVIDIA A5000; draft training on 4 A5000 GPUs; speedup reported as walltime ratio (WS@K).
  - Source: Draft settings and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S4.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.SS3.SSS1.p2; target inference cost figure: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S1.F1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (walltime speedup and accepted steps versus SFT, WordKD, SeqKD, TVDKD, DARE drafts); Appendix Table 5 (Recall and NDCG on Beauty and Games for the target LLM, the baselines, and AtSpeed instantiated on LC-Rec with LLaMA-7B); Appendix Tables 6-7 (MovieLens-1M, Goodreads, alignment-data cost).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#S4.T1; ranking results: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.T5; appendix datasets and cost: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05165v3#A1.T7.

## AWARE

- Page: pages/papers/aware.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: Geo-Prefix+HClus; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: AWARE adds agent-generated narratives about local events, culture, and seasonal trends, grounded in each user's behavior, to LLM-based next-POI generation, whose knowledge otherwise stays fixed after training.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare-NYC, Foursquare-TKY and Gowalla-CA; filter users/POIs with fewer than 10 check-ins; segment chronological trajectories at a 24-hour gap; reverse-geocode street addresses.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A1.p1
- **Split**: Temporal 80/10/10 train/validation/test; per-user versus global allocation: not reported. History budget 150 entries, reserving 40% for matching day-of-week and filling the remainder with recent entries.
  - Source: Appendix A and E: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A5.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; full-catalog versus sampled evaluation and history-POI exclusion are unspecified.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 reports prediction metrics without catalog/negative-sampling details: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; main protocol: all validation/test users and POIs are observed during training. Cross-city transfer trains on NYC and evaluates TKY/CA without adaptation; pretrained-generator/tokenizer exposure to target-city POIs: not reported. Hard cases only exclude the target from the user's last five visits, not from training.
  - Source: Appendix A guarantees seen users/POIs; Sec.4.6 defines cross-city transfer: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS4.p1
- **SID**: ROS Spatial SIDs: hierarchical clustering of Qwen3-0.6B POI text embeddings plus multi-resolution S2-cell geospatial prefixes. Numerical SID length, branching/codebook sizes, S2 levels and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.3.3, Sec.4.1 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S3.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px12.p1
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive SID prediction; HR@1 and HR/NDCG@5/10/20. Beam width, inference hardware/batch, generated-length cap and numerical latency: not reported. Qwen3-max knowledge acquisition is offline, capped at two retrieval rounds and 80/150-word narratives; no agent calls during serving. Eight MI308X GPUs are the training setup.
  - Source: Sec.3.3/4.1, Appendix E and Limitations: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S3.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#Sx1.p1
- **Results from**: Paper's Table1 main comparisons, Tables2-3 NYC ablations/hard cases, Table4 top-K and Figure5 cross-city transfer; scores average three inference runs, not three stated training seeds. ROS pretrained backbone is the controlled baseline. Other baselines' quoted-versus-rerun provenance: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.2, Sec.4.1 metrics and Tables1-4/Figure5: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.F5.g1

### Related

- id: ros; relation: predecessor; note: AWARE reuses ROS's SID-equipped pretrained backbone as the controlled baseline.; where: AWARE v1, Sec.4.2 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px12.p1.
- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID is a compared generative POI baseline.; where: AWARE v1, Sec.4.1 and Table1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.SS1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.T1.
- id: spacetime-gr; relation: competitor; note: SpaceTime-GR is a compared spatial-temporal generative baseline.; where: AWARE v1, Appendix D and Table1: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11807v1#S4.T1.

## CAPE

- Page: pages/papers/cape.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE†; Backbone: Dec-Only / Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP† / NTP†; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: CAPE is a training-free plug-in that retrieves co-occurrence-supported tail items outside the beam and fuses co-occurrence evidence into ranking, restoring item-level memorization that shared-prefix generation lacks.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Industrial & Scientific, Office Products and Beauty (5-core), plus LastFM-1K (987 users, 40429 tracks). LastFM filtering thresholds: not reported. Histories contain the latest ten items.
  - Source: Sec.5.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p1
- **Split**: I&S/Office: chronological 80/10/10; per-user versus global allocation not reported. LastFM/Beauty: last user interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: Sec.5.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p1
- **Candidates**: Reported ranking pool: 75 retrieved items, comprising 50 beam outputs plus the 25 highest-co-occurrence tail items outside the beam; not a sampled-negative pool. Full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation label and history-item exclusion: not reported. Tail metrics count all tail test cases, including unretrieved targets.
  - Source: Sec.4.1, Sec.2.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tail is the bottom 80% by training frequency. Frequency, tail partition and user/event co-occurrence matrices use training data only; tokenizer exposure to test items: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.2.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p1
- **SID**: Inherited frozen backbone identifiers: three tokens/item, with a fourth collision-resolution token for a small number of LastFM items. TIGER uses residual-quantized identifiers. Numerical codebook sizes and MiniOneRec tokenizer construction: not reported. CAPE leaves tokenization unchanged.
  - Source: Sec.5.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Beam50 +25 co-occurrence tail candidates, one batched teacher-forcing pass, calibrated ranking with fixed top1; HR/NDCG@5/10. Validation-selected lambda=0.5 on I&S/Office and 5 on LastFM. FP32 on one A40; full-request means over first128 test users: 1.20s I&S, 1.22s Office, 1.55s LastFM-MiniOneRec, 0.19s LastFM-TIGER. Timing includes input preparation, beam, retrieval, teacher forcing, evidence and ranking after two-user warm-up; one-time loading takes 5-16s separately. Request batch size: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1/4.3, Sec.5.1, Table4 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S4.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p4
- **Results from**: Paper's frozen-checkpoint inference comparisons/ablations. Released Amazon MiniOneRec checkpoints; LastFM continues SFT from that checkpoint; TIGER is trained from scratch with seeds42/43/44. Table2 main comparisons; Table3 Amazon TIGER evaluated after CAPE was frozen. Re-rankers share the 75-item pool/top1 and validation rule; 10000 user-bootstrap replicates quantify paired differences. No borrowed baseline scores are identified.
  - Source: Sec.5.1, Tables2/3 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p4

### Related

- id: minionerec; relation: predecessor; note: MiniOneRec supplies a frozen backbone and released Amazon checkpoints.; where: CAPE v1, Sec.5.1 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#A2.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER supplies the second backbone for cross-architecture evaluation.; where: CAPE v1, Sec.5.1 and Table3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.SS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S5.T3.
- id: liger; relation: alternative; note: LIGER is contrasted as a trained hybrid retrieval approach.; where: CAPE v1, Sec.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29298v1#S6.p1.

## CapsID

- Page: pages/papers/capsid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Soft-RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: CapsID replaces hard residual quantization with capsule routing, which soft-routes each item across capsules and ends its Semantic ID once confidence is high, so ID length varies per item.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports, and Toys with 5-core filtering (users / items: 22,363 / 12,101; 35,598 / 18,357; 19,412 / 11,924). Industrial: a proprietary 35M-item catalog from a large social media platform with text, image, and behavior embeddings (331.1M interactions); filtering not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T2; preprocessing statement: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A2.SS5.p1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out with 5-core filtering on the Amazon datasets; the exact validation/test position allocation is not restated. Histories are truncated to the most recent 50 interactions. Industrial split: not reported.
  - Source: Leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T2; history truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full-corpus ranking); decoding is constrained by a trie over item SIDs. Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10 on Amazon, K=50 and 100 on the 35M-item catalog.
  - Source: Full-corpus ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1; trie restricted to training-item SIDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Appendix B.2 isolates Beauty cold items, defined as items with fewer than 5 interactions in the training split (about 12% of items); these are low-frequency, not strictly unseen, and tokenizer exposure is not separately reported. The industrial cold-start tier is not defined.
  - Source: Cold subset definition: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A2.SS2.p1; industrial cold-start tier without definition: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2.
- **SID**: Variable-length SIDs: K=256 capsules per depth, up to L_max=6 levels, stopping on confidence (tau=0.82) or residual norm (epsilon=0.08); SemanticBPE then merges frequent code pairs (industrial: K=1024, mean length 3.3 after merging). Collision rates are reported: 13.4% on Beauty for CapsID and 19.4% for CapsID+SemanticBPE on the industrial catalog; a resolution rule for items sharing a SID is not reported.
  - Source: Capsule configuration: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; industrial K=1024: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1; measured collision rates: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam size 50 with trie-based invalid-ID filtering and an end-of-item token. The industrial run uses 4 x A100-80GB; public benchmarks run on a single commodity GPU. CapsID+SemanticBPE runs at 51% of COBRA's per-query latency on the same ANN infrastructure; Table 4 reports cost normalized to TIGER beam search (B=50). Inference batch size and absolute latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam 50, trie, end-of-item token: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A2.SS5.p1; latency versus COBRA: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2; normalized cost: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T4.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Beauty, Sports, Toys; mean over three seeds); Table 4 (patching versus tokenizer-centric design, with normalized cost); Table 5 (ablations); Table 6 (35M-item industrial catalog, single run); Figure 3 (collision, purity, predictability); Table 10 (Beauty cold-item subset).
  - Source: Main table: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3; patching comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T4; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T5; industrial: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T6; cold subset: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A2.SS2.p1.

### Related

- id: cobra; relation: competitor; note: COBRA patches incomplete sparse IDs with a dense vector and BeamFusion at inference; CapsID instead makes the SID itself soft-routed and variable-length, without a dense path.; where: CapsID v1, Section 4.1 baselines and fairness controls: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1; Tables 3, 4, and 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T6.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER uses fixed-length hard RQ-VAE codes; CapsID routes residuals softly across capsules and stops at an item-specific length.; where: CapsID v1, Section 4.1 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Tables 3 and 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T6.
- id: adc-sid; relation: competitor; note: CapsID labels this baseline ADA-SID and cites arXiv:2510.25622; it adapts behavior-content quantization with fixed-length codes, whereas CapsID varies code length per item.; where: CapsID v1, Table 1 and Section 2 cite it as ADA-SID [34] (arXiv:2510.25622): https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S2.T1; Section 4.1 baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3.
- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece merges feature tokens by co-occurrence frequency; CapsID's SemanticBPE uses a differentiable merge gate over learned capsule codes.; where: CapsID v1, Section 2 capsule-routing and subword paragraph: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1; Section 4.1 baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3.
- id: resid; relation: competitor; note: ReSID uses adaptive semantic quantization with residual knowledge transfer; CapsID uses capsule routing with confidence-driven stopping.; where: CapsID v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1; Section 4.1 baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3; cold-start protocol follows ReSID: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#A2.SS2.p1.

## CARD

- Page: pages/papers/card.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: NU-RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: CARD fuses text, image, and collaborative signals into a visual semantic unit before encoding and quantizes it with NU-RQ-VAE, whose learnable non-uniform transformation balances skewed embeddings.
- [Code](https://github.com/HAI-UESTC/CARD)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews: Grocery and Gourmet Food (Food), Cell Phones and Accessories (Phones), and Clothing, Shoes and Jewelry (Clothing), with 5-core filtering of users and items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Food 14,681 / 8,713 / 151,254; Phones 27,879 / 10,429 / 194,439; Clothing 39,387 / 23,033 / 278,677.
  - Source: Categories, 5-core filtering, truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T1.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: most recent interaction for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training; histories truncated or padded to the 20 most recent items.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation and history length: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard leave-one-out with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: 4 non-uniform RQ-VAE levels x 256 codewords (dimension 32), quantizing a vision-language embedding of a 512 x 512 rendered card (item image, title, collaborative-neighbor thumbnails). Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: K=4 codebooks x 256 vectors of dimension 32: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; non-uniform RQ-VAE over a vision-language encoding of a rendered item card: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p2; no collision rule found in Sections 3-4.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search over the code vocabulary; numerical beam width not reported. T5-style encoder-decoder with 4 layers each and 6 heads. Recall and NDCG at K=5, 10, and 20. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam search with top-B partial sequences, no numerical B: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S3.SS3.p2; backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Food, Phones, Clothing; paired t-tests against the best baseline); Tables 3-4 (ablations of the two CARD variants); Table 5 (non-uniform quantization with different quantizers); Table 6 (text-only encoding).
  - Source: Main table: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T4; plug-in quantizers: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T5; text-only variants: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T6.

## CausalDPO

- Page: pages/papers/causaldpo.md
- Venue: ICML’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: LLM-Vocab; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: CausalDPO extends DPO for LLM-based recommendation with backdoor adjustment, soft clustering of latent environments, and invariance constraints, to remove spurious correlations that DPO amplifies under distribution shift.
- [Code](https://github.com/user683/CausalDPO)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Yelp2018, MovieLens-10M, and Book-Crossing. Users with at least 40 interactions (Yelp2018) or 20 interactions (ML-10M, Book-Crossing) are kept; ratings above 4 (ML-10M, Yelp2018) or above 7 (Book-Crossing) are positives. Sizes (sequences / items / interactions): ML-10M 71,567 / 10,681 / 10,000,054; Yelp2018 31,668 / 38,048 / 1,561,406; Book-Crossing 278,858 / 271,379 / 1,149,780.
  - Source: Dataset list: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S3.SS6.p1; user thresholds and positive-rating rules: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T2.
- **Split**: Distribution-shift splits: popularity shift (Yelp2018) samples 20% of interactions as a popularity-balanced OOD test set; temporal shift (ML-10M) takes each user's latest 20% of interactions; exposure shift (Book-Crossing) takes the most recent 20% and imputes a fully exposed test set by matrix factorization; mixed shift (Yelp2018) samples 80% popularity-shift and 20% temporal-shift test interactions. The remainder is split 7:1:2 into training, validation, and IID test.
  - Source: Shift constructions: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.I2.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.I2.i2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.I2.i3.p1, and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.I2.i4.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (generated items are scored and ranked over the entire item space and mapped to dataset items).
  - Source: Scoring and ranking over the entire item space: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S3.SS6.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The distribution shifts concern popularity, time, and exposure of user-item interactions, not unseen items; tokenizer n/a.
  - Source: OOD shifts concern popularity, time, and exposure, not unseen items: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S3.SS6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.I2.i1.p1.
- **SID**: n/a (items are generated as text by the LLM and mapped to dataset items; no semantic IDs).
  - Source: Prompts generate items as text: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S3.SS6.p1; the item is represented through text in the prompt formulation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Llama-3.1-8B; decoding strategy and width: not reported. Experiments run on one node with 8 NVIDIA A800 80GB GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported. Table 6 reports training time per epoch (CausalDPO 2,971 s versus DPO 2,482 s). HR and NDCG at K=10 and 20.
  - Source: Hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.SS3.p1; training time per epoch: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T6.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (popularity, temporal, and exposure shifts on Yelp2018, ML-10M, Book-Crossing); Table 4 (mixed shift); Table 3 (IID test sets); Table 5 (causal regularizer added to other DPO variants); Table 8 (ablations); Table 9 (model sizes).
  - Source: OOD table: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S3.T1; IID: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T3; mixed shift: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T4; regularizer transfer: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T5; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T8; model sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#A2.T9.

### Related

(2025), OneRec, among DPO adoptions in recommendation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22335v2#S4.p2; not a baseline in Table 1.

## ChronoID

- Page: pages/papers/chronoid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Time; Tokenization: RQ-VAE / Par. VQ; Backbone: Dec-Only†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam†
- TL;DR: ChronoID is a framework and benchmark for time-aware Semantic ID learning that studies where and how explicit time signals enter the IDs, unlike existing time-agnostic Semantic ID learning.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Industrial and Office; Mercari. Item text plus interaction timestamps; interaction-count filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix B.1/Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.T1
- **Split**: Global temporal cutoff: codebook/SFT training before cutoff, test targets on/after cutoff; Appendix B uses 2018 for Amazon. Exact Mercari cutoff and validation allocation not reported. Section 4 inconsistently prints 2028 and 2018.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix B.3/B.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.T5
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 5.1 defines single-ground-truth ranking metrics but no candidate universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Visibility**: Unseen by tokenizer too for future items, as claimed in Appendix B.6; codebook fitting uses only pre-2018 interacted items and SFT training uses pre-cutoff targets. Test-item overlap/new-item fraction not reported. Users first appearing after cutoff can be test-only.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix B.2/B.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **SID**: Frozen text/time quantizer: residual early/late fusion or parallel quantization; default 3 codebooks x 256 entries, code dimension 42. Absolute/relative time encodings; text/time input dimensions 2560/768. Collision resolution not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.2/3.3 and Appendix B.3/D: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S3.SS2.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S3.SS2.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S3.SS3.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A4.T9
- **Inference budget**: HR/NDCG@3/5/10. Decoding algorithm, beam, constraints, inference hardware/batch and latency not reported; batch 1024 per GPU is SFT training.
  - Source: Table 1 and Appendix D/Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.T1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A4.T9
- **Results from**: Original Table 1 compares five baselines and six ChronoID designs on three datasets; Tables 2/6-8/10-11 give fusion, temporal/capacity and hyperparameter analyses. Baseline implementation/result provenance not reported.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.2 and Tables 1/2/6-8/10-11: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#S5.T1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A3.T6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.14260v1#A4.T11

## CID

- Page: pages/papers/cid.md
- Venue: SIGIR-AP’23
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: Spectral Clus.; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: CID studies item indexing for the P5 foundation model and proposes sequential, collaborative, semantic, and hybrid indexing, replacing random, title, and independent IDs that cause long outputs or hallucinated items.
- [Code](https://github.com/Wenyueh/LLM-RecSys-ID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Sports & Outdoors, Amazon Beauty, Yelp; paper states a Jan-Dec 2019 transaction window. Interaction-count filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S3.SS3.p1
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training. Test history includes the validation interaction.
  - Source: Section 3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S3.SS3.p2
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 3.3/5.1/5.2 do not define an evaluation candidate pool: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S3.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. CID co-occurrence edges/weights use training sequences only; graph nodes represent all items. Separate tokenizer/item holdouts not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.3/4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S3.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: CID only: recursive N-way spectral clustering until clusters contain at most k items; k shared OOV tokens encode cluster paths plus a unique-within-cluster leaf token. Variable-length fixed IDs; recommended mean length 3-4. Table 6 sweeps N=10/20 and k=200/500/1000; Table 4 default N/k not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/5.5 and Tables 6/7: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S4.SS2.SSS2.p4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS5.p4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T7
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained generation; HR/NDCG@5/10. Beam width, inference hardware/batch and latency not reported. Two RTX A5000 GPUs and batch 64 describe 20-epoch P5 training.
  - Source: Introduction, Implementation Details and Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S1.p5 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T4
- **Results from**: Original Table 4 CID row; Figures 4/5 and Tables 6/7 analyze CID clustering parameters and ID lengths. CID+IID is a separate hybrid variant, not CID. Baselines use the S3-Rec implementation; copied-versus-rerun provenance not stated.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.3/5.5/5.7 and Tables 4/6/7: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS5.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.SS7.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.06569v6#S5.T7

### Related

- id: lmindexer; relation: successor; note: LMIndexer cites this indexing study as earlier generative-recommendation work.; where: Evidence from LMIndexer v3, Section 2 and reference Hua et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2310.07815v3#S2.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2310.07815v3#bib.bib11.

## CITE

- Page: pages/papers/cite.md
- Venue: Electronics’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: CITE adds an item-level transition score with separate source and destination embeddings to a fixed parallel Semantic ID generator, modeling the directed relation between the latest item and each candidate.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Sports and Outdoors, Beauty, Toys and Games, CDs and Vinyl; RPG preprocessing, filtering threshold not reported. Additional Yelp 2019 review subset: iterative user/item 5-core, 30,431 users, 20,033 businesses, 316,354 interactions.
  - Source: Publisher version, 15 October 2026, DOI 10.3390/electronics15204749: §5.1 pp.8–9/Table 1; §5.11 pp.20–21. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **Split**: Per-user chronological: final item test, penultimate validation, earlier prefixes/next-item pairs training; histories capped at 50. Validation NDCG@10 selects CITE checkpoint and fusion weight; locked test evaluation. Yelp uses the same protocol.
  - Source: Publisher version: §§5.1–5.2 p.9; §5.4 p.10; §5.11 pp.20–21. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **Candidates**: full catalog; identical full-sort item set for RPG and CITE; graph search is not used for reported ranking metrics; history exclusion not reported.
  - Source: Publisher version: §3 pp.4–5; §4.6 pp.7–8/Algorithm 2; §5.4 p.10. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **Visibility**: Strict item-cold cohort has zero training-split occurrences (Sports/Beauty/Toys/CDs target counts 317/138/279/298); low-frequency means 1–5 occurrences. Tokenizer fitting exposure is not reported, so unseen by generator only versus unseen by tokenizer too is not established; CITE training scores every catalog destination.
  - Source: Publisher version: §5.9 pp.18–19/Tables 8–9; §4.6 p.7. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **SID**: Fixed OPQ identifiers over text embeddings; 256 codes/position, lengths Sports 16, Beauty 32, Toys 16, CDs 64; collision handling and Yelp ID length not reported. Yelp text uses text-embedding-3-large. Default CITE freezes the reproduced RPG generator and learns only the transition module.
  - Source: Publisher version: §3 p.4; §5.4 p.10/Table 2; §5.10 p.20; §5.11 p.20. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **Inference budget**: Parallel semantic scoring plus full-catalog transition matrix scoring, Recall/NDCG@5/10; no autoregressive beam or graph search in evaluation. Evaluation batch 512 (Sports/Beauty/Toys), 256 (CDs), NVIDIA A100 80GB/Intel Xeon Gold 5218. Inference latency not reported; Table 12 wall-clock includes loading, training, validation and testing.
  - Source: Publisher version: §5.4 p.10; §5.12 pp.21–22/Table 12. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
- **Results from**: Own matched RPG reproductions and CITE experiments: main comparison/ablations and Yelp use means and sample SD over seeds 2024–2028; cold-start, learned-gating and joint-fine-tuning analyses use seed 2024. Table 3 also includes published reference baseline scores. RPG checkpoints are trained from scratch and frozen before default CITE fitting; Yelp separately tunes RPG by validation.
  - Source: Publisher version: §5.4 p.10, §5.5 p.13/Table 3; §§5.8–5.11 pp.17–21/Tables 7–11; §6 p.22. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: predecessor; note: CITE adds transition scoring to a frozen reproduced RPG generator.; where: Publisher version, 15 October 2026, §1 p.2; §3 pp.4–5; §6 p.22. https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics15204749
