## CMRec

- Page: pages/papers/cmrec.md
- Venue: CIKM’26 Short
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only†; Tokenizer: –; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: CMRec learns a shared cross-country codebook and synthesizes mixed-country sequences by constrained token substitution, so knowledge transfers at the data level and not only through shared parameters.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial e-commerce advertising: >1 billion interactions, 19 million users, 25 million ads across 6 countries; largest country has about 10x the smallest's training interactions. Amazon M2/KDD Cup 2023: UK/DE/JP/IT/FR/ES; high-resource locales supply about 91% of training sessions. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Offline train/validation/test allocation and chronology not reported; all baselines use the same dataset partition. Online A/B: May 10–20, 2026, 10% live traffic across all 6 countries.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS2.p4
- **Candidates**: not reported; evaluation pool and history exclusion are unspecified. Sampled-softmax negatives train the i2i model, and cross-country neighbor filtering supports training augmentation; neither defines evaluation negatives.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS1.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS2.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Countries have disjoint users/items but are pooled for joint training; tokenizer/i2i exposure to test items is not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: Shared 4-token RQ-VAE identifiers: Qwen-VL-32B encodes multimodal content to 64 dimensions, with joint cross-country behavioral i2i alignment described before quantization. Codebook sizes and collision handling not reported; dynamic market attributes filter substitutions rather than form SID inputs.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS1.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive GenCDR backbone, Recall/NDCG@10/100; decoding algorithm/beam width, history cap, inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported. Mixing rates p=k=0.1 and neighbor thresholds are training augmentation settings.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S3.SS3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p2
- **Results from**: Own offline comparisons on shared partitions (Table 1), industrial ablations (Table 2), and two-backbone sensitivity experiments (Figure 3); no imported baseline scores stated; run counts/variance not reported. Own online six-country aggregate: advertising revenue +1.77%, orders +2.64%; online control model not identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.T1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28972v1#S4.SS2.p4

## COBRA

- Page: pages/papers/cobra.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: Casc. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Dense; Inference: BeamFusion
- TL;DR: COBRA generates a sparse Semantic ID and then a dense vector conditioned on it, trains both end to end, and decodes with BeamFusion, which combines beam search with nearest-neighbor scores.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-September 2014): Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, with 5-core filtering of users and items (users / items: 22,363 / 12,101; 35,598 / 18,357; 19,412 / 11,924). Industrial: Baidu advertising logs across list-page, dual-column, and short-video scenarios, about 5 million users and 2 million ads; filtering not reported.
  - Source: Public categories, date range, 5-core filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.T1; industrial data: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.
- **Split**: Public datasets: train/validation/test allocation not reported. Industrial: first 60 days of logs for training and the following day for testing. Online: A/B test in January 2025 with 10% of user traffic.
  - Source: Public split not stated: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial 60-day train and next-day test: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1; online A/B: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists are formed by ANN retrieval among items under the top-M generated sparse IDs, fused by BeamFusion. Public K=5 and 10; industrial K=50 to 800.
  - Source: Retrieval combines beam search over sparse IDs with ANN over items under each ID: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p5; evaluation metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard public protocol and next-day industrial test, with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Public: 3-level semantic IDs with codebook size 32 per level, generated from T5 embeddings following TIGER's method. Industrial: 2-level 32 x 32 sparse IDs (the w/o Dense variant uses 3 levels of 256). Items under the same sparse ID are distinguished by a generated dense vector and ANN search within that ID's candidate set; a collision-resolution rule for the sparse IDs is not reported.
  - Source: Public SID: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; industrial SID and the w/o Dense variant: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS2.SSS3.p1; items sharing a sparse ID are separated by the dense vector: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p5.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search returns the top M sparse IDs, then ANN retrieves the top N items per ID and BeamFusion combines beam and cosine scores; numerical M and N are not reported. The recall-diversity analysis selects tau=0.9 with the second coefficient fixed at 16. Public model: 1-layer encoder and 2-layer decoder. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam search top-M, ANN top-N, BeamFusion coefficients: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p5, https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S3.SS4.p6; tau setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p1; architecture: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Sports, Toys); Table 3 (Baidu industrial Recall@50-800 with ablated variants); Section 4.4 (online A/B: +3.60% conversion, +4.15% ARPU); Figures 4-6 (embedding analysis and recall-diversity curves).
  - Source: Public table: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.T2; industrial variants: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.T3; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS4.p1; diversity curves: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.F6.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER retrieves items from sparse semantic IDs alone; COBRA follows TIGER's SID construction but generates a dense vector after each sparse ID and fuses beam and ANN scores.; where: COBRA v1, baselines and SID setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.I1.i9.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.T2; the w/o Dense variant mirrors TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S4.I2.i2.p1.
- id: liger; relation: alternative; note: LIGER (Yang et al., 2024) unifies generative and dense retrieval as a hybrid, while COBRA cascades sparse-ID generation and dense-vector generation inside one decoder.; where: COBRA v1, Section 1 cites Yang et al. (2024), Unifying Generative and Dense Retrieval, for the fine-grained similarity gap of generative methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S1.p3; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: capsid; relation: alternative; note: CapsID removes the dense patch and instead makes the SID soft-routed and variable-length, reporting about half of COBRA's per-query latency at similar Recall@100.; where: Evidence is from the later CapsID paper: COBRA is a patch-route baseline in Tables 3, 4, and 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T6; latency comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS5.SSS0.Px5.p2.

## CogRec

- Page: pages/papers/cogrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM+Graph; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: CogRec grounds reasoning in Semantic ID structure through intra-layer graphs, item neighborhoods, and Match, LateralJump, and Explore routing steps, instead of a natural-language rationale weakly tied to the IDs.
- [Code](https://github.com/caskcsg/CogRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014: Beauty, Sports, Toys; user/item filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Chronological per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, remainder training. Direct evaluation uses the complete test set; default CoT uses a predefined subset, with separate full-test CoT evaluation.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p3
- **Candidates**: not reported; all generative variants share a trie containing the complete valid four-layer candidate-item SID set, but evaluation catalog size/sampling and history exclusion are not specified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The SID mapping and topology are shared across training stages.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S3.SS5.p2
- **SID**: BGE-base-en-v1.5 metadata embeddings (title/description/category), 768 dimensions and L2 normalization; residual K-means, 4 layers x 256 codes, 30 iterations/layer; 1,024 layer-specific tokens plus 2 boundary tokens. Intra-layer top-16 centroid graphs retain cosine >=0.15 edges; the mapping/topology is fixed across later stages. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 ; #S3.SS5.p2
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-1.7B; trie-constrained SID beam 10, temperature 0.6, top-p 1.0, max 8 new SID tokens. Reasoning samples 5 traces (temperature 1.5, top-p 0.95), up to 50 trace-conditioned SID hypotheses. Full-test CoT alone tail-truncates histories to Beauty/Sports/Toys 21/20/18 items. Reasoning-token cap, inference hardware/batch size and latency not reported; A800 GPUs are specified for training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S3.T1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p2 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p3
- **Results from**: Own CogRec experiments and controlled OneRec-Think Direct/CoT reproductions (Table 4/Figure 3); Table 3 mostly imports cited baseline scores, including standalone LETTER from RAGR and OneRec-Think from its original paper. Cross-source baselines do not share a guaranteed identical implementation/protocol.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S4.SS3.p2 ; #S4.SS2.p4 ; #S4.SS5.p1

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Hierarchical SID recommendation provides the identifier-generation foundation; TIGER also appears in the broad baseline comparison.; where: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24402v1#S2.p2 ; #S4.SS2.p3

## ColaRec

- Page: pages/papers/colarec.md
- Venue: CIKM’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: H-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: ColaRec builds generative identifiers from a pretrained collaborative filtering model and generates them from interacted-item content, with an item indexing task and a contrastive loss aligning both spaces.
- [Code](https://github.com/Junewang0614/ColaRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews: Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Cell Phones and Accessories (Phone); Food.com Recipe. Users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 198,502; Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 296,337; Phone 27,879 / 10,429 / 194,439; Recipe 17,813 / 41,240 / 555,618.
  - Source: Datasets and 5-interaction filter: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.T1.
- **Split**: General recommendation, not sequential: each user's interactions are randomly split 8:1:1 into training, validation, and test. Three runs are averaged.
  - Source: Random 8:1:1 per-user split for general (non-sequential) recommendation: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS2.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog
  - Source: Candidate set is the whole item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Random interaction split with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS2.p1; long-tail users are analyzed separately: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.T3.
- **SID**: GID length l=3 from hierarchical constrained K-means over pretrained LightGCN item embeddings, K=32 clusters per level (48 for Recipe). Collisions are avoided by construction: clusters hold at most K^(l-t) items and leaf positions are assigned randomly, so each item has a unique GID.
  - Source: Constrained hierarchical K-means over LightGCN embeddings, random leaf assignment, one unique GID per item: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.SS2.p2; l=3, K=32 (Recipe 48): https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search over valid GID prefixes; numerical beam width not reported. T5-small backbone. Recall and NDCG at n=5 and 10 (Table 2). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.SS5.p5; no numerical width found in Section 5.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (four datasets; mean of three runs); Table 3 (long-tail users); Table 4 (multi-task ablation and GID types); Figures 4-5 (GID length and cluster number).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.T2; long-tail users: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.T3; ablation and GID types: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.T4; GID length and K: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS7.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS7.SSS2.p2.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER builds content-only RQ-VAE identifiers; ColaRec builds collaborative GIDs from LightGCN embeddings and aligns them with item content through item-item indexing.; where: ColaRec v2, Section 5.3 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.I2.i8.p1 (adapted without sequential order); Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.T2.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec learns TIGER-style indices and aligns an LLM through language tasks; ColaRec uses a T5-small generator with collaborative GIDs and a contrastive ranking loss.; where: ColaRec v2, Section 5.3 baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.I2.i9.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S4.T2.
- id: cid; relation: alternative; note: P5-CID builds collaborative IDs for prompt-based P5 models that rank a candidate list in the prompt; ColaRec generates GIDs over the whole item set.; where: ColaRec v2, Section 5.3 explains why P5-based methods including Hua et al. (2023) are excluded as baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S5.SS3.p2; related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S2.SS2.p3.
- id: seater; relation: alternative; note: SEATER also builds tree-structured identifiers for generative recommendation; ColaRec derives its tree from collaborative LightGCN embeddings and adds content-based item-item indexing.; where: ColaRec v2, Section 1 and Section 2.2 cite SEATER among generative identifier methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18480v2#S2.SS2.p3; not a baseline in Table 2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: The generative identifiers (GIDs) come from offline LightGCN embeddings and clustering, so items without interactions have no collaborative representation to cluster (Sec. 4.2).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Existing LLM-based methods fuse content and collaborative signals but rely on textual language generation, which the authors state is not fully aligned with recommendation (Abstract). ColaRec instead decodes item identifiers with a sequence-to-sequence model tailored to recommendation (Abstract).

> "To model collaborative signals, the GIDs are constructed from a pretrained collaborative filtering model, and the user is represented as the content aggregation of interacted items." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Interactions") --> B["LightGCN"]
    B --> C["Hierarchical constrained K-means"]
    C --> D("GIDs")
    E("Item text + users") --> F["Shared encoder-decoder"]:::key
    D --> F
    F --> G["Constrained beam search"]
    G --> H("Next-item GID")
    L1{{"Recommendation loss"}} -.-> F
    L2{{"Indexing loss"}} -.-> F
    L3{{"BPR loss"}} -.-> F
    L4{{"Weighted contrastive loss"}} -.-> F
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Generative Identifier Construction

ColaRec applies constrained K-means hierarchically to item representations from a pretrained LightGCN model (Sec. 4.2).

> "Specifically, we first extract item representations from a pretrained LightGCN model. Then the constrained K-means algorithm is called hierarchically based on the item representations." (Sec. 4.2)

#### Item Indexing Task

The indexing task maps an item's text, together with the users who interacted with it, to the item's GID (Sec. 4.4, Eq. 7). It shares the encoder-decoder with the recommendation task (Sec. 4.4).

#### Training Objective

The recommendation loss, the indexing loss, a BPR loss with one sampled negative, and a weighted contrastive loss are trained jointly (Sec. 4.5, Eq. 11).

> "The idea is that items with similar GIDs should also be similar in the content-based semantic space." (Sec. 4.5)

#### Inference

Constrained beam search limits each token to those valid under the prefix (Sec. 4.5).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: ColaRec reports better performance than the baselines on four benchmark datasets (Abstract, Table 2).
- Ablation: Table 4 removes the textual content, the indexing task, the BPR loss, or the contrastive loss, and replaces the GIDs with three other identifier types (Table 4).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The contrastive loss pulls content representations toward the GID structure. This suggests that content similarity is reshaped by collaborative clusters, which may hurt items whose clusters are noisy.
- SEATER also uses tree-structured identifiers (`Tree-Clus.`) from `CF` input; ColaRec adds item content to the input (`Text+CF`).

## CoST

- Page: pages/papers/cost.md
- Venue: RecSys’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: C-RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: CoST trains the item tokenizer with a contrastive quantization objective that captures neighborhood relationships between items, instead of the reconstruction loss used by RQ-VAE.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: MIND news (preprocessing following Feng et al. 2022: interactions with at least 15 users kept, sequences capped at 70; 29,207 users / 12,251 items) and Amazon Office (users with fewer than 5 interactions removed), split by item count into Office (S) (2,868 users / 14,618 items) and Office (L) (16,696 users / 37,347 items).
  - Source: Datasets and filters: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out: last item for test, penultimate for validation, the remaining items for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates).
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard leave-one-out with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p3.
- **SID**: 3 residual-quantization levels with a codebook of size 64 shared across levels, 96-dimensional latent; Sentence-T5 768-dimensional input. The paper states each item receives a unique 3-tuple, but the mechanism that guarantees uniqueness is not reported.
  - Source: 3 shared codebooks of size 64, 96-dimensional latent, unique 3-tuples: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p2; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.F4.
- **Inference budget**: TIGER-style encoder-decoder; decoding method and beam width not reported. Recall and NDCG at K=5, 10, 20, 40 (MIND) and 10, 20 (Office). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Generator follows TIGER's structure, no decoding settings: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S3.SS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (MIND) and Table 3 (Office (S) and Office (L)), comparing random hashing, reconstruction-only RQ-VAE, contrastive-only, and combined losses; Figures 3-4 (temperature, epochs, codebook size, number of codebooks, embedding dimension).
  - Source: MIND: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.T2; Office: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.T3; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.F3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.F4.

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER's RQ-VAE is trained only with reconstruction loss; CoST keeps TIGER's generator and adds a contrastive loss so that neighboring items get distinguishable codes.; where: CoST v2, Section 1 identifies RQ-VAE from TIGER as the starting point: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S1.p3; Section 3.2 follows TIGER's architecture: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S3.SS2.p1; the reconstruction-only row in Tables 2-3 is the TIGER-style tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S4.T3.
- id: eager; relation: alternative; note: EAGER tokenizes items by hierarchical k-means and also integrates collaborative information, whereas CoST trains a residual quantizer with a contrastive objective over item neighborhoods.; where: CoST v2, Section 1 and Section 2 cite Wang et al. (2024b), EAGER, for hierarchical k-means and semantic-collaborative tokenization: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S2.p2; not compared in Tables 2-3.

## DACT

- Page: pages/papers/dact.md
- Venue: SIGIR’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec / Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: DACT fine-tunes a collaborative tokenizer as interactions drift, with an item-level drift detector and relaxed-to-strict code reassignment, to update Semantic IDs without full retraining or mass ID changes.
- [Code](https://github.com/HomesAmaranta/DACT)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Tools, Toys; users/items with <5 interactions removed. Amazon release year not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS1.p2
- **Split**: Chronological interaction stream: P0 is the first 60% for pretraining; P1-P4 equally divide the remaining 40%. Sliding-window sequences and leave-one-out train/validation/test; exact window and held-out positions not reported. Fine-tuning uses the current period from the previous checkpoint; retraining uses all accumulated periods.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2 ; #S4.SS1.SSS2.p3
- **Candidates**: not reported; only HR/NDCG@5,10 are specified, without evaluation catalog size, negative sampling or history exclusion.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Visibility**: Continual arrivals; warm items occur in P0 tokenizer training, cold items first appear after P0 (unseen by tokenizer too at initialization). TIGER/Toys warm-cold analysis evaluates P1 after current-period tokenizer/GRM updates; evaluation-time zero exposure is not established. CF is fine-tuned on current-period data; its validation/test-item exposure is not separately reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS2.p3 ; #S3.SS2.p4
- **SID**: Title/description semantic embeddings plus LETTER-style CF regularization; RQ-VAE, 3 layers x 256 codes, 32-dimensional code embeddings. DACT fine-tunes with drift/stability constraints, reassigns layer 1, and updates deeper codes only when layer 1 changes. Content-encoder/CF-model identity and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S2.SS1.p1 ; #S2.SS1.p5 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #S3.SS2.p2 ; #S3.SS2.p3
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive TIGER (T5 encoder-decoder; size not reported) or LCRec (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct decoder). CDIM is training-only. Beam, decoding constraints, token cap, inference hardware/batch size and latency not reported; Figure 8 measures relative training time.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; #S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS4.SSS5.p1
- **Results from**: Own P1-P4 continual-update experiments: TIGER on Beauty/Tools/Toys and LCRec on Beauty/Tools, comparing frozen/fine-tuned/retrained components and Reformer; LCRec additionally compares LSAT/PESO. Baseline scores are presented as experiments in this study; no imported-score source is identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.29705v1#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.SS1.SSS2.p2 ; #S4.SS2.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS2.SSS2.p1

## DAS

- Page: pages/papers/das.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Dual RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: DAS optimizes quantization and collaborative alignment in one stage, with multi-view contrastive alignment and dual quantization of users and ads, instead of two-stage alignment that loses information.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou advertising platform only (public datasets excluded). CTR task: 1.8 billion user-ad samples from about 100 million users and 8 million ads, with ad clicks as positives. Generative task: user-ad sequences from the past 15 days with length at least 10, about 50 million users.
  - Source: Industrial-only data and filters: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Split**: CTR: chronological 80% training / 20% testing. Generative task: leave-one-out (citing TIGER); the exact validation/test allocation is not reported. Online: multi-week A/B test with 10% of traffic (about 40+ million users).
  - Source: CTR chronological 80/20 and generative leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates for the generative HR@K/NDCG@K task).
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: Offline: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Online results report larger gains in cold-start scenarios (eCPM +8.98%), but generator/tokenizer visibility for those items is not reported.
  - Source: Offline protocols are in-domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; online cold-start scenarios are named but not defined: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS4.p1.
- **SID**: Separate user and ad SIDs from jointly trained RQ-VAEs: 3 codebooks x 512 codes, code dimension 32, k-means-initialized codebooks; ad embeddings 256-dimensional, user embeddings 1,024-dimensional. Collision handling: not reported (SIDs are also used as prefix-ngram sparse features in CTR models).
  - Source: 3 codebooks x 512 codes, dimension 32, k-means initialization: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S2.SS1.SSS2.p1; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Generative task: TIGER architecture on T5 (4-layer encoder and decoder, 13M parameters), trained on four NVIDIA GPUs for five days; decoding method, beam width, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. CTR models are trained on 16 T4 GPUs. Online, top-k SID predictions from TIGER++ feed two deployment strategies.
  - Source: Generative model details: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; online use of top-k SID predictions: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS4.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (offline CTR AUC/UAUC/GAUC with SID feature variants); Table 2 (generative HR/NDCG for TIGER, TIGER+, TIGER++); Table 3 (dual-alignment ablation); Section 4.4 (online A/B: eCPM +3.48% overall, +8.98% in cold-start scenarios).
  - Source: CTR table: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.T1; generative table: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.T3; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS4.p2.

### Related

- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER aligns the quantizer with CF embeddings in a two-stage pipeline; DAS trains quantization and debiased CF jointly in one stage and aligns user and ad SIDs dually.; where: DAS v2, Section 4.2 variant (4) +ASID (LETTER): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS2.p2; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.T1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER with unaligned RQ-VAE ad SIDs is the generative baseline; DAS replaces them with aligned ad SIDs (TIGER+) and adds aligned user SIDs (TIGER++).; where: DAS v2, Section 4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.SS2.p4; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.10584v2#S4.T2.
- id: adc-sid; relation: alternative; note: ADC-SID compares against DAS and adds adaptive alignment strength and dynamic behavioral weighting to denoise long-tail collaborative signals.; where: Evidence is from the later ADC-SID paper: DAS is a baseline in Section 4.1.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.I3.i4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.25622v3#S4.T2.

## DASO

- Page: pages/papers/daso.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: DASO reallocates part of each GRPO rollout group to prefix-guided completions at Semantic ID levels where candidates leave the target path and adds a graded prefix reward, unlike vanilla GRPO.
- [Code](https://github.com/LucasXinYu/DASO)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 Industrial & Scientific and Office Products, 5-core; proprietary user-to-item task with 1.36M recommendation examples and 319K users. Internal filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Experimental Setup and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.SSx1.p1
- **Split**: Public: fixed chronological next-item prediction, earlier interactions as history and a held-out next item. Train/validation/test sequences: Office Products 38924/4866/4866; Industrial and Scientific 36259/4532/4533. Split assignment rule and history-item cap: not reported. Internal: SFT train/eval 1139832/60168, GRPO training prompts 100326, and about 36K disjoint constrained-generation evaluation prompts; allocation rules not reported.
  - Source: Table 1, Appendix C and Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p1
- **Candidates**: Valid-catalog SID trie and 50-beam generated ranking for public evaluation. Full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation and history-item exclusion: not reported.
  - Source: Preliminaries, Appendix B and D: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx3.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A2.SSx2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A4.SSx4.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Easy/Medium/Hard diagnostics measure frozen-SFT prefix/target recovery, not item holdouts. Item-level exposure to the pretrained tokenizer: not reported.
  - Source: Experimental Setup and Appendix F: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A6.p2
- **SID**: Public: official frozen MiniOneRec RQ-VAE assignments from Qwen text embeddings, 3 levels x256 codes. Internal: 4 levels x2048 codes; SID construction details not reported. Collision handling: not reported for either setting.
  - Source: SID construction and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.SSx2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Public: trie-constrained beam50, HR@5/10 and NDCG@5. Internal: level-wise Top1/20 recall; internal beam width not reported. Primary training/evaluation setup uses 8x A100 80GB; inference batch and latency not reported. G=16 rollouts, Bmax=9 guided replacements and batch128 are training settings.
  - Source: Appendix D evaluation and H compute resources: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A4.SSx4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A4.SSx4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A8.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A4.T5
- **Results from**: Paper's Table2 public and Table3 internal experiments plus appendix ablations/diagnostics. SFT-only, MiniOneRec-style GRPO, uniform GT injection, Sibling-GRPO and DASO share SFT initialization and fixed SID/trie per setting. One algorithm run per dataset/backbone/method; no multi-seed significance tests. No borrowed baseline scores are identified.
  - Source: Experimental Setup, Tables2/3 and Appendix B: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A2.SSx2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A2.SSx2.p2

### Related

- id: minionerec; relation: predecessor; note: MiniOneRec supplies public SIDs and the baseline SFT-to-GRPO recipe.; where: DASO v1, Experimental Setup and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#Sx5.SSx1.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2608.20611v1#A3.SSx1.p2.

## Deco

- Page: pages/papers/deco.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text / –; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: Deco reads each history item as one fused token, condenses the history into a next-item concept, and runs beam search in a light KV-cached decoder instead of the full backbone.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon-2014 Beauty/Sports/Toys and Amazon-2023 BPC-23/Books-23, published 5-core subsets; MovieLens-25M subset (filtering rules not reported); Yambda-500M last30 days, exact deduplication, consecutive track-repeat collapse and user/item thresholds5/20.
  - Source: Sec.4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Global temporal: latest10% interactions test, latest10% of the remainder validation; Yambda uses last day test and preceding day validation. Each user's last event per held-out period is target; earlier within-period events enter history. History cap20 Amazon,100 MovieLens/Yambda. Separate Beauty leave-one-out comparison also reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1.2/4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS2.SSS1.Px5.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog: the training item catalog; history items are not excluded because repeats are legitimate targets. Main beam100; larger candidate budgets up to1000 are separately tested.
  - Source: Sec.4.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Yambda new targets mean absent from the last100 history items, not globally unseen items. Tokenizer-fitting exposure to test items/interactions: not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 protocol and repeat/new analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.F6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS2.SSS4.Px2.p1
- **SID**: Fixed RQ-KMeans,4 levels x2048 codes, from multilingual E5-large metadata embeddings or provided128-dimensional Yambda item embeddings. Popularity-based collision resolution is stated; detailed rule not reported. Depth study uses2-8 nested levels x256 codes.
  - Source: Sec.4.1.4 and SID-depth study: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS2.SSS3.Px2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Testbeam100 (validationbeam10), NDCG/Recall@10/50/100; copy pointer on Yambda. One H10080GB, bf16; main serving pipeline compiled with CUDA graphs and beam-shared history cache. Report batch128, peak sweep and50ms p95 budget;3.2-7.3x FusedGR throughput under that budget. GPU batch latency includes concept prefill/full beam/trie masking, excludes data loading/SID-item mapping and compilation/capture/warm-up. Each point repeats3 times,100 timed batches after10 warm-ups (50/5 above batch64). Table3 instead uses common eager PyTorch, batch128.
  - Source: Sec.4.1.4, Sec.4.2.2 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS2.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Results from**: Table2: paper's six matched-family models, shared SIDs/training budgets, mean+SD over3 seeds. Table3 external baselines are tuned/retrained from scratch under this protocol; eager native-path timing, RPG graph construction excluded. Separate Table4 Beauty leave-one-out baseline scores come from literature. Main throughput includes prefill; decoder-only comparisons excluding prefill are separate.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 baselines, Tables2-4 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS2.SSS1.Px5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: KV-cached TIGER is retrained as an autoregressive comparison.; where: Deco v2, Sec.4.1.3 and Table3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.T3.
- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: RPG is compared with both graph search and full-catalog scoring.; where: Deco v2, Sec.4.1.3 and Table3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.32980v2#S4.T3.

## DECOR

- Page: pages/papers/decor.md
- Venue: SIGIR’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: DECOR refines Semantic ID token embeddings by interaction context and fuses pretrained codebook embeddings with learned collaborative embeddings, instead of static token assignments that overwrite pretrained semantics.
- [Code](https://github.com/yliuaa/DECOR.git)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Scientific, Instrument and Game (paper labels); user/item 5-core filtering; chronological histories capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.T1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; full-ranking evaluation without sampling.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. RQ-VAE/text-encoder exposure to test items not reported; collaborative embeddings are learned from recommendation sequences.
  - Source: Sections 3.2/3.3/4.1 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: Sentence-T5 embeddings; frozen RQ-VAE with 3 levels x 256 entries, plus an incremental index token resolving identical 3-token prefixes: 4-token IDs. Token assignments remain fixed while embeddings are contextually composed and fused with learned collaborative embeddings.
  - Source: Sections 3.2/3.3/4.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS2.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; Recall/NDCG@5/10; experiments on one Tesla A40. Table 5 batches 8/16/32/64/128: DECOR 4.49-4.70 ms/sample, 213-223 samples/s; batch 128 adds 0.85 ms over TIGER. Prefix constraints not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2/4.8 and Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS8.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.T5
- **Results from**: Original Table 2 test results use seed 2025; significance tested across five seeds. Generative baselines rerun from official code; other baselines adapted or quoted when protocols match. Table 5 measures inference cost; Figure 5 measures convergence, excluding ETEGRec tokenizer-update epochs.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/4.2/4.7 and Tables 2/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.T5 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS7.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: DECOR augments TIGER's fixed tokenization with contextual token embeddings.; where: DECOR v2, Sections 3.2/4.1.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.T2.
- id: etegrec; relation: alternative; note: DECOR adapts embeddings without ETEGRec's repeated re-tokenization.; where: DECOR v2, Sections 3.4/4.7: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.SS4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS7.p1.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER is a tokenizer-enhancement baseline in the shared evaluation.; where: DECOR v2, Sections 1/4.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S1.p6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.T2.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID is a collaborative-indexing baseline.; where: DECOR v2, Section 4.2 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2509.10468v2#S3.T2.

## DIGER

- Page: pages/papers/diger.md
- Venue: SIGIR’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Learn. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam†
- TL;DR: DIGER makes Semantic IDs differentiable so recommendation gradients update the tokenizer, and adds decaying Gumbel noise against codebook collapse, instead of a tokenizer trained only for reconstruction.
- [Code](https://github.com/junchen-fu/DIGER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: B-Shop (cosmetic products), I-Shop (music-related products), Yelp (restaurants); remove users/items with fewer than five interactions. LLaMA-7B-generated item content; review text supplies interactions only. History cap not reported.
  - Source: Section 5, Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p1
- **Split**: Leave-one-out; exact validation/test allocation not reported. All reported results use the test set.
  - Source: Section 5, Evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p2
- **Candidates**: full catalog; predicted item ranked against the full item set.
  - Source: Section 5, Evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Pretrained RQ-VAE/content-encoder exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.3/5 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S4.SS3.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p2
- **SID**: Pretrained RQ-VAE initialization, then jointly optimized differentiable IDs: 3 code positions x 256 entries plus one conflict code. Conflict-code assignment details not reported. Training uses Gumbel exploration with uncertainty decay; validation/inference tokenizer assignments are deterministic.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/4.3/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S4.SS3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p4
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive next-SID generation; Recall/NDCG@10. Decoder search/beam, prefix constraints, inference batch and latency not reported. Experiments use two H100 GPUs; tokenizer argmax is reported separately from generation.
  - Source: Sections 3/4.2/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S3.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S4.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p4
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3 compare DIGER variants and baselines; main DIGER uses FrqUD. Most baseline results are quoted from LETTER (Wang et al., 2024); implemented methods are validation-tuned. Original Tables 4/5 give component and capacity/length ablations.
  - Source: Sections 5/6.2 and Tables 2/3/4/5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.T3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.SS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S7.T4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S7.T5

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER supplies the reference two-stage framework for differentiable-ID training.; where: DIGER v3, Sections 3/5 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.T3.
- id: etegrec; relation: alternative; note: DIGER replaces alternating distillation with direct recommendation gradients through indexing.; where: DIGER v3, Sections 2/6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S2.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S2.p4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.SS2.p2.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER is a comparison method and the source of most quoted baseline results.; where: DIGER v3, Sections 5/6.2 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S5.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.SS2.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19711v3#S6.T3.

## DiGR

- Page: pages/papers/digr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: DiGR uses Semantic ID tokens as item representations and scores items with one item-level function, instead of generating tokens, after showing that token decoding adds no ranking expressiveness.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SimGR-C408/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018: Musical Instruments, Arts/Crafts/Sewing, Video Games; user/item 5-core; chronological histories capped at 20.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, all earlier interactions training; learning rate and training epochs selected by validation grid search.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx4.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog for DiGR and other scoring-based methods; autoregressive baselines use prefix-constrained beam 20; history exclusion not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer exposure to test items is not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx3.p1 ; inductive capability is discussed, not evaluated as an item-holdout protocol.
- **SID**: RQ-VAE SIDs composed by mean-pooling shared position-specific SID-token embeddings; SID length, codebook sizes, tokenizer input encoder and collision handling not reported. Appendix D additionally compares R-KMeans and OPQ on Instruments.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx4.SSx2.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#A4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Precomputed item vectors and direct item-level scoring; no SID decoding. HR@1/5/10 and NDCG@5/10. Instruments timing: 0.074 s/user on one NVIDIA A100; inference batch size not reported. Beam 20 belongs to main autoregressive baselines, with 50/100 in the separate timing study.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx4.SSx2.SSS0.Px3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.T3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx3.p1
- **Results from**: Own recommendation comparison and controlled ranking/efficiency studies; ID baselines use RecBole, generative baselines follow official designs, LC-Rec shares Qwen3-4B/LoRA settings. Ranking-overlap reference is exhaustive LC-Rec scoring, not observed ground-truth preference order. Appendix D uses GPT-2 controls; no imported baseline scores stated; run counts/variance not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#A4.p1

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: Parallel SID-generation baseline in the main comparison.; where: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.T2
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: Autoregressive SID-generation baseline in the main comparison.; where: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.SSx1.SSSx2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07847v2#Sx5.T2

## DiscRec

- Page: pages/papers/discrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE / Learn. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: DiscRec adds item-level position embeddings and splits semantic and collaborative signals into two gated branches, one with attention inside each item, instead of fusing them in one embedding space.
- [Code](https://github.com/Ten-Mao/DiscRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Review subsets Beauty, Musical Instruments, Arts, Toys; remove users/items with fewer than 5 interactions; keep latest 20 history items, padding shorter histories.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Main per-user chronological leave-one-out: most recent item test, second-most-recent validation, remaining interactions training. Additional Beauty user-level random split: train/validation/test 8:1:1, with all models retrained from scratch.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS5.p2
- **Candidates**: full catalog; reported full-ranking evaluation over the entire item set, with prefix-tree-constrained generation; history exclusion not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Beauty additionally evaluates held-out users and low-popularity targets; LETTER uses pretrained SASRec embeddings, whose test-item exposure is not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS5.p2
- **SID**: 4 RQ-VAE codebooks, 256 entries/level, 32 dimensions/entry, from LLaMA2-7B title/description representations. DiscRec-T uses TIGER tokenization; DiscRec-L uses LETTER collaborative/diversity regularization with pretrained SASRec embeddings. Tokenizer trained before recommender; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S3.SS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Prefix-tree-constrained autoregressive decoding, beam 20; Recall/NDCG@5/10; inference hardware, batch size and measured latency not reported. The paper gives theoretical complexity rather than serving measurements.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S3.SS3.p4
- **Results from**: Own DiscRec-T/DiscRec-L comparisons, ablations and Beauty generalization studies. Baselines follow referenced implementations under a unified generative configuration; EAGER is resized to dimension 128 and its histories are correctly sorted chronologically. No copied baseline result scores stated; run counts/variance not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.15576v2#S4.SS5.p2

## DOS

- Page: pages/papers/dos.md
- Venue: WWW’26 Short
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Orth. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only†; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: DOS aligns the Semantic ID codebook with the generation space through a user-item dual flow over collaborative signals and rotates the semantic space with orthogonal residual quantization.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Private Meituan production data only: past-year quantization data covering 24M unique items, and 60-day downstream data with 180M interactions. User/item filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S3.SS1.SSS1.p2
- **Split**: Quantization data: train/validation/test 8:1:1, partition method not reported; 50-click histories predict the 51st item. Downstream data: first 57 days training, last 3 days validation; a generation test split is not separately reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p2 ; #S3.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported for Hit@10 generation. Quantization classification uses randomly sampled negatives; negative count, sampling distribution and user-history exclusion not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p2 ; #S3.SS1.SSS2.p1 ; #S3.SS2.SSS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The quantization dataset covers past-year business items; validation/test-item exposure during SID learning is not separately reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p2 ; #S3.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **SID**: Qwen3-0.6B-embedding encodes restaurant name/categories, reservation status, prices and dishes into 1,024 dimensions. Dual user/item Transformer flows share an orthogonal residual quantizer: 3 layers x 1,024 codes, with salient-feature selection and residual propagation. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S2.SS1.p2 ; #S2.SS1.p3 ; #S2.SS1.p6 ; #S2.SS1.p8 ; #S2.SS2.p5 ; #S3.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Downstream generation evaluated within HSTU. Model size, beam/decoding constraints, token budget, inference hardware/batch size and latency not reported; batch 1,024 is a training setting.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; #S3.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Results from**: Own offline quantization AUC/F1 and HSTU Hit@10 experiments; RQ-KMeans/RQ-VAE baselines are fine-tuned for application metrics. Own one-week A/B test on 30% of production traffic reports +1.15% revenue from adding DOS SIDs to the original baseline.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04460v1#S3.SS2.p1 ; #S3.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; #S3.SS4.p1 ; #S3.SS4.p2

## DPE-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/dpe-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: – / Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Masked → RL (→ Masked KD for Fast); Inference: Diff.+Legalize
- TL;DR: DPE-Rec completes bundles with a diffusion language model, adding semantic-fork-aware GRPO to keep bundles diverse and pseudo-trajectory distillation to reveal more tokens per denoising step.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Spotify playlists (K=30/60/90), POG outfits (K=4), IQON3000 outfits (K=8). Remove bundles shorter than K, truncate longer bundles; IQON3000 also drops outfits with missing images. User/item-frequency filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Split**: Disjoint bundles: released Spotify/POG partitions (ratios not reported); IQON3000 shuffled outfits split 7:1:2. Each evaluation bundle exposes its first K/2 items and predicts the remainder. Training-only adjacent-swap/random contiguous-K augmentation uses r=0.4 for Spotify, 0.8 for POG/IQON3000.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Candidates**: sampled: 100N total, where N=K/2 targets: Spotify K=30/60/90 uses 1,500/3,000/4,500; POG 200; IQON3000 400. Shared sets contain all N targets plus uniformly sampled non-target items; observed-bundle/user-history exclusion not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Partitions are bundle-disjoint; CLHE representation fitting and SID-quantizer exposure to validation/test items are not separately reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1
- **SID**: Fixed 64D CLHE features (released Spotify/POG; IQON3000 trained on text/image features); 3 residual-VQ tokens with C=256 for Spotify/IQON3000, 128 for POG. A fourth catalog-order token disambiguates collisions (max 74/53/171 for Spotify/POG/IQON3000). Separate level vocabularies plus boundary/MASK tokens; generated SIDs undergo exact-match or reconstructed-embedding cosine legalization, removing selected candidates for distinct outputs.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p3 ; #S8.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p5 ; #S4.SS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Sequential AO teacher reveals one SID token/step; Fast reveals confidence-qualified positions in parallel plus a quota meeting budget F. Numeric default F/threshold, model size and inference batch size not reported. All experiments use one A100-80GB. Per-bundle DPE/Fast latency (ms): Spotify K=30 443.59/62.34, K=60 903.41/65.79, K=90 1340.05/66.72; POG 59.38/46.49; IQON3000 112.51/58.32.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5 ; #S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1 ; #S4.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p4 ; #S8.SS2.p1 ; #S5.T2
- **Results from**: Own training/evaluation of all methods with 5 seeds, reporting mean/std quality and measured latency. Spotify/POG backbone pretraining is from scratch with the DDBC recipe; fixed CLHE representations are shared. Compared generators are UniGRec, DiffGRM and DDBC; no imported recommendation-score source is identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.34700v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 ; #S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S8.SS2.p1 ; #S5.T2

## DREAM

- Page: pages/papers/dream.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: CART; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Altern.; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: DREAM refines cold-start item Semantic IDs after the initial assignment, with an intent-aware tokenizer proposing candidates, the frozen generator selecting one, and a dynamic beam keeping weighted ID hypotheses.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games; iterative user-core-5 and item-core-3 filtering.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p3
- **Candidates**: full catalog
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The cold subset means at most five interactions, not exclusively unseen items; Section 3.1 counts training frequency whereas Section 4.1 says total frequency. Strict item-level generator/tokenizer holdouts: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1 and 4.1 define low-frequency subsets, not a separate unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **SID**: Frozen Llama-3-8B text embeddings initialize shared RQ-VAE SIDs (4 positions x 256 codes). CART refines assignments with collaborative residuals, Gumbel-Softmax/STE, diversity regularization and a static-index anchor, exporting top-8 candidates per cold item. UC3 produces a refined single-path index; CPDE preserves alternative SIDs for multi-path inference (B=4). Collision disambiguation: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.1, 3.3-3.6 and 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p4
- **Inference budget**: Beam-Aware multi-path inference is primary: B=4 retained SID paths per cold item and one per warm item in a union trie; Compat-Top1 retains one path per item for ablations. LoRA is merged into the backbone at deployment. Evaluation K=5/10/50; numerical autoregressive decoding beam width, inference hardware, batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 3.5-3.6 and 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS5 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S3.SS6 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS1.p4
- **Results from**: This paper's experiments: Tables 2/3/4 report cold/overall/warm comparisons with DREAM's primary Beam-Aware view; Table 5 reports stage ablations and Compat-Top1; Figures 2-4 report Sports mechanism diagnostics.
  - Source: Tables 2-5 and Figures 2-4: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.T2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.T3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.T4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.T5 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06947v1#S4.SS5

## EAGER

- Page: pages/papers/eager.md
- Venue: KDD’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Dual H-KM; Backbone: Dual Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: Fusion
- TL;DR: EAGER decodes behavior tokens and semantic tokens with a shared encoder and two decoders, adding contrastive and semantic-guided transfer tasks, instead of using only one type of item information.
- [Code](https://github.com/yewzz/EAGER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-July 2018): Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games; Yelp 2019 transactions (January-December 2019). 5-core filtering of users and items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 198,360; Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 296,175; Toys 19,412 / 11,924 / 167,526; Yelp 30,431 / 20,033 / 316,354.
  - Source: 5-core filtering and timestamp ordering: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS1.p1; Amazon and Yelp scope: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.I2.i2.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training; training histories limited to 20 items.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation and history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS1.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-k lists come from beam search in two streams.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard leave-one-out with no cold-start experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS1.p2.
- **SID**: Two codes per item: behavior codes from DIN embeddings and semantic codes from Sentence-T5 embeddings, each built by hierarchical k-means with k=256 branches, splitting until each child cluster contains a single item; code length l follows from the item count and k.
  - Source: Dual hierarchical k-means codes until each leaf holds one item: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S3.SS3.p3; k=256: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS1.p3; length varies with k: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.SS5.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search in each of the behavior and semantic decoders returns top-k codes; the 2k predictions are merged by log-probability confidence. Table 6 (Beauty, top-k=5, beam size 100): 0.0325 s per sample for EAGER versus 0.0281 s for TIGER; hardware and inference batch size not reported. Recall and NDCG at 5, 10, and 20.
  - Source: Two-stream beam search and confidence ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S3.SS6.p2; speed table: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T6.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Sports, Toys, Yelp versus sequential, tree-based, and generative baselines); Table 3 (TSG/GCT/STT ablations); Tables 4, 5, 7 and Figures 4-6 (modalities, summary token, contrastive metric, layers, cluster number); Table 6 (inference speed).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S3.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T3; analyses: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T7; speed: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T6.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER decodes one content-based semantic ID; EAGER decodes behavior and semantic hierarchical k-means codes with two decoders and merges them by confidence.; where: EAGER v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.I6.i1.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S3.T2; speed comparison in Table 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S4.T6.
- id: seater; relation: alternative; note: SEATER also uses tree-structured identifiers for generative retrieval; EAGER builds separate behavior and semantic trees and aligns them with contrastive and transfer tasks.; where: EAGER v2, Section 1 cites SEATER among generative recommenders: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S1.p2; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: lmindexer; relation: alternative; note: LMIndexer learns semantic IDs from text with a language model; EAGER keeps fixed k-means codes from pre-trained behavior and semantic encoders.; where: EAGER v2, Section 2 cites LMIndexer among semantic indexing methods: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S2.p2; not a baseline in Table 2.
- id: cost; relation: alternative; note: CoST learns RQ codes with a contrastive objective, whereas EAGER clusters frozen embeddings and adds contrastive learning on the generator side.; where: EAGER v2, Section 2 cites CoST: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.14017v2#S2.p2. CoST v2, Section 2 in turn cites EAGER as a hierarchical k-means tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.14774v2#S2.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: Removing the two-stream architecture causes the largest drop in the ablation (Sec. 4.3, Table 3), and on Beauty EAGER takes 0.0325 s per sample at inference against 0.0281 s for TIGER (Table 6).
Limitation: Inference runs beam search in two decoders and merges the results, which makes EAGER slower than TIGER (Sec. 3.6, Table 6).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Existing generative methods use either the behavioral or the semantic side of item information, which the authors state neglects their complementary nature (Abstract). EAGER names three requirements for combining them: one architecture for both feature types, independent learning for each, and interaction between them (Abstract).

> "we propose (1) a two-stream generation architecture leveraging a shared encoder and two separate decoders to decode behavior tokens and semantic tokens with a confidence-based ranking strategy" (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("User history") --> B["Shared encoder"]
    B --> C["Behavior decoder"]
    B --> D["Semantic decoder"]
    C --> E("k behavior codes")
    D --> F("k semantic codes")
    E --> G["Confidence ranking of 2k codes"]:::key
    F --> G
    G --> H("Items")
    L1{{"GCT: summary-token distillation"}} -.-> C
    L1 -.-> D
    L2{{"STT: masked code reconstruction"}} -.-> C
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Behavior Codes and Semantic Codes

A pre-trained DIN model is the behavior encoder and Sentence-T5 is the semantic encoder, with hidden size 128 (Sec. 4.1). Hierarchical k-means with cluster number 256 turns each embedding into codes (Sec. 3.3, Sec. 4.1).

#### Global Contrastive Task

A summary token in each stream is distilled toward that stream's pre-trained item embedding with a positive-only contrastive metric instead of InfoNCE (Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3).

#### Semantic-Guided Transfer Task

The semantic global feature reconstructs masked behavior codes, and a recognition objective adds a relevance classifier (Sec. 3.5).

#### Confidence-Based Ranking

Each decoder returns $`k`$ codes, and the $`2k`$ predictions are ranked by log probability (Sec. 3.6).

> "With the 2*k prediction codes, we calculate the log probabilities over the codes as the confidence score of each prediction, which is similar to the perplexity used in the language model and the lower value indicates more confidence." (Sec. 3.6)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: EAGER reports better performance than existing methods on four public benchmarks (Abstract).
- Ablation: removing the global contrastive task (GCT) costs more than removing the semantic-guided transfer task (STT) (Sec. 4.3, Table 3).

  > "Removing GCT leads to more performance drops than removing STT, suggesting that global information distillation of the inter-code is slightly more important than the knowledge flow between the intra-code." (Sec. 4.3)

- Visual features: on Yelp, ViT-B features of item covers produce a visual semantic code (Sec. 4.4, Table 4).
- Inference speed: with top-k 5 and beam size 100 on Beauty, RecForest takes 0.0499 s and DIN 0.2349 s per sample (Table 6).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- Both code sets come from frozen encoders and offline clustering. This suggests that adding items requires re-running both encoders and the clustering.
- CoST trains its codes with a contrastive objective (`C-RQ`); EAGER keeps `Dual H-KM` codes fixed and adds the contrastive term on the generator side.
