## LC-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/lc-rec.md
- Venue: ICDE’24
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: LC-Rec assigns non-conflicting item indices by vector quantization with uniform semantic mapping and tunes an LLM with alignment tasks, so it generates items from the whole catalog without candidate lists.
- [Code](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/LC-Rec/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews (May 1996-October 2018): Musical Instruments, Arts Crafts and Sewing, Video Games; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered; sequences capped at 20 items. Sizes (users / items / interactions): Instruments 24,773 / 9,923 / 206,153; Arts 45,142 / 20,957 / 390,832; Games 50,547 / 16,860 / 452,989.
  - Source: Amazon 2018 subsets, 5-interaction filter, length 20: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T2.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: most recent item for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking over the entire item set instead of sampled evaluation). Separate analysis (Table 5): choose between the target and one negative that is language-similar, collaborative-similar (by SASRec embeddings), or random; history exclusion for these negatives not reported.
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; separate pairwise test with one negative: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over mean-pooled LLaMA embeddings of title and description, added to the LLaMA tokenizer as new tokens. Conflicts are resolved without an extra suffix level: the last-level codewords of each conflicting group are redistributed under a uniform-distribution constraint.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32 over LLaMA text embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; uniform last-level redistribution for conflicts: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p3.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 20 for all generative methods; tokens leading to invalid item indices get zero probability. LLaMA backbone with DeepSpeed; hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. HR and NDCG at 1, 5, 10.
  - Source: Beam size 20 and invalid-token masking: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS4.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Instruments, Arts, Games; LC-Rec averaged over instruction templates); Table 4 (alignment-task ablation); Table 5 (similar-negative ranking accuracy).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T4; negative-item analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T5.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER resolves leaf conflicts with an extra index level and uses a small seq2seq model; LC-Rec redistributes conflicting last-level codes uniformly and tunes LLaMA with language-collaborative alignment tasks.; where: LC-Rec v4, conflict discussion: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1; baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.I1.i10.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T3.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID builds collaborative indices and also adds a supplementary index for conflicts; LC-Rec learns semantic RQ indices from LLM text embeddings.; where: LC-Rec v4, conflict discussion: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1; baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.I1.i9.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S4.T3.
- id: vq-rec; relation: predecessor; note: LC-Rec borrows the idea of learned semantic indices from VQ-Rec and TIGER, then adapts it for LLM tuning.; where: LC-Rec v4, Section 3.2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS2.SSS1.p4.
- id: transrec; relation: alternative; note: TransRec also builds LLM-based generative recommendation with multi-facet identifiers; LC-Rec uses learned VQ indices with alignment tuning.; where: LC-Rec v4, Section 2.2 and Section 3.5 related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S2.SS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2311.09049v4#S3.SS5.p3.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: The item indices come from text embeddings only, so collaborative semantics enter only through the tuning tasks (Sec. III-B).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Items in recommender systems are often indexed by IDs outside the vocabulary of a large language model (LLM), which leaves a semantic gap between the two (Abstract).

> "In essence, LLMs capture language semantics while recommender systems imply collaborative semantics, making it difficult to sufficiently leverage the model capacity of LLMs for recommendation." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Item text") --> B["LLaMA embeddings"]
    B --> C["Vector quantization + uniform semantic mapping"]
    C --> D("Item indices")
    D --> E["LLaMA instruction tuning"]:::key
    L1{{"Sequential item prediction"}} -.-> E
    L2{{"Explicit: text to index and back"}} -.-> E
    L3{{"Implicit: asymmetric, intention, preference"}} -.-> E
    E --> F("Generated index")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Item Indexing

LC-Rec encodes item text with LLaMA and quantizes the embeddings (Sec. III-B). Uniform semantic mapping redistributes the last-level codewords of items that would otherwise share an index (Sec. III-B2).

#### Alignment Tuning

Sequential item prediction is the main objective (Sec. III-C1). Two explicit tasks map titles or descriptions to indices and back (Sec. III-C2). Implicit tasks add asymmetric item prediction, intention-based prediction, and preference inference (Sec. III-C3).

> "On the one hand, the LLM should be capable of accurately identifying the item indices based on the associated title or description. On the other hand, it is expected that LLM can naturally capture relevant item information from its indices." (Sec. III-C2)

#### Training

All tasks are formatted as conditional language generation for one instruction-tuned model (Sec. III-D).

> "To this end, we employ LLaMA [25] as our backbone model and then optimize it via instruction tuning." (Sec. III-D)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: LC-Rec outperforms traditional recommenders and existing LLM-based recommenders (Abstract).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- TIGER uses the same `RQ-VAE` codes with an `Enc-Dec` generator; LC-Rec uses a `Dec-Only` LLM trained with `Multi-task NTP`.

## LESSRec

- Page: pages/papers/lessrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text / Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE / R-KM / LETTER; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: LESSRec encodes the history separately at each Semantic ID level and restricts attention to the target token's level, adding an item-level semantic sequence, instead of attending to all levels.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023 Games/Software and earlier Amazon Beauty; iterative user/item 5-core filtering; histories capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Leave-one-out; exact validation/test allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4.1.3 specifies a shared candidate index but not full-catalog versus sampled evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. LETTER uses SASRec collaborative embeddings; its exposure to test items is not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.3/4.1.4 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE, RQ-Kmeans, or LETTER: 4 levels x 256 codes, fixed offline; Sentence-T5 text embeddings. RQ-Kmeans uses trainable conditional subcodebooks. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.4 and Appendix B.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#A2.SS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained beam 10; batch 32; single RTX 4090 24GB; K=5/10. End-to-end latency not reported; Figure 6 measures encoder CUDA time per sample.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.5/4.6 and Figure 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.F6
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: three-seed comparisons across tokenizers; baselines implemented using official code or RecBole. Table 6 reports training costs, not inference latency.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5 and Tables 2/6: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37286v1#S4.T6

## LETTER

- Page: pages/papers/letter.md
- Venue: CIKM’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: Learn. RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: LETTER regularizes an RQ-VAE tokenizer with a collaborative alignment loss and a diversity loss, so that item Semantic IDs carry collaborative signals and reduce code assignment bias found in earlier identifiers.
- [Code](https://github.com/HonghuiBao2000/LETTER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Instruments, Amazon Beauty, and Yelp; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are discarded. Dataset release/date windows and retained corpus sizes are not reported.
  - Source: Dataset names and explicit filtering of both users and items: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Split**: Chronological interaction histories with leave-one-out evaluation; training histories contain at most 20 items. The exact validation/test position allocation is not reported beyond the leave-one-out label.
  - Source: Leave-one-out and the 20-item training-history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; chronological histories: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS2.SSS1.p1. Methods/Experiments and Appendix 7 do not spell out the exact validation-versus-test position allocation beyond naming leave-one-out.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); generation is constrained to valid identifier continuations with a trie.
  - Source: Inference defines trie-constrained generation, but not full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1; evaluation states only metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; Methods/Experiments and Appendix 7 were checked.
- **Visibility**: Standard leave-one-out evaluation; per-target generator/tokenizer training visibility is not reported. The tokenizer uses item content and SASRec collaborative embeddings before generator training, but inclusion of held-out-only items in tokenizer/CF training is not reported. A dedicated cold-start evaluation is not reported.
  - Source: Tokenizer training precedes generator training: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS2.p1; LLaMA2 content embeddings and SASRec collaborative embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; leave-one-out: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1. Methods/Experiments and Appendix 7 give no item-disjoint cold-start experiment or explicit tokenizer/CF visibility for held-out-only items.
- **SID**: Main configuration: 4 residual-quantization levels x 256 codewords, with 32-dimensional code embeddings; the identifier contains 4 learned codes. Collision handling or an additional collision suffix: not reported.
  - Source: Four levels, 256 entries each, and 32-dimensional embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2; L is the identifier length: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p4. Methods/Experiments and Appendix 7 do not specify collision resolution or an additional disambiguation suffix; the four learned levels must not be replaced by TIGER's three levels plus suffix.
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained autoregressive generation; numerical beam width not reported. Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. All experiments use 4 NVIDIA RTX A5000 GPUs; allocation specifically for inference is not reported. Inference batch size and measured latency: not reported.
  - Source: Trie-constrained autoregressive generation: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1; metric cutoffs: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; experiment hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1. Methods/Experiments and Appendix 7 specify no beam width, inference batch, or measured latency; the 1,024 batch in https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 is tokenizer training, not inference.
- **Results from**: Original paper Table 1, with separate LETTER-TIGER and LETTER-LC-Rec rows on Instruments, Beauty, and Yelp. The authors reimplement TIGER and instantiate LC-Rec with LoRA-tuned LLaMA2-7B; these are this paper's experimental configurations, not the original TIGER paper's results.
  - Source: Original main table and model instantiations: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS2.p1; TIGER reimplementation and LC-Rec/LoRA setup: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: LETTER builds on TIGER's RQ-VAE semantic tokenization by adding collaborative and diversity regularization plus a ranking-guided generation loss.; where: LETTER, Section 3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p6; Section 4.3.1 defines the progression from TIGER to LETTER-TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: LC-Rec supplies an existing code-ID recommender with auxiliary language-alignment tasks; LETTER reuses it as a backend for its learnable tokenizer.; where: LETTER, Section 4.1.2 describes LC-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Section 4.1.4 explicitly instantiates LETTER on LC-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; Table 1 includes LC-Rec and LETTER-LC-Rec: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.T1.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: LETTER compares against P5-CID, which builds identifiers by spectral clustering of an item co-appearance graph instead of LETTER's regularized RQ-VAE tokenization.; where: LETTER, Section 4.1.2 identifies the P5-CID baseline from Hua et al.: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Table 1 compares P5-CID with LETTER: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S4.T1; Section 3.1 defines LETTER's RQ-VAE tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.07314v1#S3.SS1.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On Instruments, LETTER-TIGER reports Recall@10 of 0.1122 against 0.1058 for TIGER, and adding either regularization alone also improves TIGER (Table 2).
Limitation: The collaborative regularization needs embeddings from a separately trained CF model (Sec. 3.1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Earlier item identifiers, whether plain IDs, text, or codebook codes, fall short in encoding semantics, carrying collaborative signals, or handling code assignment bias (Abstract). LETTER's Semantic IDs (SIDs) serve two generators, TIGER and LC-Rec (Sec. 4.1.3).

> "LETTER incorporates Residual Quantized VAE for semantic regularization, a contrastive alignment loss for collaborative regularization, and a diversity loss to mitigate code assignment bias." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Semantic embedding") --> B["RQ-VAE tokenizer"]:::key
    L1{{"Semantic: RQ-VAE loss"}} -.-> B
    L2{{"Collaborative: align with 32-dim SASRec"}} -.-> B
    L3{{"Diversity: constrained k-means clusters"}} -.-> B
    B --> C("Fixed identifiers")
    C --> D["TIGER or LC-Rec generator"]
    L4{{"Ranking-guided generation loss"}} -.-> D
    D --> E["Trie-constrained generation"]
    E --> F("Next item")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Semantic Regularization

An RQ-VAE quantizes the item's semantic embedding level by level, so the identifier keeps a coarse-to-fine semantic hierarchy (Sec. 3.1).

#### Collaborative Regularization

A contrastive alignment loss pulls each item's quantized embedding toward its embedding from a trained collaborative filtering (CF) model (Sec. 3.1, Eq. 3). The paper names SASRec and LightGCN as example CF models, and the experiments use 32-dimensional SASRec embeddings (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 4.1.3).

> "Intuitively, collaborative regularization encourages items with similar collaborative interactions to exhibit similar code sequences." (Sec. 3.1)

#### Diversity Regularization

A diversity loss groups the code embeddings by constrained k-means, pulls embeddings in the same cluster together, and pushes different clusters apart (Sec. 3.1, Eq. 4). It targets code assignment bias, where some codes receive more items than others, and item generation bias (Sec. 1).

> "As illustrated in Figure 5(a), a biased code embedding distribution is more likely to cause biased code assignment in the latent space, where some codes are assigned to more items." (Sec. 3.1)

#### Training and Generation

LETTER first trains the tokenizer with the combined loss (Eq. 5), then uses it to tokenize items for training and inference of the generator (Sec. 3.2). LETTER also adds a ranking-guided generation loss to the generator's training to improve its ranking ability (Abstract, Sec. 1). At inference, a trie restricts generation to valid identifiers.

> "To ensure generating valid identifiers, we follow (Hua et al., 2023) to employ constrained generation (De Cao et al., 2020) via Trie" (Sec. 3.2.2)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main results: LETTER-TIGER and LETTER-LC-Rec outperform their backend models on Instruments, Beauty, and Yelp (Sec. 4.2, Table 1).
- Ablation: adding either the collaborative or the diversity regularization to TIGER improves its performance (Sec. 4.3.1, Table 2).
- Code usage: the collaborative regularization lowers the number of codes that TIGER uses, and the diversity regularization raises it again (Sec. 4.3.2, Fig. 6).

  > "Although adding collaborative regularization decreases the code utilization of TIGER (from 148 to 76), integrating diversity regularization inversely compensates for the drop in code utilization." (Sec. 4.3.2)

- Collaborative signals: Tables 3 and 4 analyze how well the identifiers carry collaborative information (Sec. 4.3.4).
- Hyperparameters: the paper varies the identifier length $`L`$, the codebook size $`N`$, the loss weights $`\alpha`$ and $`\beta`$, the cluster number $`K`$, and the temperature $`\tau`$ (Sec. 4.3.5).

  Longer identifiers lower performance beyond 4 tokens, which the authors attribute to error accumulation in autoregressive generation.

  > "Continuously increasing the identifier length from 4 to 8 will inversely degrade the performance. This is reasonable because autoregressive generation suffers from error accumulation (Ren et al., 2024b)." (Sec. 4.3.5)

  A codebook that is too large can also hurt.

  > "However, 2) blindly expanding N might inversely hurt the performance, where larger codebook size might be more susceptible to noise in the item's semantic information, potentially leading to the over-fitting of some meaningless semantics." (Sec. 4.3.5)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The conclusion names three directions for future work: tokenization with rich user behaviors, cross-domain item tokenization, and combining natural-language user instructions with tokenized interaction histories (Sec. 6).

**Our analysis.**

- The tokenizer is trained once and then fixed (`Fixed`), so a change in the catalog requires retraining the tokenizer and re-tokenizing items. ETEGRec updates the tokenizer and the generator in turns (`Altern.`), and DIGER lets the generator loss update the tokenizer directly (`Joint`).
- The collaborative regularization needs a CF embedding for every item. This suggests that items without interactions receive no collaborative signal in their identifiers.
- The opposite effects of the two terms on code usage (Sec. 4.3.2) suggest that their weights trade one property against the other.

## LGRID

- Page: pages/papers/lgrid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: DSRQ; Backbone: Disc.; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: LGRID encodes item fields jointly with an LLM, routes hidden states into geographic and semantic slots, and quantizes the two streams separately, instead of quantizing one entangled representation.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou local-life industrial data (10,000,000 interactions, 6,673,350 users, 2,251,418 items, 1,000 categories) and public Foursquare (244,896 interactions, 1,084 users, 38,334 POIs, 401 categories; coarse location text derived from coordinates). SID-construction fine-tuning uses a curated, category-balanced subset of 120,000 training and 5,000 validation POIs with incomplete descriptions excluded. Interaction filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.T8; curated SID-construction subset: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS2.p1.
- **Split**: All methods share the same train/validation/test split, but the split rule is not reported.
  - Source: Shared split statement without allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: Kuaishou: a spatially constrained candidate set within a fixed 15 km offline distance threshold (following LGSID), shared by all methods. Foursquare: full catalog (standard full-ranking protocol).
  - Source: Kuaishou distance-thresholded candidates and Foursquare full ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. SID construction uses item text only and no interaction labels.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol; SID construction uses no interaction labels: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p1.
- **SID**: 4-token SID from dual-stream residual quantization of Qwen3-8B slot representations: 2 geographic codes + 2 semantic codes; per-level codebook size: not reported. For non-SID backbones, the SID embedding is concatenated with the original item-ID embedding; a collision-resolution rule is not reported. Full-SID collision rate is 39.9% on Kuaishou (RQ-VAE 98.0%, LGSID 97.0%).
  - Source: Dual-stream RQ with D=2 per stream, 4-token SID: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S3.SS6.SSS2.p1; collision rate: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T5; SIDs as features beside item IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S3.SS6.SSS3.p1.
- **Inference budget**: n/a for generation (SIDs feed discriminative and sequential rankers that are scored by AUC). Offline SID construction 21.80 ms per item versus 13.97 ms for RQ-VAE; online input preparation 0.50 versus 0.48 ms per request (Table 10); hardware for timing not stated in the main text. SID-construction fine-tuning uses 4 GPUs (effective batch 192); recommender batch 10,240.
  - Source: Offline SID construction and online lookup cost: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS4.p1; training batches: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS2.p3.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (AUC across ten recommendation backbones with SID baselines on Kuaishou and Foursquare); Tables 2-4 (full-corpus POI self-retrieval, attribute decoding, joint versus field-wise encoding); Table 5 (utilization and collision rate); Tables 6-7 (ablations); Section 4.5 and Table 10 (efficiency).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S3.T1; retrieval and decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T4; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T5; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T7.

### Related

- id: lgsid; relation: competitor; note: LGSID injects geography into one fused representation before quantization; LGRID disentangles geographic and semantic slots and quantizes them in two streams, cutting full-SID collisions from 97.0% to 39.9%.; where: LGRID v1, baselines and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S3.T1; collisions in Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T5; candidate protocol follows LGSID: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER's RQ-VAE on a single representation is the base SID baseline; LGRID keeps residual quantization but applies it per disentangled stream.; where: LGRID v1, RQVAE baseline attributed to Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS1.p2; Table 1 and Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T5.
- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc adds geographic signals to SID generation through a shared representation; LGRID argues such geo-aware variants still entangle attributes.; where: LGRID v1, Section 1 and Section 2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S2.SS1.p1; not a baseline in Table 1.
- id: gnpr-sid; relation: alternative; note: GNPR-SID builds POI SIDs from one fused embedding for next-POI generation; LGRID targets ranking features with disentangled geographic codes.; where: LGRID v1, Section 1 and Section 2.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S2.SS1.p1; not a baseline in Table 1.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On Kuaishou and Foursquare, LGRID reports up to a 5.44% relative AUC gain over SID baselines, and reduces the full-SID collision rate to 39.9% against 97.0% for LGSID (Abstract).
Limitation: The geographic slots mirror a fixed administrative hierarchy of province, city, district, and town (Sec. 3.4.1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Existing Semantic ID (SID) frameworks build one representation and then quantize it (Abstract). The authors state that this mixes geography, brand, and category, causes information loss and collisions, and gives SID positions no clear meaning (Abstract). LGRID gives each SID position an explicit attribute.

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Item fields") --> B["Joint LLM encoding"]
    B --> C["SD-Block"]:::key
    C --> D("k geographic slots")
    C --> E("N-k semantic slots")
    L1{{"Hierarchical hard negatives"}} -.-> C
    L2{{"LDR: orthogonal slots"}} -.-> C
    D --> F["Dual-stream RQ"]
    E --> F
    F --> G("Attribute-aligned SIDs")
    G --> H["Discriminative ranker"]
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Structured Disentangled Block

The Structured Disentangled Block (SD-Block) splits the hidden states into $`N`$ slot tokens with Semantic Anchor Injection, Anchor-Guided Perception, and Structured Causal Routing (Sec. 3.4). There are $`k`$ geographic slots and $`N-k`$ semantic slots such as brand and category (Sec. 3.4.1).

#### Synergistic Alignment Learning

Alignment learning makes the slots both decodable and discriminative (Abstract). Contrastive learning uses hierarchical hard negatives (Sec. 3.5.2).

> "To prevent inter-slot redundancy, we impose Latent Diversity Regularization (LDR), which encourages subspace orthogonality so that each slot captures non-overlapping features." (Sec. 3.5.3)

#### Dual-Stream Residual Quantization

The two streams are quantized separately, so SID positions correspond to item attributes (Abstract).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Attribute decoding: accuracy is over 99% for coarse-grained geographic fields (Abstract).
- Hard negatives: they raise town-level discrimination from 37.17% to 83.51% (Sec. 4.4).

  > "In the SACL group, vanilla sampling yields limited fine-grained discrimination (Town: 37.17%), whereas hierarchical hard negatives raise it to 83.51%." (Sec. 4.4)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- A full-SID collision rate of 39.9% still leaves many items sharing an SID. This suggests that LGRID fits discriminative ranking, which tolerates shared SIDs, better than generation.
- TIGER quantizes one representation with `RQ-VAE`; LGRID quantizes two streams (`DSRQ`) and feeds a discriminative ranker.

## LGSID

- Page: pages/papers/lgsid.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Geo+CF; Tokenization: Geo-Idx+RQ; Backbone: Disc. / Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim. / NTP; Inference: Scoring / Beam†
- TL;DR: LGSID aligns an LLM to spatial relationships with a reward model and G-DPO, then builds Semantic IDs from spatial and content attributes plus residual tokens from the aligned LLM representation.
- [Code](https://github.com/JiangHaoPG11/LGSID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou local-life feed data only: 50,000,000 samples, 19,080,888 users, 2,325,266 items, 19,408 brands, 818 categories, with item text and geographic location. For discriminative models, all positives are kept and negatives down-sampled 1:4. Further filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Industrial-only dataset and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SS0.SSSx1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.T4.
- **Split**: Generative models: leave-one-out on the down-sampled data (last item for test, second-last for validation, the rest for training). Discriminative models: split rule not reported; settings selected on validation data.
  - Source: Leave-one-out for generative models on the down-sampled data: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SS0.SSSx1.p1; split for discriminative AUC not stated.
- **Candidates**: Discriminative AUC: evaluation samples with negatives down-sampled at 1:4 to positives; how negatives are drawn and whether user history is excluded: not reported. Generative Hit and NDCG at 5 and 10: full catalog versus sampled not reported.
  - Source: Negative down-sampling and metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SS0.SSSx1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SS0.SSSx1.p1.
- **SID**: Hierarchical residual quantizer over G-DPO-aligned BGE embeddings (1,024-dimensional) with a KL regularizer toward uniform cluster usage; number of levels and per-level codebook sizes K_l: not reported. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Hierarchical quantizer with uniform-usage regularization: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx4.SSx3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx4.SSx3.p5; BGE embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SSx1.p1; no codebook sizes or collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: SIDs are used as features in DIN, DIEN, SIM, TWIN, ETA and as targets in TIGER and OneRec generators; decoding method and beam width: not reported. All experiments on two 48GB GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SSx2.p1; generative backbones: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SSx3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (AUC of five discriminative rankers with different tokenizers); Table 2 (TIGER and OneRec generators with different tokenizers); Table 3 (semantic and geographic coverage after alignment); Table 5 (robustness over runs); Table 6 (similarity weight).
  - Source: Discriminative: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T1; generative: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T2; alignment: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T3; robustness: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A4.T5; lambda: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A4.T6.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER's RQ-VAE is a tokenizer baseline and TIGER is one of two generative backbones; LGSID aligns the LLM embedding with geographic rewards before a hierarchical quantizer.; where: LGSID v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SSx3.p1; Tables 1 and 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T2.
- id: onerec; relation: predecessor; note: OneRec serves as the second generative backbone into which LGSID's SIDs are plugged.; where: LGSID v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#A2.SSx3.p1; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx5.T2.
- id: gnpr-sid; relation: alternative; note: GNPR-SID builds POI SIDs for next-POI generation; LGSID targets local-life ranking features and aligns embeddings with geographic distance rewards.; where: LGSID v1, related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx2.SSx2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14221v1#Sx4.SSx2.p1.
- id: lgrid; relation: successor; note: LGRID later follows LGSID's candidate protocol and replaces its single fused representation with disentangled geographic and semantic streams.; where: Evidence is from the later LGRID paper: protocol https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#A1.SS3.p2; baseline and collision comparison https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27944v1#S4.T5.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: LLM alignment needs a separately trained list-wise reward model before G-DPO, and the residual tokens change whenever that alignment is redone (Abstract).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Text-based recommenders encode item text with prompts and tokenize items into discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) (Abstract). In local-life services, the authors state that putting location into the prompt misses fine-grained spatial characteristics and real distances between items (Abstract).

> "However, in domain-specific tasks such as local-life services, simply injecting location information into prompts fails to capture fine-grained spatial characteristics and real-world distance awareness among items." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Item text + location") --> B["List-wise reward model"]
    B --> C["G-DPO"]:::key
    L1{{"In-batch contrastive regularizer"}} -.-> C
    C --> D("Geographic vectors")
    D --> E("Residual tokens")
    F("Spatial and content attributes") --> G("Primary tokens")
    G --> H("SIDs")
    E --> H
    H --> I["DIN, TWIN, TIGER, OneRec ..."]
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Reward Model

A list-wise reward model learns spatial relationships among items (Introduction).

> "The RL-based alignment module first trains reward models using distance-aware list-wise sampling to capture and compress real-world spatial relationships." (Introduction)

#### G-DPO Alignment

G-DPO uses the reward model to inject spatial knowledge and collaborative signals into the LLM (Abstract). An in-batch contrastive loss keeps each item's embedding close to the reference model's output (G-DPO, Eq. 7-8).

> "To preserve LLMs' semantic representations during G-DPO updates, we introduce an in-batch contrastive loss as a similarity regularizer, as shown in Eq. 7." (G-DPO)

#### Hierarchical Geographic Item Tokenization

Primary tokens come from discrete spatial and content attributes, and residual tokens come from the aligned LLM's geographic vectors (Abstract).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: on Kuaishou industry datasets, LGSID outperforms discriminative and generative recommendation models (Abstract).
- Downstream models: Table 1 uses the SIDs in DIN, DIEN, SIM, TWIN, and ETA, and Table 2 in TIGER and OneRec (Tables 1-2).
- Other analyses: the paper reports ablations, visualizations, and case studies (Abstract).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- Primary tokens need discrete attributes. This suggests that items with missing attributes need a fallback.
- LGRID uses `DSRQ` codes for discriminative ranking only; LGSID uses `Geo-Idx+RQ` codes for both ranking and generation.

## LIGER

- Page: pages/papers/liger.md
- Venue: arXiv’24
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Dense; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: LIGER integrates sequential dense retrieval into a Semantic ID generative retriever, after a controlled comparison of both approaches, to narrow their performance gap and improve cold-start recommendation.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, and Steam with 5-core filtering of users and items; sequences truncated to the 20 most recent items. Sizes (users / items / cold-start items): Beauty 22,363 / 12,101 / 43; Toys 19,412 / 11,924 / 56; Sports 35,598 / 18,357 / 81; Steam 47,761 / 12,012 / 400.
  - Source: Datasets, 5-core, truncation: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS1.p1; statistics and cold-start counts: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#A2.T3.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item for test, preceding item for validation, the rest for training; early stopping on in-set NDCG@10; mean and standard deviation over three seeds. Test targets are reported separately for in-set and cold-start items.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS1.p4; three seeds: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS2.p1.
- **Candidates**: Hybrid: generative retrieval returns K=20 candidates by beam search, which are ranked together with the cold-start items by dense retrieval (K swept from 20 to 100 and K=N in Table 4). Dense baselines score the full catalog.
  - Source: Hybrid candidates (K from beam, ranked with cold-start items by dense scores): https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS2.p2; K sweep: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#A3.T4.
- **Visibility**: In-set targets: warm. Cold-start targets: unseen by tokenizer too; cold-start items are excluded from RQ-VAE training (the paper says to avoid contamination), and the generators fail to produce them. Exact criterion for selecting cold-start items beyond the counts in Table 3: not reported.
  - Source: Cold-start items excluded from RQ-VAE training: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS1.p4; cold-start definition beyond counts not stated.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 128) over sentence-T5-XXL text embeddings; following TIGER, an extra token is appended to make IDs unique.
  - Source: 3 levels x 256 with dimension 128 and an extra uniqueness token: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS1.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search retrieves K candidates (K=20 for the main result) from a T5 encoder-decoder (6 layers each), then a dense head ranks them with cold-start items. Complexity is stated as O(tK) versus O(N) for dense retrieval (Table 1); hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam retrieval of K candidates and complexity: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S2.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S3.T1; model: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Sports, Toys, Steam; in-set and cold-start Recall@10 and NDCG@10; three seeds); Table 4 (number of retrieved candidates K); Figures 1, 3, 4 (dense versus generative retrieval and cold-start generation probabilities); Appendix D (ablations).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.T2; K sweep: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#A3.T4; motivation figures: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S1.F1, https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S2.F3, https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S2.F4.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER retrieves only by beam search over semantic IDs and almost never generates cold-start items; LIGER reranks TIGER-style beam candidates plus cold-start items with a dense head trained jointly.; where: LIGER v2, faithful TIGER implementation: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S1.p5; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.T2; cold-start analysis of TIGER's epsilon quota: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S2.SS4.p3; LIGER builds on TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#S4.SS2.p2.
- id: vq-rec; relation: alternative; note: VQ-Rec uses vector-quantized codes inside a dense retriever; LIGER keeps generative beam search and adds dense ranking only over a small candidate set.; where: LIGER v2, Appendix A related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.18814v2#A1.p2.
- id: cobra; relation: alternative; note: COBRA later cascades sparse-ID generation with a generated dense vector inside one decoder and cites LIGER for the fine-grained similarity gap of generative methods.; where: Evidence is from the later COBRA paper, Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.02453v1#S1.p3.
- id: gem-rec; relation: successor; note: GEM-Rec later builds on LIGER's reproduction of the TIGER architecture and its 5-core preprocessing.; where: Evidence is from the later GEM-Rec paper, Section 5.4 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#S5.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.22231v1#A2.SS1.p1.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: Every cold-start item joins the candidate set, and the design assumes that cold-start items are few (Sec. 3).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Sequential dense retrieval stores one representation per item, so memory grows with the catalog (Abstract). Generative retrieval predicts Semantic IDs (SIDs) instead, but a fair comparison of the two was missing (Abstract).

> "Our findings indicate that the model's learned conditional probabilities tends to overfit to items seen during training, leading to a significantly reduced capability to generate cold-start items." (Sec. 2.4)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("SID tokens + text + positions") --> B["T5 encoder-decoder"]
    L1{{"Next-token loss"}} -.-> B
    L2{{"Cosine loss to next item text"}} -.-> B
    B --> D["Beam search: K items"]
    D --> E("Candidates")
    F("Cold-start items") --> E
    E --> G["Rank by encoder embedding"]:::key
    G --> H("Top items")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Input and Training

Each SID token embedding adds the item's text representation and two position embeddings (Sec. 3). Training combines a cosine-similarity loss toward the next item's text representation with next-token prediction on its SID (Sec. 3).

#### Hybrid Inference

The decoder proposes candidates, and the encoder output ranks them together with the cold-start items (Sec. 3, Algorithm 1).

> "During inference, the decoder retrieves K items by beam search, then supplemented with cold-start items and ranked with the encoder's output embeddings." (Sec. 3)

The authors base this design on an assumption about cold-start items (Sec. 3).

> "This design choice is based on the hypothesis that cold-start items are relatively sparse compared to in-set items, as recommendation systems periodically update themselves to incorporate newly introduced items." (Sec. 3)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Reporting setup: generative retrieval returns 20 items, which are ranked with the cold-start items (Sec. 4.2).
- Main result: LIGER narrows the gap to dense retrieval and improves cold-start recommendation on the evaluated datasets (Abstract).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The final order comes from the dense embedding. The generated SID selects candidates but does not decide their order.
- TIGER retrieves by `Beam` search only; LIGER adds a dense loss (`NTP + Dense`) and `Hybrid` ranking.

## LLaDA-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/llada-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Par. VQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Masked; Inference: Diff.
- TL;DR: LLaDA-Rec generates parallel Semantic IDs by discrete diffusion with bidirectional attention, history-level and item-level masking, and an adapted beam search, instead of left-to-right autoregressive decoding.
- [Code](https://github.com/TengShi-RUC/LLaDA-Rec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Industrial Scientific (50,985 users / 25,848 items), Musical Instruments (57,439 / 24,587), Video Games (94,762 / 25,612). Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Amazon 2023 categories and ordering: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T2.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out: last item for test, second-to-last for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-k lists from the adapted beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Parallel semantic IDs from a Multi-Head VQ-VAE over Sentence-T5 embeddings: the embedding is split into 4 sub-vectors, each quantized by its own codebook of 256 codes (dimension 32). Collision handling: not reported.

Bidirectional Transformer encoder (4 layers; 6 for Game). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported. Recall at 1, 5, 10 and NDCG at 5, 10.
  - Source: Beam search adapted to diffusion decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.SS3.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.SS3.SSS4.p1; no numerical beam size or hardware found.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Scientific, Instrument, Game versus item-ID, diffusion, and semantic-ID baselines; paired t-tests); Table 4 (ablations including RQ-VAE tokenizer and greedy decoding); Figure 3 (attention mechanisms); Section 5.4 (hyperparameters).

### Related

- id: rpg; relation: competitor; note: RPG predicts long unordered OPQ codes in parallel with multi-token prediction; LLaDA-Rec generates parallel VQ codes by discrete diffusion with an adapted beam search.; where: LLaDA-Rec v1, Table 1 comparison and semantic-ID baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T3.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates hierarchical RQ-VAE codes left to right with causal attention; LLaDA-Rec uses bidirectional attention and fills code positions in any order.; where: LLaDA-Rec v1, Table 1 and baselines (TIGER and TIGER-SAS): https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T3.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER improves a hierarchical tokenizer for left-to-right generation; LLaDA-Rec replaces the hierarchy with parallel codes suited to diffusion.; where: LLaDA-Rec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2; Tables 1 and 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T3.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec aligns an LLM to semantic IDs with auxiliary tasks and causal decoding; LLaDA-Rec trains a bidirectional masked predictor with history-level and item-level masking.; where: LLaDA-Rec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2; Tables 1 and 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T3.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec pools product-quantized codes into an item representation for discriminative ranking; LLaDA-Rec generates parallel codes directly.; where: LLaDA-Rec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p2; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.06254v1#S4.T3.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: Fewer diffusion steps improve generation efficiency but lower recommendation performance, and the authors leave a better trade-off as an open question (Sec. 5.4.3, Fig. 5).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Autoregressive generative recommenders decode a Semantic ID (SID) one token at a time with causal attention. The authors name two limitations of this setup: each token attends only to its predecessors, and errors in early tokens propagate through the fixed left-to-right order (Abstract). LLaDA-Rec replaces left-to-right decoding with discrete diffusion over all SID positions.

> "To address these issues, we propose LLaDA-Rec, a discrete diffusion framework that reformulates recommendation as parallel semantic ID generation." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Item text embedding") --> B["Multi-Head VQ-VAE"]
    B --> C("Parallel SIDs")
    C --> D["Mask predictor"]:::key
    L1{{"User-history masking"}} -.-> D
    L2{{"Next-item masking"}} -.-> D
    D --> E["Adapted beam search"]
    E --> F("Next item")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Parallel Tokenization

A Multi-Head VQ-VAE splits the item's text embedding into sub-vectors and quantizes each sub-vector independently, one head per SID position (Sec. 4.1). The authors use this scheme because residual quantization does not match a bidirectional architecture (Abstract).

#### Masked Training

Training uses two masking mechanisms (Abstract). User-history masking captures sequential dependencies between items. Next-item masking masks tokens of the target item's SID while the user history stays visible, so the predictor learns relationships between tokens of the same item (Sec. 4.2.3).

#### Adaptive-Order Decoding

Inference starts from a fully masked SID and fills it over several steps (Sec. 4.3.4). At each step the model selects positions to keep and remasks the rest.

> "All unselected positions are remasked so that the MASK predictor can re-evaluate them in the context of the partially generated sequence." (Sec. 4.3.4)

The number of steps is controllable, and each step can predict several tokens (Sec. 4.4.2). An adapted beam search keeps several candidates during this process, because standard beam search does not fit diffusion-based generation (Abstract).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S0("All positions masked") --> P["Predict all masked positions"]
    P --> K["Keep selected positions"]:::key
    K --> R["Remask the rest"]
    R -->|next step| P
    K --> D("Full SID after the last step")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: LLaDA-Rec outperforms ID-based and generative recommenders on three real-world datasets (Abstract).
- Generation order: the adaptive order performs best, and left-to-right sometimes performs worst (Sec. 5.4.2, Fig. 4).

  > "The adaptive approach consistently delivers superior performance, with left2right occasionally producing the poorest results, highlighting the shortcomings of the commonly used left2right scheme." (Sec. 5.4.2)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The tokenizer is trained once and kept fixed (`Fixed`), and it encodes item text only (`Text`). This suggests that collaborative signals enter only through the generator.
- RPG also generates parallel codes with a `Non-AR` generator; RPG uses `Par. OPQ` codes and `Graph` decoding, while LLaDA-Rec uses `Par. VQ` codes and `Diff.` decoding.

## MACRec

- Page: pages/papers/macrec.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Cross RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MACRec applies cross-modal quantization over text and image features to build Semantic IDs with fewer conflicts, and adds implicit and explicit cross-modal alignment to generator training.
- [Code](https://github.com/zhangfw123/MACRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-October 2018): Musical Instruments (17,112 users / 6,250 items), Arts Crafts and Sewing (22,171 / 9,416), Video Games (42,259 / 13,839), with text and image features. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and date range: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (following P5 and Hua et al. 2023); the exact validation/test allocation is not reported beyond the label.
  - Source: Leave-one-out named only: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking across the entire item collection rather than sampling).
  - Source: Full ranking across the entire collection: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p3.
- **SID**: Separate text (LLaMA) and image (ViT-L/14) semantic IDs from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codewords, aligned by layer-wise cross-modal contrastive and alignment losses. Conflicting IDs are resolved as in MQL4GRec by reassigning codewords according to item-codebook distances. Pre-resolution collision rates, e.g. Instruments text 2.38% and image 3.23%.
  - Source: Per-modality RQ-VAE, 4 levels x 256, conflict reassignment following MQL4GRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx1.SSSx2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx1.SSSx3.p5; collision rates: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T4.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search generates candidates in each modality, and the two modalities' scores are averaged; beam width not reported. T5 backbone with 4-layer encoder and decoder. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained beam search per modality and score averaging: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx2.SSSx3.p3; T5 backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Instruments, Arts, Games; MQL4GRec run without its extra-category pre-training); Table 3 (ablations); Table 4 (item collision rates); Figures 3-4 (hyperparameters and code assignment).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T3; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T4; code distribution: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.F4; hyperparameters: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.F3.

### Related

- id: mql4grec; relation: competitor; note: MQL4GRec quantizes each modality into its own SIDs with cross-modal translation; MACRec adds layer-wise cross-modal contrastive learning in quantization and implicit and explicit alignment in generation, and reuses MQL4GRec's conflict resolution and ensemble.; where: MACRec v2, baselines without pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4; Table 2 and Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T4; reused conflict resolution: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx1.SSSx3.p5.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER quantizes a single text embedding; MACRec quantizes text and image separately and aligns them, while keeping TIGER's T5 backbone and constrained beam search.; where: MACRec v2, baselines and backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.SSx1.p4; Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID uses collaborative clustering IDs for a P5 model; MACRec builds multimodal semantic IDs.; where: MACRec v2, Table 2 baseline P5-CID: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2.
- id: card; relation: alternative; note: CARD later renders image, title, and neighbors into one visual card and quantizes it with a non-uniform RQ-VAE, comparing against MACRec.; where: Evidence is from the later CARD paper: baselines and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.I1.i9.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26427v1#S4.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: MACRec leads all baselines on HR@10, NDCG@5, and NDCG@10 on all three datasets, while on Games HR@5 MISSRec reports 0.0674 against 0.0671 for MACRec (Table 2).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Generative recommendation needs Semantic IDs (SIDs) that are hierarchical, have few conflicts, and support generator training (Abstract). Earlier multimodal generative recommenders quantize each modality on its own, so text and image do not inform each other's IDs.

> "However, existing multimodal GR models typically encode each modality separately to obtain semantic IDs for different modalities." (Related Work)

MACRec adds cross-modal interaction at two points: inside the quantizer and in the generator's training tasks (Methodology).

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Text embeddings") --> C["Text RQ"]
    B("Image embeddings") --> D["Image RQ"]
    A -.-> PT("Text pseudo-labels")
    B -.-> PI("Image pseudo-labels")
    PI -.-> L1{{"Residual-level contrastive"}}:::key
    PT -.-> L2{{"Residual-level contrastive"}}:::key
    L1 -.-> C
    L2 -.-> D
    C --> E("Text SIDs")
    D --> F("Image SIDs")
    E --> G["Generator"]
    F --> G
    L3{{"Implicit + item- and sequence-level alignment"}} -.-> G
    G --> H["Average scores"]
    H --> I("Next item")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Dual-Modality Pseudo-Labels

MACRec clusters items separately by their text embeddings and by their image embeddings. The cluster labels define positive pairs for contrastive learning in the quantizer (Dual-modality Pseudo-label Generation).

#### Cross-Modal Quantization

Each modality passes through an MLP and a residual quantizer. A contrastive loss at the residual levels uses the labels of the other modality (Cross-modal Quantization with Contrastive Learning).

> "More concretely, we use visual pseudo-labels to enhance the residual representations of the text modality, and conversely, use textual pseudo-labels to optimize those of the visual modality." (Cross-modal Quantization with Contrastive Learning)

Reconstruction and quantization losses keep the codes able to recover the original embeddings (Cross-modal Reconstruction Alignment).

#### Multi-Aspect Alignment

The generator trains on next-item prediction within each modality, an implicit alignment of the two SID representations, and explicit item-level and sequence-level tasks across modalities (Generative Recommendation with Multi-aspect Alignment).

> "For sequence-level alignment, we construct a prediction task where a historical sequence of textual semantic IDs is used to predict the visual semantic ID of the next recommended item." (Explicit Alignment with Different Generation Tasks)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Ablation: removing any module lowers HR@10 on all three datasets (Table 3).
- Collisions: MACRec has lower item ID collision rates than MQL4GRec (Table 4).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- MQL4GRec also builds separate text and image SIDs (`Dual RQ`); MACRec replaces this with `Cross RQ` and adds a contrastive term to the generator objective (`NTP + Ctr.`).
- The representation uses text and image only (`Text+Img`). CARD adds collaborative signals (`Text+Img+CF`) and quantizes one combined input with `NU-RQ`.

## MBGen

- Page: pages/papers/mbgen.md
- Venue: CIKM’24
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: Bal. VQ+KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: MBGen interleaves behavior tokens and item tokens in one sequence, predicts the next behavior type and then the next item, and scales with a position-routed sparse architecture.
- [Code](https://github.com/anananan116/MBGen)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Retail (Taobao/Tmall) and IJCAI; purchase/cart/favorite/click behaviors, with purchase as target. Remove items occurring fewer than five times in training sequences; maximum history 50 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2 ; #S4.SS1.SSS1.p3 ; #S4.SS1.SSS1.p4 ; #S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: latest interaction test, penultimate validation; remaining interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; target ranked against all other items rather than sampled negatives.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; retained items have at least five training occurrences. SID features come from pretrained MB-STR embeddings; pretraining exposure to test interactions not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p4 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **SID**: Three item tokens with per-position size K=64 Retail/96 IJCAI. Balanced SID: K-entry VQ codebook, K-cluster residual K-means per first-token bucket, then random collision-disambiguation token. Balanced CID: random item-number remapping and base-K digits, without features. Behavior token precedes each item.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S3.SS2.p3 ; #S3.SS2.p4 ; #S3.SS2.p5 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; top-10 outputs; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Hardware, inference batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4
- **Results from**: Original Tables 3/4/5: target-behavior, behavior-specific, joint behavior-item prediction. Most baselines reproduced in RecBole; MB-GMN excepted, with result provenance not specified. Table 6: ablations; Table 7: token distribution.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2405.16871v1#S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.T6 ; #S4.T7 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p1

## MBGR

- Page: pages/papers/mbgr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MBGR adds business-aware Semantic IDs, business-specific prediction, and dynamic label routing to generative recommendation, to avoid a seesaw between businesses that share one ID space.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Meituan only. Generative training data: one year of click sequences from 38,258,649 users over 54,875,570 merchants in four businesses (A 61.47%, B 9.56%, C 12.31%, D 16.66%). Downstream data: 37,349,276 users and 783,946,360 interactions over a rolling 30-day window. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.I1.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.I1.i2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.I2.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.I2.i2.p1.
- **Split**: Offline: not reported (the paper mentions a validation set for hyperparameter search but not how train, validation, and test are formed). Online: one-week A/B test with 30% of Meituan production traffic against the baseline without MBP; CTCVR +3.98%.
  - Source: No offline split rule stated; validation used for grid search: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS4.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS6.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S1.I1.i3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled candidates for HR@10); downstream ranking uses business-wise GAUC.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS3.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Business-aware semantic IDs: each item's K token embeddings are re-encoded with its business type through a gated encoder and decoded per business; number of SID levels, codebook sizes, and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Business-aware encoder/decoder over K input tokens: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S4.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S4.SS1.p6; no codebook settings found.
- **Inference budget**: Decoding method and beam width: not reported. 16-layer Transformer (8 heads, 128-dimensional embeddings), sequences up to 1,500 items; trained and deployed on NVIDIA A100-80GB GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Hardware and architecture: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.SS1.SSS4.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (HR@10 per business versus SASRec, TIGER, HSTU); Table 2 (downstream CTCVR GAUC); Table 3 (ablations); Tables 4-7 (time decay, business weights, expert count).
  - Source: Generative: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T1; downstream: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T3; hyperparameters: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T6, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02684v1#S6.T7.

## MDGR

- Page: pages/papers/mdgr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: –; Tokenization: Par. OPQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Masked; Inference: Diff.+Beam
- TL;DR: MDGR uses a parallel codebook, adaptive masking along time and samples, and warm-up two-stage parallel decoding for masked diffusion recommendation, instead of fixed-order autoregressive Semantic ID decoding.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Electronics/Books: remove users with fewer than five interactions, maximum history 20. Industrial Southeast Asian e-commerce logs: May-December 2025, >1B interactions, 18M users, 25M items, mean history 128; industrial filtering not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Sliding-window next-item training; chronological leave-one-out: latest interaction test, penultimate validation, remainder training. Online A/B: January 5-12, 2026, control/treatment each 20% uniformly sampled users.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S5.SS6.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 5.1 gives metrics but no evaluation universe or negative-sampling protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S5.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S5.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **SID**: OPQ-based parallel codebooks: 8 x 300, 256-dimensional code vectors, using Qwen3-8B content embeddings. Complete SIDs map to item sets through an offline index; collision disambiguation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S4.SS2 ; #S5.SS1.SSS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; four single-position warm-up steps, then two positions/step. Table 3 reports six total steps and 2.527 QPS versus 2.212 for eight serial steps; implementation text inconsistently says four subsequent parallel steps. Recall/NDCG@5/10; inference-specific hardware, batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #S5.T3 ; #S5.SS3.SSS2.p2
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: offline three-dataset comparison; baseline-result reuse not stated. Table 3: industrial efficiency; Table 4: industrial ablations; Section 5.6: online A/B against production TIGER.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.19501v1#S4.T2 ; #S5.T3 ; #S5.T4 ; #S5.SS6.p1

## Merge-and-Branch

- Page: pages/papers/merge-and-branch.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: Merge-and-Branch compresses each history item's Semantic ID and text into few learned tokens and predicts several target IDs from one shared history in a tree layout, reducing fine-tuning cost.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2014 5-core Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games.

- **Split**: Per-user chronological last/penultimate interactions test/validation; earlier interactions training. Main M&B result selects the best of five seeds by validation NDCG@10.
  - Source: Section 4.1 Metrics and protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; invalid or unresolved predictions count as misses.
  - Source: Section 4.1 Metrics and protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Held-out items do not fill missing future branches; tokenizer/CF-teacher item exposure: not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.4 and Appendix B.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#A2.SS2.p1
- **SID**: Sentence-T5-XXL plus 3-level RQ-VAE, 256 codes/level, deterministic collision suffix: four-token SID.
  - Source: Appendix B.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#A2.SS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Main: beam 50, Recall/NDCG@5/10; inference batch/hardware not reported. Efficiency: H200, batch 1, beam 100, synthetic contexts 64-2048, four merged tokens/item; Tree latency 76.33-83.85 ms/request including prefill/search.
  - Source: Section 4.1, Appendix B.3 and Table 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#A2.SS3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.T4
- **Results from**: Table 3 mixes authors' runs with original-paper scores (TIGER, LETTER-Beauty, EAGER, EAGER-LLM-Beauty/Sports, GRAM) and GRAM reproductions (P5-CID, LC-Rec). M&B and Table 4 decoding measurements are this paper's experiments.
  - Source: Table 3, Table 4 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37973v1#A2.SS1.p1
