## MiniOneRec

- Page: pages/papers/minionerec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: MiniOneRec is an open-source framework for RQ-VAE Semantic ID construction, supervised fine-tuning of Qwen backbones, and reinforcement learning with constrained decoding, to test generative scaling on public benchmarks.
- [Code](https://github.com/AkaliKong/MiniOneRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Industrial and Scientific, Office Products. Trimming follows Bao et al. (2024): users and items with fewer than 5 interactions removed; events limited to October 1996-November 2018 for Industrial; histories truncated to at most 10 items. Retained sizes: in Appendix B (not restated here).
  - Source: Datasets and trimming: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#A2.p1.
- **Split**: Chronological 8:1:1 split into training, validation, and test. OOD study: train only on Industrial and evaluate on Office without tuning.
  - Source: Chronological 8:1:1: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#A2.p1; OOD transfer: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported explicitly (the policy predicts among all catalog candidates and returns the top-k beams; whether metrics are full-catalog is not stated).
  - Source: Ranking among all catalog items via beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S3.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: In-domain: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. OOD: Office items are unseen by the generator (trained only on Industrial); whether the RQ-VAE was fit on Office items: not reported.
  - Source: In-domain chronological split; OOD on a never-seen domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS4.p2.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords over Qwen3-Embedding-4B text embeddings; the three layers of 256 SID tokens are appended to the Qwen2.5-Instruct tokenizer vocabulary. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: L=3 x K=256 RQ-VAE over Qwen3-Embedding-4B, SID tokens added to vocabulary: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S3.I1.i3.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#A1.SS1.p2; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search returns the top-k list; the numerical width at evaluation is not reported (RL rollouts use beam width 16). SFT on 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam search for recommendation lists and RL rollouts (width 16): https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S3.SS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S3.SS4.SSS1.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS5.SSS2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Industrial and Office versus traditional, generative, and LLM-based baselines); Table 2 (unseen Office domain); Table 3 (pre-trained versus random initialization); Figures 1 and 4 (scaling and rollout strategies).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.T1; OOD: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.T2; pre-training effect: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.T3; rollout strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.SS5.SSS2.p2.

### Related

- id: onerec; relation: predecessor; note: MiniOneRec is an open-source reproduction of the OneRec-style pipeline: SID construction, SFT, and RL with constrained beam rollouts on public data.; where: MiniOneRec v1, Section 1 positions it against OneRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S1.p3; Section 3.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S3.SS3.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER trains a small generator with next-token prediction only; MiniOneRec uses an LLM with SID alignment tasks and GRPO.; where: MiniOneRec v1, Table 1 generative baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec aligns an LLM to SIDs with SFT tasks; MiniOneRec keeps such alignment throughout SFT and RL and adds reinforced preference optimization.; where: MiniOneRec v1, Table 1 generative baselines (LCRec): https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S5.T1; related work: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S2.SS1.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: The scaling study measures training and evaluation losses as the model grows, not ranking metrics (Sec. 5.2, Fig. 1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Industrial generative recommenders that replace embedding tables with Semantic ID (SID) sequences are mostly proprietary (Abstract). The authors ask whether scaling laws hold on public benchmarks and which post-training recipe is enough for competitive performance.

> "Yet most industrial deployments remain proprietary, leaving two fundamental questions open: (1) Do the expected scaling laws hold on public benchmarks? (2) What is the minimal post-training recipe that enables competitive performance?" (Abstract)

MiniOneRec answers with an open framework that covers SID construction, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), and releases code, training pipelines, and checkpoints (Sec. 1).

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Titles and descriptions") --> B["Frozen text encoder"]
    B --> C["RQ-VAE"]
    C --> D("SIDs added to vocabulary")
    D --> E["SFT"]
    E --> F["GRPO"]:::key
    L1{{"Next-item + alignment tasks"}} -.-> E
    L1 -.-> F
    L2{{"Correctness + ranking reward"}} -.-> F
    F --> G["Constrained beam"]
    G --> H("Next item")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Item Tokenization

A frozen text encoder embeds item titles and descriptions, and an RQ-VAE quantizes the embedding into a hierarchical SID (Sec. 3.2).

> "The codebooks, the encoder and the decoder are trained jointly, while the text encoder remains frozen." (Sec. 3.2)

#### Full-Process SID Alignment

The SID tokens are added to the LLM vocabulary. Next-item prediction and auxiliary alignment tasks, such as mapping between titles and SIDs, are optimized jointly in both the SFT stage and the RL stage (Sec. 3.3, Sec. 6).

#### Reinforced Preference Optimization

The RL stage uses GRPO with constrained beam search as the sampler, so every generated item is valid (Sec. 3.4.1). The default reward combines a binary correctness rule with a ranking term that penalizes hard negatives (Sec. 3.4.2).

> "The mixed reward discussed combines binary correctness with a soft ranking term, helping the LLM tell hard negatives apart." (Sec. 3.4.2)

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Scaling: training and evaluation losses decrease as the Qwen backbone grows from 0.5B to 7B parameters (Abstract, Sec. 5.2).
- Alignment: the variant that keeps SID alignment through the whole pipeline scores highest on every metric among the alignment variants (Sec. 5.5.1, Fig. 4a).
- Cross-domain: a model trained only on Industrial is applied to the unseen Office domain without further tuning (Sec. 5.4, Table 2).
- World knowledge: the paper compares pre-trained and randomly initialized backbones (Sec. 5.6, Table 3).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- LC-Rec also aligns a `Dec-Only` LLM to `RQ-VAE` SIDs with auxiliary tasks (`Multi-task NTP`); MiniOneRec keeps such tasks in a following RL stage (`NTP → RL`).
- OneRec builds SIDs from multimodal and collaborative signals (`MM+CF`) with `R-KM`; MiniOneRec uses text only (`Text`) with `RQ-VAE`.

## MME-SID

- Page: pages/papers/mme-sid.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: MM-RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: MME-SID feeds an LLM multimodal embeddings together with Semantic ID embeddings from MM-RQ-VAE, trained with maximum mean discrepancy and contrastive alignment, to reduce embedding collapse and forgetting.
- [Code](https://github.com/Applied-Machine-Learning-Lab/MME-SID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2014 5-core: Beauty (22,332 users / 12,086 items), Toys and Games (19,121 / 11,757), Sports and Outdoors (35,092 / 18,090); items lacking a title or image are removed. Positives are ratings above 3.
  - Source: 5-core Amazon 2014 and item removal: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#A2.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Per user, the N-th (last) item is the test target and the (N-1)-th item the training target; a validation split is not reported. Results averaged over 3 runs.
  - Source: Last and second-last item as test and training targets: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; three runs: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); items are scored by dot products between the LLM output and multimodal item embeddings, with HR and nDCG at 5, 10, 20.
  - Source: Scores over target item embeddings: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.SS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. A frequency-aware fusion module reweights modalities by each item's training-set frequency.
  - Source: Standard split; frequency-aware fusion for cold versus warm items without an unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.SS3.p3.
- **SID**: Separate collaborative, textual, and visual SIDs from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codes (300 for Sports), used as LLM input embeddings alongside projected modality embeddings. The paper states that MME-SID does not need to tackle collisions because multimodal data discriminate between items; no resolution rule is described.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 (300 for Sports) per modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#A1.T4; no collision handling needed by design: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.I1.i2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: No autoregressive decoding: one forward pass of Llama3-8B-instruct, then scoring against item embeddings. All experiments on A100 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Scoring instead of autoregressive decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 3 (Beauty, Toys, Sports versus ID, multimodal, and SID-based baselines; t-tests); Figure 3 (embedding collapse and SR performance); Appendix Table 4 (hyperparameters).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3; collapse analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.SS3.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER-MM generates per-modality RQ-VAE semantic IDs autoregressively and must resolve collisions; MME-SID feeds multimodal SIDs and embeddings to an LLM and scores items directly.; where: MME-SID v1, baseline TIGER-MM: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.I2.i7.p1; collision contrast: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S4.I1.i2.p1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3.
- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER regularizes the tokenizer for generative retrieval on a TIGER backbone; MME-SID avoids generation and aligns modalities with an MMD loss.; where: MME-SID v1, baseline LETTER implemented on TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.I2.i9.p1; Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S5.T3.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec aligns an LLM to item indices but decodes autoregressively; MME-SID scores items from the LLM output for lower latency.; where: MME-SID v1, Section 6.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.02017v1#S6.SS2.p1.

## MMGRec

- Page: pages/papers/mmgrec.md
- Venue: TOMM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: Graph RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MMGRec assigns each item a Rec-ID with Graph RQ-VAE over multimodal and collaborative features and trains a Transformer with relation-aware self-attention to generate it, instead of embed-and-retrieve.
- [Code](https://github.com/hanliu95/MMGRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: MovieLens, TikTok, Kwai multimodal recommendation benchmarks; filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p2
- **Split**: Per-user random interaction split: 80% training, 10% validation, 10% test; non-sequential CF, without temporal labels.
  - Source: Sections 5.1-5.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS2.p2

  - Source: Sections 4.4 and 5.1 specify generated top-K lists but no full-catalog/sampled evaluation declaration: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Graph RQ-VAE uses user-item interactions; test-interaction exposure in graph construction: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2.1 and 5.1 define no unseen-item evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3
- **SID**: Graph RQ-VAE: 3 semantic tokens plus popularity-rank collision suffix. Codebooks tuned over 64/128/256; Kwai analysis favors 128; selected per-dataset sizes not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2.2, 5.3 and 6.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.SS5.p4
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam width K, default K=10. Figure 5 plots approximately 60-125 ms/user across 1/16-to-full Kwai. Hardware, inference batch size and timing scope: not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.4-4.5, Section 6.4 and Figure 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S4.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F5
- **Results from**: This paper's experiments using public baseline implementations: Table 2 main; Tables 3-5 ablations; Figures 4-6 hyperparameters, inference efficiency, Rec-ID design. TIGER is explicitly excluded from the benchmark.
  - Source: Tables 2-5, Figures 4-6 and baseline implementation statement: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S6.F5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16555v4#S5.SS2.p2

## MMQ

- Page: pages/papers/mmq.md
- Venue: WSDM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: MoE-VQ; Backbone: HeterRec; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: MTP; Inference: –
- TL;DR: MMQ trains a multimodal tokenizer with modality-shared and modality-specific experts under orthogonal regularization, then fine-tunes its Semantic IDs on behavior objectives with a multimodal reconstruction loss.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty; retrieval uses user/item 5-core filtering and histories capped at 20. Southeast Asian advertising logs, October 2024-May 2025 (30M users, 40M ads); industrial filters not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3
- **Split**: Beauty ranking: chronological 90% train/10% test; ratings >3 positive, <=3 negative. Retrieval and industrial offline splits not reported. Online A/B: July 6-August 6, 2025; treatment 10% random user traffic.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.1 and 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S5.p1

  - Source: Section 4.1.1/4.1.2 gives labels and metrics, not retrieval candidates: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Section 4.1 defines no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: 6 positions: 2 shared, 2 text-specific, 2 visual-specific; codebook size 100 (Beauty), 3000 (industrial). Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2
- **Inference budget**: Retrieval K=5/10 using HeterRec; ranking uses PPNet. Decoding budget, hardware, inference batch size, and latency not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/4.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1

  - Source: Table 1 and Section 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.15281v1#S5.p1

## MQL4GRec

- Page: pages/papers/mql4grec.md
- Venue: ICLR’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Dual RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: MQL4GRec translates item text and images from several domains into a shared quantitative language and pre-trains generation tasks over it, to transfer recommendation knowledge across domains and modalities.
- [Code](https://github.com/zhaijianyang/MQL4GRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 (May 1996-October 2018). Pre-training on six categories (Pet, Cell, Automotive, Tools, Toys, Sports); target tasks on Instruments (17,112 users / 6,250 items), Arts (22,171 / 9,416), Games (42,259 / 13,839). Users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are filtered; sequences capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Pre-training and target categories: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.p1; filtering and length: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A1.T6.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out (allocation not restated beyond the label). Separate zero-shot study: models pre-trained on source categories are tested on the targets without fine-tuning.
  - Source: Leave-one-out named only: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; zero-shot study: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS5.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full ranking over the entire item set instead of sample-based evaluation).
  - Source: Full ranking over the entire item set: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Zero-shot: target-domain items are unseen by the pre-trained generator; whether the RQ-VAE translators saw them: not reported.
  - Source: Standard split; zero-shot uses target-domain items absent from pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS5.p1.
- **SID**: Separate text (LLaMA) and image (ViT-L/14) quantitative languages from RQ-VAEs with 4 levels x 256 codewords (dimension 32). Colliding items have tokens reassigned by the distances between their residuals and code vectors, instead of an appended identifier.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32 per modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A3.p1; distance-based reassignment for collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 20 in each modality; the two recommendation lists are re-ranked so items in both rank higher. T5 encoder-decoder with 4 layers each. Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 20 and dual-list re-ranking: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1; T5 backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#A3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Instruments, Arts, Games versus sequential, multimodal, and generative baselines); Table 2 (collision handling versus TIGER's appended index); Tables 3-4 (generation tasks and pre-training); Figures 3-4 (pre-training data and epochs); Table 5 (zero-shot).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1; collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T2; tasks and pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T4; zero-shot: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T5.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER uses one text modality and an appended index for collisions; MQL4GRec translates text and images into separate quantitative languages and reassigns colliding tokens by distance.; where: MQL4GRec v1, Table 1 baseline TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T1; collision comparison in Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S4.T2.

(2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2504.05314v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.

- id: macrec; relation: successor; note: MACRec later reuses MQL4GRec's collision reassignment and dual-modality ensemble and adds cross-modal contrastive alignment during quantization.; where: Evidence is from the later MACRec paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx1.SSSx3.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx3.SSx2.SSSx3.p3; MQL4GRec is its main baseline in Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.15122v2#Sx4.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: With both modalities, pre-training does not improve results on Games, and zero-shot ability on the target domains is weak (Sec. 4.3, Sec. 4.5).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Generative recommenders that build on pre-trained language models carry general linguistic knowledge that does not match recommendation needs, and they rarely use the complementary knowledge in item text and images (Abstract). MQL4GRec turns the content of items from many domains and modalities into one discrete vocabulary, so that a generator trained on source domains can transfer to a target domain.

> "Our key idea is to transform items from different domains and modalities into a unified language, which can serve as a bridge for transferring recommendation knowledge." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Text via LLaMA") --> C["Text translator RQ-VAE"]
    B("Image via ViT") --> D["Image translator RQ-VAE"]
    C --> E("Prefixed quantitative language")
    D --> E
    E --> F["Source pre-training: next-item tasks"]
    F --> G["Target fine-tuning: all tasks"]:::key
    G --> H("Text list + image list")
    H --> I["Re-rank by item scores"]
    I --> J("Next item")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Quantitative Translators

A frozen modal encoder, LLaMA for text or ViT for images, encodes item content (Sec. 3.1). An RQ-VAE per modality quantizes the representation, and each modality has its own codebooks.

> "We train a quantitative translator for each modality, then add prefixes to the codewords from each of the two codebooks to form a dictionary." (Sec. 3.1)

#### Generation Tasks

Next-item generation predicts the next item's quantitative language in the same modality. Asymmetric item generation predicts the image language from a text history, or the reverse (Sec. 3.2). Quantitative language alignment tasks map an item's text language to its image language and back.

#### Pre-Training and Fine-Tuning

Pre-training on the source domains uses only the two next-item generation sub-tasks. Fine-tuning on the target domain uses all generation tasks (Sec. 3.3).

At inference, the generator returns one recommendation list per modality, and a re-ranking step merges the two lists by their item scores (Sec. 3.3, Eq. 7).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: MQL4GRec performs best in most cases across Instruments, Arts, and Games, especially on NDCG (Sec. 4.2, Table 1).
- Pre-training: with both modalities, pre-training improves results on Instruments and Arts but not on Games.

  > "Under dual modalities, pre-training significantly improves performance on the Instruments and Arts datasets; however, it does not yield a notable improvement for the Games dataset, potentially due to overfitting." (Sec. 4.3)

- Zero-shot: pre-trained models without fine-tuning show preliminary but weak zero-shot ability on Instruments and Arts, and none on Games (Sec. 4.5, Table 5).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The two quantizers are trained separately (`Dual RQ`), so the text and image codes are linked only by the generation tasks. MACRec replaces them with `Cross RQ`, which adds cross-modal contrastive learning inside quantization.
- TIGER quantizes text only (`Text`); MQL4GRec adds images (`Text+Img`) and keeps the same `Enc-Dec` generator with `Beam` decoding.

## MSCGRec

- Page: pages/papers/mscgrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE+DINO; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP; Inference: Trie/C-Beam
- TL;DR: MSCGRec quantizes images with self-supervised DINO-based learning, adds collaborative features as a separate modality, and restricts training outputs to permissible tokens, to scale generative recommendation to large catalogs.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023 Beauty and Personal Care (724,796 users / 203,843 items), Sports and Outdoors (408,287 / 151,632), and PixelRec (8,886,078 / 407,082). 5-core filtering of users and items; for Amazon, samples with empty or placeholder images are removed and items with identical images are merged into one ID; sequences capped at 20 items.
  - Source: Datasets and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T1.
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out into training, validation, and test; for Amazon every item in a training sequence is a separate target, for PixelRec only the last item.
  - Source: Chronological leave-one-out and target construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from constrained beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The collaborative modality uses SASRec item embeddings trained on the interaction data.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol; SASRec embeddings as the collaborative modality: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **SID**: Per-modality residual quantizers (image via DINO self-supervised quantization, LLAMA text, SASRec collaborative) with 3 levels x 256 entries each, applied directly in embedding space; an extra collision level per modality makes each item's code unique (TIGER style). The collaborative codes serve as generation targets.
  - Source: 3 levels x 256 per modality plus a collision level: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS1.p2; DINO-based image quantization: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam search with 20 beams; T5 encoder-decoder; training and evaluation on four NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Constrained beam search with 20 beams and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p3; constrained training softmax: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S3.SS3.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Beauty, Sports, PixelRec versus sequential and generative baselines); Table 3 (component ablations, modality Shapley values, image-only).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T2; ablations and Shapley values: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03713v1#S4.T3.

## MuSID-KD

- Page: pages/papers/musid-kd.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-MLP; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: MuSID-KD distills a generative teacher into lightweight students by aligning candidate distributions at successive Semantic ID prefix levels and weighting supervision by ranking impact, instead of uniform alignment.
- [Code](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/m7k2-review-83f9/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty/Toys, Amazon Reviews 2023 Video Games, and Steam-100K; histories capped at 20. Filtering rules not reported.
  - Source: Section 6.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Chronological leave-one-out; exact validation/test allocation not reported. Checkpoints selected by validation NDCG@10.
  - Source: Section 6.1 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p3
- **Candidates**: Evaluation: not reported. The 64 teacher candidates per request are training support, not sampled evaluation negatives.
  - Source: Section 6.1 separates evaluation from training candidates: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Frozen teacher encoder/token embeddings/mapping shared with students; additional distillation caches use training requests only. Teacher/tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections 6.1/B.1 define no item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p3
- **SID**: Main RQ-VAE: 4 positions x 256 codes; frozen and shared teacher/student mapping. R-KMeans additionally tested. Unique SIDs assumed; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Sections 6.1/6.2 and Appendix B.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S3.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 50; K=5/10; student batch 32 (teacher throughput batch 64). MuSID-KD MLP/GRU/CNN: 3036/3423/3024 requests/s; GRU/CNN serving totals 0.292/0.331 ms/request. Hardware not reported.
  - Source: Section 6.1/6.5 and Appendix B.3/Table B1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.SS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A2.T6
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: Amazon, mean over seeds 42-44; Table S1: Steam; Figure 6: R-KMeans. KD baselines adapted to shared teacher/students/decoding; TIGER is a teacher reference, excluded from student comparisons.
  - Source: Table 1, Figure 6 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#S6.F6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35218v1#A1.T3

## NAU

- Page: pages/papers/nau.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: –; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec†; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: –
- TL;DR: NAU adds explicit control over the probability mass on forgotten items' Semantic ID neighborhoods to interaction-level unlearning, because shared tokens let unlearning degrade neighboring items.
- [Code](https://github.com/pierre-lubitzsch/neighborhood-aware-unlearning)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports, Toys using released five-core preprocessing. Table 24 additionally lists Food k5 SID diagnostics; its source and preprocessing details not reported.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix H Table 24: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A8.T24
- **Split**: Chronological train/validation/test; allocation sizes not reported. Training histories capped at 20 items; all unlearning methods start from the same original model.
  - Source: Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; no items are filtered from generated candidates during unlearning evaluation.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Users, items and SIDs remain fixed during NAU.
  - Source: Sections 2/4 study interaction deletion with existing items, without an unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4
- **SID**: RQ-KMeans/RQ-VAE diagnostics: 3 semantic levels plus fourth deduplication level. Codebook sizes not reported; Table 24 shows 256 occupied first-level RQ-KMeans codes. LETTER and TRACER-compatible tokenizers also evaluated; their sizes not reported.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix H Table 24: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A8.T24
- **Inference budget**: Top-10 utility/exposure metrics; beam width, inference hardware, inference batch size and recommendation latency not reported. One H200 and NAU's 3.9s measure unlearning per request, not recommendation inference.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix D Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A4.T9
- **Results from**: Original Tables 1/3/4: spam/unwanted-item removal; Appendices D/F: extended results. Five data seeds. RQ-KMeans selection uses validation; other-tokenizer operating-point selection uses test results.
  - Source: Section 5 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#S5.p9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.27232v1#A4.p1

## NEO

- Page: pages/papers/neo.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text / Audio; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: NEO adapts a decoder-only LLM to interleave natural language and typed item Semantic IDs in one sequence, with constrained decoding, to unify search, recommendation, and reasoning without tools.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial media logs: >10M episodes, shows, audiobooks and artists; about 15M users; 5M grounding examples, 10M instruction-training examples, 100K test examples. Filtering not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Global temporal protocol: context through t, labels at t+k, evaluation at t+2k; k=1 day for episodes/shows, 7 days for audiobooks. Baselines share train/test windows; dates and validation allocation not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; NEO and baselines use the same candidate universe.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5 specifies a common candidate universe but not full-catalog versus sampled evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. User cold-start simulated by removing listening history and retaining user metadata.
  - Source: Section 4.1.5 and its cold-user experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.Px1.p1
- **SID**: Separate residual K-Means vocabularies by type: 4 x 256 for audiobooks/episodes/shows, 4 x 1024 for artists. Each collision bucket resolves to one popularity-selected item.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2
- **Inference budget**: Trie-constrained beam 30; HR/NDCG@10/30. Top-p alternative: temperature 0.6, top-k 20, top-p 0.95. Inference hardware, batch size and absolute latency not reported; Table 3 latency@10 decreases 2.92% without constraints and 7.91% with sampling.
  - Source: Section 4.2.1 and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.Px5.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.T3
- **Results from**: Original Tables 5/8/9: production-baseline comparisons, cold/warm users and search breakdowns. Recommendation baseline is GNN/two-tower; search baseline dense retrieval. NEO uses about half the production baseline's historical logs.
  - Source: Original Tables 5/8/9 and Sections 4.1.1/4.2.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#A2.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#A2.T9 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS1.SSS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17533v1#S4.SS2.SSS3.Px1.p1

- Page: pages/papers/netflix-sid-comparison.md

MTP throughput is 75% higher on 8B.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S3.SS3 ; #S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 1-2: controlled single-head versus MTP quality/system comparison. Tables 3-4: SID recipe versus previous non-SID auxiliary-head baseline; Tables 5-7: ablations. Proprietary scores/costs reported relatively; no imported baseline result table identified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.15864v1#S4.T1 ; #S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.SS2.p1

## NEZHA

## OneLoc

(2025), OneRec arXiv:2502.18965, for unified generation and preference alignment: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S6.SS2.p1; Section 2 describes OneLoc's geographic modules and rewards: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.14646v1#S2.p1.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: In a one-week online A/B test on 10% of traffic, OneLoc reports GMV +21.016% and order volume +17.891% against the production multi-stage pipeline (Sec. 5, Table 4).
Limitation: Location enters the SID only through one fused embedding before residual k-means, so no SID position is tied to geography (Sec. 2.2).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

In Kuaishou's local-life service, each recommended video is linked to a store location, so a recommendation must match both the user's interest and the user's real-time location (Abstract). The authors state that end-to-end generative recommenders such as OneRec had not yet been built for this setting (Abstract).

> "The first challenge is how to make full use of geographic information. The second challenge is how to balance multiple objectives, including user interests, the distance between user and stores, and some other business objectives." (Abstract)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Video + location") --> B["Multimodal LLM"]
    B --> C["Residual k-means"]
    C --> D("Geo-aware SID")
    D --> E["GA-Attn encoder"]:::key
    E --> F["Decoder with neighbor-aware prompt"]:::key
    L1{{"NTP loss"}} -.-> F
    L2{{"DPO on geo + GMV rewards"}} -.-> F
    F --> G("Next video")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Step 1: Geo-Aware Semantic IDs

Each video $`v`$ is assigned a location $`l`$. The location is a GeoHash block with context information such as coordinates, brand, and category (Sec. 2.1). OneLoc follows OneRec and builds SIDs with residual k-means. The input to the first level is one embedding that a multimodal large language model extracts from the video content and the location context.

> "To inject geographic information, each residual $`r^{0}_{i}`$ in the initial residual set $`\mathcal{R}^{0}`$ is represented as an embedding of video content and location context information, extracted by a multimodal large language model." (Sec. 2.2)

At each level $`i`$, k-means on the residuals builds the codebook, and each residual moves to its nearest centroid (Eq. 1–3):

```math
\mathcal{C}^{i} = \mathrm{KMeans}(\mathcal{R}^{i}, N_c), \qquad q^{i}_{j} = \arg\min_{k} \left\| c^{i}_{k} - r^{i}_{j} \right\|, \qquad r^{i+1}_{j} = r^{i}_{j} - c^{i}_{q^{i}_{j}}
```

where:
- $`\mathcal{R}^{i}`$ is the set of residuals at level $`i`$, and $`r^{i}_{j}`$ is the residual of item $`j`$;
- $`\mathcal{C}^{i} = \{c^{i}_{k}\}`$ is the level-$`i`$ codebook of $`N_c`$ centroids;
- $`q^{i}_{j}`$ is the $`i`$-th token of the SID of item $`j`$.

#### Step 2: Geo-Aware Self-Attention in the Encoder

The encoder reads the user's watch, click, and purchase sequences (Eq. 4). Each behavior $`i`$ has a fused embedding $`z_i`$, built by an MLP from its video ID, location ID, and location context embeddings, and a location context embedding $`e^{lc}_i`$ (Eq. 5–7).

> "GA-Attn module is proposed to capture relevant behaviors from the user's interaction history according to the user's real-time location." (Sec. 2.3.3)

GA-Attn adds a location context similarity to the attention scores (Eq. 11–12), then scales each output row with a gate computed from the user's real-time location (Eq. 13–14):

```math
A = \mathrm{Softmax}\left( (Z W_q)(Z W_k)^{\top} / \sqrt{d} + E^{lc} (E^{lc})^{\top} \right), \qquad \widetilde{O} = A (Z W_v) W_o
```

```math
g_i = 2 \cdot \mathrm{Sigmoid}\left( \mathrm{MLP}\left( \mathrm{Concat}(e^{lc}_u, E^{lc}_{i*}) \right) \right), \qquad O_{i*} = g_i\, \widetilde{O}_{i*}
```

where:
- $`Z`$ is the sequence of fused behavior embeddings $`z_i`$, and $`E^{lc}`$ is the sequence of location context embeddings;
- $`W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o`$ are the query, key, value, and output matrices;
- $`e^{lc}_u`$ is the context embedding of the user's real-time location $`l_u`$;
- $`g_i \in (0, 2)`$ scales the $`i`$-th output row.

Each encoder block applies GA-Attn and a feed-forward network, both with RMSNorm and residual connections (Eq. 8–10).

#### Step 3: Neighbor-Aware Prompt and Next-Token Prediction

The decoder starts from a prompt that summarizes the area around the user.

> "In local life service, it is vital to model location contexts surrounding the user, such as surrounding brands, bestselling products, etc. Thus, we use cross-attention to capture the surrounding information." (Sec. 2.4.1)

OneLoc takes the context embeddings of the 8 locations around $`l_u`$ as $`E^{s}`$ and computes one prompt embedding $`e^{s} = \mathrm{CrossAttn}(e^{lc}_u, E^{s})`$, with $`e^{lc}_u`$ as the query (Eq. 15). The decoder input is $`H^{0} = \{e^{s}, e_{q^1_t}, e_{q^2_t}, e_{q^3_t}\}`$ (Eq. 19). Each decoder block has causal self-attention, cross-attention to the encoder output, and a feed-forward network (Eq. 16–18). The output at the prompt predicts the first SID token, the output at the first token predicts the second, and so on:

```math
\hat{y}^{j} = \mathrm{Softmax}\left( \mathrm{MLP}(H^{K}_{j-1}) \right) \in \mathbb{R}^{N_c}, \qquad \mathcal{L}_{ntp} = \sum_{j=1}^{3} -\log \hat{y}^{j}_{q^{j}_{t}}
```

where $`H^{K}_{j-1}`$ is the last-layer decoder output at position $`j-1`$, and $`q^{j}_{t}`$ is the $`j`$-th token of the target SID (Eq. 20–21, Sec. 2.4.2).

#### Step 4: Geographic and GMV Rewards with DPO

Next-token prediction only fits the videos that the previous system exposed (Sec. 2.5). OneLoc therefore defines two rewards. The geographic reward is the inverse distance within a threshold (Eq. 22), and the GMV reward is the output of a GMV scoring model (Eq. 23):

```math
R^{geo}(v, l_u) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \mathrm{Dis}(v, l_u) \gt D, \\ 1 / \mathrm{Dis}(v, l_u) & \text{otherwise}, \end{cases} \qquad R^{gmv}(v, S, l_u) = \mathrm{GMV}(v, S, l_u)
```

> "The geographic reward signal is proposed to encourage generating videos nearby and thus a closer video would get a higher reward" (Sec. 2.5.1)

For each training sample, the pre-trained model generates $`N`$ videos by beam search (Eq. 24). OneLoc computes both rewards for each video and pairs the video with the highest reward (positive) and the one with the lowest reward (negative) (Sec. 2.5.2). A new model $`\theta_{i+1}`$, initialized from $`\theta_i`$, is trained on these pairs together with next-token prediction:

```math
\mathcal{L}_{dpo} = -\log \sigma\left( \beta \log \frac{p_{\theta_{i+1}}(Q_p \mid S, l_u)}{p_{\theta_{i}}(Q_p \mid S, l_u)} - \beta \log \frac{p_{\theta_{i+1}}(Q_n \mid S, l_u)}{p_{\theta_{i}}(Q_n \mid S, l_u)} \right), \qquad \mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{ntp} + \lambda \mathcal{L}_{dpo}
```

where:
- $`Q_p`$ and $`Q_n`$ are the SIDs of the positive and negative videos;
- the previous iterate $`\theta_i`$ serves as the reference model;
- $`\sigma`$ is the sigmoid function, and $`\lambda = 0.05`$ (Sec. 4.1.4).

Eq. 25 in v1 is printed without $`\sigma`$; the form above follows standard DPO.

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

def ga_attn(Z, E_lc, e_u, Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo, gate_mlp):
    """
    Z:        [T, d] fused behavior embeddings z_i (Eq. 6)
    E_lc:     [T, d] location context embeddings of the behaviors (Eq. 7)
    e_u:      [d]    context embedding of the user's real-time location
    gate_mlp: maps [T, 2d] -> [T, 1]
    """
    d = Z.size(-1)
    A = torch.softmax((Z @ Wq) @ (Z @ Wk).T / d ** 0.5 + E_lc @ E_lc.T, dim=-1)        # Eq. 11, [T, T]
    O = A @ (Z @ Wv) @ Wo                                                               # Eq. 12, [T, d]
    g = 2 * torch.sigmoid(gate_mlp(torch.cat([e_u.expand_as(E_lc), E_lc], dim=-1)))     # Eq. 13, [T, 1]
    return g * O                                                                        # Eq. 14

def oneloc_loss(ntp_loss, logp_new_pos, logp_old_pos, logp_new_neg, logp_old_neg, beta, lam=0.05):
    """Sequence log-probabilities of the positive and negative SIDs; old = previous iterate theta_i."""
    margin = beta * ((logp_new_pos - logp_old_pos) - (logp_new_neg - logp_old_neg))
    return ntp_loss + lam * (-F.logsigmoid(margin).mean())                             # Eq. 25-26
```

Simplifications: The code shows one attention head and leaves out RMSNorm, the feed-forward network, and the residual connections of each block. It takes the projection matrices, the gate MLP, and the log-probabilities as inputs, and it does not build preference pairs or run beam search.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M("Model θi") --> B["Beam search: N videos"]
    B --> R["Geo + GMV rewards"]
    R --> P("Highest = positive, lowest = negative")
    P --> L{{"L = NTP + 0.05 DPO"}}:::key
    L --> N("Model θi+1, reference θi")
    N -->|next round| M
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Foursquare: OneLoc outperforms the baselines in Table 1, which include TIGER and GNPR-SID, on the NYC and Tokyo subsets (Table 1).

  > "Similarly, on the Foursquare global dataset, it attains an average performance boost of 13.18% in Recall@5 and 16.34% in NDCG@5." (Sec. 4.2)

- Online A/B test: OneLoc reports GMV +21.016%, order volume +17.891%, and new local-service buyers +23.027%, with p < 0.01 under two-tailed t-tests (Sec. 5, Table 4).

  > "In this experiment, 10% of the traffic was allocated to the treatment group using the end-to-end OneLoc system, while the control group retained the production-level multi-stage recommendation pipeline" (Sec. 5)

- Ablations: the study covers the neighbor-aware prompt, geo-aware self-attention, and the two rewards (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 4, Table 3, Fig. 5). It measures Recall and NDCG, and adds GMV for the rewards. The authors report lower scores for every ablated variant than for the full model.

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.** The conclusion names two directions for future work: scaling laws of model size and sequence length, and RL methods adapted to local-life services (Sec. 7).

**Our analysis.**

- OneLoc mixes location into the input (`Text+Img+Geo†`). LGSID instead uses geographic indexing with residual quantization (`Geo-Idx+RQ`), and LGRID uses `DSRQ`, so their SID positions carry geography directly. GeoGR adds geographic and collaborative signals to text (`Text+Geo+CF`).
- KuaiLLSR, the GMV scoring model, and the online test all come from Kuaishou, so only the Foursquare results can be reproduced from public data (Sec. 4.1.1, Sec. 5).

## OneMall

- Page: pages/papers/onemall.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: R-KM+FSQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: (NTP + Ctr.) → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneMall unifies product-card, short-video, and live-streaming e-commerce in one generator, with a business-aware tokenizer, Query-Former and sparse MoE layers, and a ranking model as reinforcement learning reward.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou product-card, short-video, and live-streaming logs; dates/sample counts not reported. Tokenizer: 70M product-product pairs (<=40 occurrences/item), 12M video-product pairs from long views 1-5 minutes before product clicks, excluding News/Comedy/Dance/Film-TV/Selfie videos and downsampling frequent products/same-user pairs.
  - Source: Sections 3.1.1 and 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.p1

- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Frozen codebooks can tokenize new uploads; encoder/tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.2/4 define no unseen-item evaluation protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S2.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4
- **SID**: Two Res-Kmeans levels plus a 4096-code FSQ final level; residual-only baseline uses 3x4096. Final variant's residual codebook sizes not separately stated. FSQ reduces collisions; residual collision resolution not reported.

- **Inference budget**: Deployed 0.5B-total/0.1B-active model; HR@50/100/500. Serving beam width, hardware, inference batch size, latency not reported; beam 768 is RL training candidate generation.
  - Source: Sections 4/4.2/4.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21770v1#S4.SS4.p1

## OneRec

- Page: pages/papers/onerec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: MM+CF; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Sess. Beam
- TL;DR: OneRec replaces the retrieve-and-rank cascade with one encoder-decoder generator using sparse MoE, generates whole sessions of videos, and aligns preferences by iterative DPO with a reward model.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou short-video interaction logs; training sessions are built from high-quality user sessions (a session is 5-10 videos per request; the listed criteria include at least 5 videos actually watched, total watch time above a threshold whose value is not given, and interactions such as liking, collecting, or sharing). Dataset size: not reported.
  - Source: Industrial Kuaishou data and session construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S4.p1; no dataset statistics found.
- **Split**: Offline: evaluation on a randomly sampled set of test cases in each iteration; the train/test construction is not reported. Online: A/B test on Kuaishou's main-page video scenarios with 1% of main traffic.
  - Source: Offline evaluation on randomly sampled test cases: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS5.p1.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking metrics: generated sessions are scored by a pre-trained reward model (session watch time, view, follow, and like probabilities), not ranked against a candidate set.
  - Source: Reward-model evaluation of generated sessions: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: 3 levels x 8,192 codes from multi-level balanced residual K-means over multimodal video embeddings aligned with user behavior; balanced K-means equalizes cluster sizes. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Balanced residual K-means, L=3 x K=8192: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with beam size 128 (also used to generate 128 responses per user for DPO); KV-cache decoding with float16 quantization; MoE with 24 experts, 2 active (about 13% of parameters active at inference). Training on NVIDIA A800 GPUs; serving hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 128 online and for DPO sampling; KV cache and float16: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (offline reward-model metrics versus pointwise, listwise, and preference-alignment baselines); Figure 4 (DPO sample ratio); Table 2 (online A/B: OneRec-1B+IPA +1.68% total watch time, +6.56% average view duration).
  - Source: Offline: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.T1; DPO ratio: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.F4; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.T2.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates one next item from RQ-VAE semantic IDs; OneRec generates whole sessions with balanced residual K-means IDs, an MoE encoder-decoder, and iterative DPO.; where: OneRec v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S5.I1.i4.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.T1; tokenizer contrast with RQ-VAE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18965v1#S3.SS1.p2.
- id: minionerec; relation: successor; note: MiniOneRec later reproduces the OneRec-style SID, SFT, and RL pipeline in open source on public data.; where: Evidence is from the later MiniOneRec paper, Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.24431v1#S1.p3.
- id: gflowgr; relation: alternative; note: GFlowGR later compares against OneRec's IPA alignment and replaces it with a GFlowNet objective over reward-weighted trajectories.; where: Evidence is from the later GFlowGR paper: IPA baseline and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.I2.i6.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.16114v3#S4.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: In the online test, OneRec improves watch time but is weaker on interaction indicators such as likes (Sec. 6).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Most recommenders run a retrieve-and-rank cascade, and a generative model, when present, only selects candidates in the retrieval stage (Abstract). The authors argue that each stage caps the stage after it.

> "existing methods typically treat each ranker independently, where the effectiveness of each isolated stage serves as the upper bound for the subsequent ranking stage, thereby limiting the performance of the overall ranking system." (Sec. 1)

OneRec replaces the cascade with a single-stage generative model and was deployed in the main scene of Kuaishou (Abstract, Sec. 1).

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Behavior history") --> B["Encoder"]
    B --> C["Session decoder"]:::key
    C --> D("Session list of SIDs")
    E["Balanced K-means"] --> F("SIDs") --> C
    D --> G["Beam samples"]
    G --> H["Reward model"]
    H --> L{{"DPO on best vs worst"}}
    L -.->|next round| C
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Balanced Semantic IDs

Each item receives a Semantic ID (SID) from balanced K-means, in which every cluster holds the same number of items (Sec. 3.1, Algorithm 1).

#### Session-Wise List Generation

Instead of predicting one next item, OneRec generates the list of items for a whole session and considers the content and order of items within it (Sec. 1). An encoder models the user's history, and a decoder generates the session list (Sec. 3.2).

> "The decoder takes the semantic IDs of the target session as input and generates the target in an auto-regressive manner." (Sec. 3.2)

#### Iterative Preference Alignment

A recommender shows each request only once, so true positive and negative lists for the same request are not available (Abstract). OneRec samples several responses with beam search, scores them with a pre-trained reward model, and pairs the highest-scoring and lowest-scoring responses for DPO (Sec. 3.3.2). The model then generates new samples in the next round.

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Session-wise generation: OneRec outperforms dot-product retrieval methods and point-wise generation such as TIGER on the reward-model metrics (Sec. 5.2, Table 1).
- Preference alignment: adding IPA further improves the generated sessions (Sec. 5.2, Table 1).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.**

> "Additionally, our analysis of online results reveals that, besides user watch time, our model has limitations in interactive indicators, such as likes." (Sec. 6)

**Our analysis.**

- The DPO pairs are ranked by the reward model, not by observed user feedback on both lists. This suggests that alignment quality is bounded by the reward model.
- MiniOneRec reproduces the pipeline on public data with `RQ-VAE` SIDs over text only (`Text`), a `Dec-Only` generator, and RL in place of DPO (`NTP → RL`).

## OneRec-Think

- Page: pages/papers/onerec-think.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text+Img+CF†; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT
- TL;DR: OneRec-Think adds explicit in-text reasoning to OneRec-style generation through item-text alignment, reasoning scaffolding, and a recommendation reward for multiple valid targets, instead of implicit prediction alone.
- [Code](https://github.com/wangshy31/OneRec-Think)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Toys, and Sports; users and items with fewer than 5 interactions are discarded. Industrial: Kuaishou short-video data with daily incremental training on about 20B tokens per day. Retained corpus sizes: not reported.
  - Source: Public datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2; filtering and split: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; industrial deployment: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.
- **Split**: Public: leave-one-out (allocation not restated beyond the label); training histories capped at 50 items. Online: one-week A/B test with a 1.29% traffic group.
  - Source: Leave-one-out and history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS2.Px1.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); top-K lists from beam search with width 10.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **SID**: Public: four-level hierarchical semantic IDs with 256 tokens per level (1,024 new tokens). Industrial: three levels x 8,192 itemic tokens (24,576 new tokens), plus item boundary tokens. The tokenizer algorithm is not restated; collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Public 4 levels x 256; industrial 3 levels x 8,192: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS1.p1; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: Public: beam search with width 10 after the reasoning text (Qwen3-1.7B). Industrial: Think-Ahead serving generates the reasoning and the first two itemic tokens offline with Qwen-8B, then a real-time OneRec model completes the last token online; latency numbers: not reported. Daily training on a cluster of 80 GPUs.
  - Source: Beam width 10 for public evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; Rollout-Beam reward with width K: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.SS3.p2; two-stage serving: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.SS4.p2; training cluster: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty, Toys, Sports versus sequential and generative baselines); Table 2 (alignment and reasoning ablation on Beauty); Table 3 (online A/B); Table 4 (user and video understanding BertScore).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.T1; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T3; understanding benchmarks: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.T4.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates the next itemic tokens directly; OneRec-Think first generates interleaved text-and-item reasoning and is rewarded with a beam-based signal.; where: OneRec-Think v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S5.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S4.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec aligns LLMs to item indices with auxiliary tasks; OneRec-Think adds itemic-textual alignment followed by reasoning activation and RL.; where: OneRec-Think v2, Section 3 and Appendix A.1 cite Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2510.11639v2#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1; not a baseline in Table 1.
- id: grlm; relation: alternative; note: GRLM later compares against OneRec-Think and replaces numeric itemic tokens with natural-language term IDs.; where: Evidence is from the later GRLM paper: LLM-based baselines and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S4.I1.i3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.06798v1#S5.T2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: In the online A/B test on Kuaishou, the Think-Ahead deployment increases App Stay Time by 0.159% against the online model (Sec. 5.4.2, Table 3).
Limitation: Multi-step reasoning conflicts with real-time latency requirements, so the full model runs only offline and a separate real-time OneRec model produces the last itemic token online (Sec. 4.4).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Generative recommenders such as OneRec predict item tokens directly and do not produce explicit, controllable reasoning (Abstract). OneRec-Think lets an LLM write a reasoning sequence and then the next itemic tokens in the same output.

> "In contrast, we reformulate this task to unify reasoning and recommendation in a single autoregressive pass." (Sec. 3)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Itemic alignment: token warm-up, four tasks"] --> B["Reasoning activation SFT"]
    B --> C["GRPO reasoning enhancement"]:::key
    L1{{"Rollout-Beam reward"}} -.-> C
    C --> D("Reasoning text")
    D --> E("Itemic tokens")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Itemic Alignment

Multi-task pre-training under next-token prediction teaches the LLM to read natural language and itemic tokens together (Sec. 4.1). The four tasks are interleaved user persona grounding, sequential preference modeling, itemic dense captioning, and general language modeling. A token warm-up substage first trains only the itemic token embeddings with the base LLM frozen, and then all parameters are trained jointly.

#### Reasoning Activation

Industrial behavior sequences are noisy. Supervised fine-tuning first extracts reasoning trajectories from pruned user contexts and then uses them to guide rationale generation over the raw behavior data (Sec. 4.2). The rationale and the target item are trained with a joint likelihood.

#### Reasoning Enhancement

RL with GRPO refines the reasoning paths (Sec. 4.3). After each sampled rationale, a constrained beam generates candidates, and the reward is the best position-wise match between a candidate and the target itemic tokens (Eq. 6).

> "To overcome this, we introduce the Rollout-Beam reward that evaluates reasoning capability by the model’s best achievable performance within a constrained beam." (Sec. 4.3)

#### Think-Ahead Serving

The full OneRec-Think model generates the reasoning path and the first two itemic tokens offline (Sec. 4.4).

> "It utilizes the pre-generated item-tokens as a constrained prefix to rapidly produce the final itemic token." (Sec. 4.4)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Offline as OneRec-Think, offline
    participant Online as Real-time OneRec, online
    Offline->>Offline: reasoning path + first two itemic tokens
    Offline->>Online: tokens as constrained prefix
    Online->>Online: final itemic token
```

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Public benchmarks: OneRec-Think performs best on Amazon Beauty, Toys, and Sports against the baselines in Table 1 (Sec. 5.2).
- Ablation: on Beauty, adding itemic alignment to the base model and then the reasoning mechanism both improve the recommendation metrics (Sec. 5.3, Table 2).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- OneRec uses an `Enc-Dec` generator trained with `NTP → DPO`; OneRec-Think uses a `Dec-Only` LLM trained with `NTP → RL` and generates reasoning before the item (`CoT`).
- The online gain comes from a split system in which a different model produces the last token. This suggests that the measured effect mixes the offline reasoning with the online model's own updates.

## OneRec-V2

- Page: pages/papers/onerec-v2.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img+CF†; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Lazy Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: OneRec-V2 replaces the OneRec encoder-decoder with a lazy decoder-only architecture that cuts sequence-encoding compute, and aligns with real user feedback through duration-aware reward shaping and adaptive ratio clipping.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou impressions, August 10-14 2025, for streaming architecture experiments; Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite feeds for online evaluation. Filtering and dataset sizes not reported.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1
- **Split**: Offline holdout allocation not reported. Online: one week, 5% experimental traffic; V2 serves 25% of degraded traffic within that group (Appendix D wording). Separate 1% group disables caching and serves V2 for every request.
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4 and Appendix D: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 2.3/4 describe training loss and online tests without candidate-enumeration protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold-start video-view metrics are reported, but subset criteria and tokenizer exposure are not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4/5 and Appendix D do not define a held-out unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.p2
- **SID**: 3 semantic tokens using the OneRec-V1 tokenizer; codebook sizes and collision handling not reported here.
  - Source: Section 2.2.2 Tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Online 1B model, context 3000, beam 512, L20 GPUs, latency 36ms, MFU 62%; inference batch size not reported.
  - Source: Section 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2-5: architecture/scaling; Tables 6-8: online alignment/deployment comparisons; Table 9: caching disabled. Online improvements are relative to OneRec-V1.
  - Source: Original Tables 2-8 and Appendix D Table 9: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S2.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S3.T6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#S3.T8 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20900v4#A4.T9

## PAD-Rec

- Page: pages/papers/pad-rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text+SID; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP†; Inference: Spec. Dec.
- TL;DR: PAD-Rec adds gated item-slot and draft-step position embeddings to the draft model of speculative decoding, instead of treating all Semantic ID draft tokens uniformly.
- [Code](https://github.com/Jiaju-Chen/PAD-Rec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty (12,101 items / 22,363 sequences), Instruments (9,922 / 24,772), Games (17,332 / 49,156), and Yelp (20,033 / 30,431). Users with fewer than 11 interactions are removed; each remaining user's 10 most recent items form the target list.
  - Source: Datasets and statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T1; preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.
- **Split**: User-level 8:1:1 split into training, validation, and test, so all interactions of a user fall in one partition; targets are each user's 10 most recent items.
  - Source: User-level 8:1:1 split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.
- **Candidates**: n/a for candidate ranking: the model generates a 10-item list that is compared with the user's 10 most recent items (Recall@10, NDCG@10).
  - Source: List-wise recall against the 10-item ground-truth list: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.I4.i3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.I4.i4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Test users are held out from training (user-level split), while items are shared across splits.
  - Source: Test users are disjoint from training users; items are shared: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE semantic IDs over embeddings that integrate semantic and collaborative signals (following LETTER), with separator tokens between items; codebook size and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: K=4 RQ-VAE codebooks following LETTER, separators between items: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S3.SS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.
- **Inference budget**: EAGLE-2-style tree speculative decoding with speculation depth 6 and tree width 10, at temperature 0 and 0.5; target LLM Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (3B and 8B in scaling). Latency measured on NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs in fp16 with batch size 1 after three warm-up runs; Table 3 lists naive target-LLM latency (e.g. Beauty 693.55 at temp 0, units as in the table).
  - Source: Tree-based speculative decoding settings and timing protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p3; baseline latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T3.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (wall-clock speedup, accepted length, Recall@10, NDCG@10 versus EAGLE-2, HASS, FSPAD, GRIFFIN on four datasets); Table 3 (naive decoding latency); later tables and figures (ablations, model scaling, hyperparameters).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T2; latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.27747v1#S5.T3; ablations and hyperparameters in Section 5.

### Related

## PCR-CA

- Page: pages/papers/pcr-ca.md

- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: PC-AE; Backbone: Disc.; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: PCR-CA learns parallel codebook representations of app text, unlike hierarchical RQ-VAE, and aligns them contrastively with collaborative signals for CTR prediction on multiple-category apps.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Microsoft Store impression logs with click/install labels over several months; approximately 80K apps, click rate 6.148%; histories up to 50 interactions. Filtering rules not reported.

- **SID**: PC-AE: 4 parallel codebooks x 32 entries, 16-dimensional vectors, selecting/summing two nearest codes per book. Codebooks train jointly with CTR prediction after pretraining. Unique-ID collision resolution: n/a; codes supply predictive features.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S3.SS2.p3 ; #S3.SS2.p7 ; #S4.SS1.p2
- **Inference budget**: Discriminative scoring; beam n/a; top-10 lists for diversity. Simulated throughput: 120K candidate items/s versus base 150K/s on the same unspecified server. Inference hardware, batch size and request latency not reported; offline text embedding costs 22 ms/new app.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18166v1#S4.SS4.p2 ; #S4.SS4.p3 ; #S4.SS4.p4
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: AUC by app-popularity bucket; Tables 3-4: ablations; Table 5: online A/B. SaviorRec is explicitly reimplemented; no baseline-result reuse stated.

## Pctx

- Page: pages/papers/pctx.md
- Venue: CIKM’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam+Agg.
- TL;DR: Pctx tokenizes each item with the user's interaction history as context, so the same item can receive different Semantic IDs for different users, instead of one static item-only mapping.
- [Code](https://github.com/YoungZ365/Pctx)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023: Musical Instruments, Industrial & Scientific, Video Games; exclude users/items with fewer than five interactions; chronological histories capped at 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 ; #A3.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: most recent item test, penultimate validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS3.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog; full-ranking evaluation rather than negative sampling.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#A3.SS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Auxiliary DuoRec is pretrained on the same training data, and representative contexts come from training interactions; textual-tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS2.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS1.Px1.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; #A3.SS3.p1
- **SID**: 3 x 256 residual semantic codes plus an auxiliary collision token of unreported vocabulary size; multiple context-conditioned SIDs/item. Same-item IDs differing only in collision token are merged; collision tokens distinguish different items. Main text names RQ-VAE; appendix specifies FAISS quantization.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS2.SSS2.Px1.p1 ; #S2.SS2.SSS2.Px2.p2 ; #A3.SS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beam decoding with aggregation of generated SID probabilities per item; Recall/NDCG@5/10. GR baseline beam 50; Pctx-specific beam width not separately reported. Inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1 ; #A3.SS3.p1 ; #S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1
- **Results from**: Table 1: Pctx experiments with most baseline rows (including TIGER/LETTER) copied from Zheng et al. (2025); other baselines reconstructed. Table 2: ablations; Table 3: ensemble comparisons; Table 6: explainability.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.21276v1#S3.T1 ; #S3.T2 ; #S3.T3 ; #A3.SS4.p1 ; #A4.T6

### Related

## PinGER

- Page: pages/papers/pinger.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: V. Efficiency
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: –; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Div. C-Beam
- TL;DR: PinGER interleaves Semantic ID and dense tokens with an asymmetric attention mask so serving uses one token per item, and steers retrieval by goal conditioning, reinforcement learning, and diversity penalties.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Pinterest session-centric UniPinRec data: historical cross-surface actions paired with target-surface session engagements; session sampling reflects traffic. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Split**: Evaluation uses held-out users in a later, non-overlapping window disjoint from training. Window dates, allocation ratios and validation split: not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Candidates**: full catalog: generated identifiers resolve against the full production corpus.
  - Source: Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Users are held out; fresh-content analysis uses Pins created within 28 days, without specified generator/tokenizer item holdouts.
  - Source: Section 5.1 and online fresh-content analysis: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS1.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE 5x2048; content-only PinCLIP input, OmniSage engagement distillation. Index resolves shared-SID item lists; insufficient leaves fall back to coarser prefixes, with round-robin interleaving across beams.
  - Source: Sections 3.2 and 4.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S3.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.SS3.p2
- **Inference budget**: Offline beam100, Recall@10/100. Online Related Pins beam60/penalty3; notifications beam100/penalty1. Serving L40S at ~200QPS/host: e2e p50/p99 51/77ms (beam60),54/81ms (beam100); batch not reported. Attention microbenchmark: A10G,batch4,history1018.
  - Source: Sections 5.1/5.3, Table 1 and Figure 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.SS3.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.F5

  - Source: Tables 1-4 and Appendix Tables 5-8: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#A1.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.33435v1#A1.T8

## PLUM

- Page: pages/papers/plum.md
- Venue: WWW’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam

## PrefixMem

- Page: pages/papers/prefixmem.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: MM; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PrefixMem gives an LLM a pre-trainable Semantic ID encoder built from prefix n-gram memory tables, so each token gets a prefix-conditioned representation instead of a plain vocabulary embedding.

- Relations: 3

- **SID**: RQ-VAE on PinCLIP multimodal embeddings: 5 levels x 2048 codes. Collisions acknowledged; full-SID recall matches codes without resolving item collisions.
