## ProGEO

- Page: pages/papers/progeo.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: R-KM+Geo-CB; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam+Geo-Filter
- TL;DR: ProGEO builds a proximity-aware geo-codebook with a geo-centroid local coordinate system and geo-rotary position encoding, so Semantic IDs model semantics and geography jointly.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Industrial: two months of transaction records from a Chinese local-life service platform (search query, user location, merchant exposure sequence, interactions); size and filtering not reported. Public: Foursquare NYC (1,083 users / 5,135 POIs) and TKY (2,293 / 7,873), filtered as in GNPR-SID (POIs with fewer than 10 interactions, users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed), and Yelp (150,346 POIs; clustering analysis only).
  - Source: Industrial and public data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1; public statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.
- **Split**: Industrial: two months of records for training and additional daily data reserved for validation; the test construction is not reported. Public: preprocessing follows GNPR-SID; the split is not restated.
  - Source: Two-month training with extra daily validation data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1; public split follows GNPR-SID but is not restated.
- **Candidates**: Industrial inference: for each generated semantic ID, the 10 POIs closest to the user's location form the candidate set, with beam width 20. Evaluation reports Hit@1, Hit@50, Hit@100 and NDCG@50, @100; full catalog versus sampled not otherwise stated.
  - Source: Ten location-nearest POIs per semantic ID as candidates, then beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS3.p3.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Residual quantization with geographic rotary encoding (Geo-RoPE) at the third layer over 128-dimensional Qwen3-Embedding-8B text embeddings. Codebooks: [512, 512, 512] industrial; [32, 32, 32] NYC/TKY; [64, 64, 64] Yelp. Conflicts: industrial uses closest-location matching among POIs sharing a SID (best in Table 3); public datasets use a TIGER-style fourth-layer code because user location is unavailable.
  - Source: Codebooks [512,512,512] industrial, [32,32,32] NYC/TKY, [64,64,64] Yelp, Geo-RoPE at layer 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1; conflict strategies: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T3.
- **Inference budget**: Beam search with width 20 on Qwen2.5-1.5B; all experiments on 8 GPUs with 80GB memory. Inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam width 20 and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.SS2.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (industrial quantization and recommendation metrics versus RQ-VAE, RQ-Kmeans, HyMiRec-style RQ-Kmeans, RQ-OPQ); Table 2 (geographic attributes); Table 3 (conflict-resolution strategies); Table 6 (public datasets versus RQ-Kmeans); Figures 7-10 (sensitivity and case studies).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T1; geographic attributes: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T2; conflicts: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.T3; public: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#A2.T6; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S4.F7.

(2025): https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S2.SS1.p2.
- id: lgsid; relation: alternative; note: LGSID aligns LLM embeddings with geographic rewards before quantization; Pro-GEO encodes geography within the quantization layers.; where: Pro-GEO v1, Section 2.1 cites LGSID: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.23156v1#S2.SS1.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On the industrial dataset, ProGEO reports Hit@50 of 0.4243 against 0.4056 for RQ-Kmeans, and an average geographic clustering distance of 25.41 km against 46.71 km for RQ-OPQ (Table 1).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Local service platforms need recommendations that are relevant and also geographically reachable (Abstract). Semantic codebooks cluster items by content alone.

> "existing semantic codebooks neglect geographic constraints, often resulting in recommendations that are semantically relevant yet geographically unreachable." (Abstract)

ProGEO keeps standard semantic codewords and adds a geo-codeword that encodes each POI's position relative to its semantic cluster, so geography becomes part of the Semantic ID (SID) instead of a weak auxiliary feature (Abstract, Sec. 1).

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("POI features") --> B["Layer 1-2: cosine clustering"]
    B --> C("Two-layer SID subset")
    C --> D["Geographic centroid, polar coordinates"]
    D --> E["Geo-RoPE rotation of layer-2 residual"]:::key
    E --> F("Geo-codeword")
    F --> G("Three-token SID")
    G --> H["Fine-tuned LLM"]
    H --> I("Nearby POIs")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Semantic Layers

The first two codebook layers cluster mixed feature vectors with cosine similarity as the metric and pass projection residuals to the next layer (Sec. 3.1). The SID has two standard codebook layers and one geo-codebook layer (Fig. 2).

#### Geo-Centroid Local Coordinates

POIs that share the same two-layer SID form a subset. The actual latitudes and longitudes of these POIs define a geographic centroid, and each POI's global position becomes polar coordinates around it (Sec. 1, Sec. 3.2).

#### Geo-RoPE

Geo-RoPE encodes each POI's offset from the centroid as complex-valued rotations of the residual from the second layer (Sec. 1, Sec. 3.3). The similarity between two rotated vectors then depends on both their semantic factors and their spatial relation.

> "We extend RoPE to the spatial domain, formalizing geographic proximity as rotary operations in high-dimensional feature space." (Sec. 3.3)

#### Generation

In the industrial setting, the LLM prompt contains the search query, the city, and a GeoHash of the user's location (Table 4).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Geo-RoPE layer: applying Geo-RoPE only at the third clustering layer gives the highest CUR (7.67%) and ICR (57.08%) among the tested placements (Sec. 4.3.2, Fig. 5).
- Case study: with Geo-RoPE, the recommended POIs lie close to the user, while the variant without it returns a POI in another city (Sec. 4.5.2).

  > "when Geo-RoPE is introduced, the recommended POIs are concentrated much closer to the user, typically within a 6-kilometer radius." (Sec. 4.5.2)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- The geographic signal enters only the third SID token. This suggests that the generator still chooses the semantic cluster before it uses any spatial information.
- OneLoc uses plain `R-KM` codes; ProGEO adds a geo-codebook layer to the same kind of tokenizer (`R-KM+Geo-CB`).
- GNPR-SID also encodes geography in POI SIDs (`Attr+Geo+CF`) but uses a plain `RQ-VAE`, without a dedicated geo-codebook layer.

## PROMISE

- Page: pages/papers/promise.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Inference
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: PRM-Beam
- TL;DR: PROMISE adds a lightweight process reward model that scores intermediate Semantic ID steps and prunes beam branches with it, to correct early-token semantic drift and scale with inference compute.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Public: Amazon Beauty and Sports and Outdoors (May 1996-July 2014), following TIGER's preprocessing (users with fewer than 5 reviews removed). Industrial: Kuaishou online-learning logs (over 400 million daily active users, about 50 billion interactions per day, more than 100 million items).
  - Source: Public datasets and TIGER protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial logs: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2.
- **Split**: Public: chronological leave-one-out (last item for test, second-to-last for validation, rest for training). Industrial: online learning on real logs; the offline test construction is not reported. Online: 7-day A/B test on Kuaishou and Kuaishou Lite, with 5% of users (about 20 million) in the experimental group and another 5% in the control group for each app.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial online learning: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2; online A/B groups and length: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); public Recall/NDCG at 5 and 10, industrial at 100, 500, 1000 from beam search.
  - Source: Metrics only: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Public: 3-level RQ-VAE x 256 codes. Industrial: residual K-means over multimodal representations, depth 3 x 8,192 codes. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Public 3 x 256 RQ-VAE: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; industrial residual K-means d=3, M=8192: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS1.p2; no collision rule found.
- **Inference budget**: PRM-guided beam search: expand to K+ candidate paths per step, score them with a lightweight path-level PRM, and keep K'. Industrial: K=K'=1000 with K+ of 4,000 or 6,000; 4 encoder and 4 decoder blocks plus 1 PRM block. Public beam settings, hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: PRM-guided beam: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S3.SS3.p3; industrial K=K'=1000 and K+ in {4000, 6000}: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS2.SSS3.p1; public beam settings not found.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty and Sports; baseline numbers taken from the original papers or identical settings); Table 2 (Kuaishou offline versus six deployed retrievers); Table 3 (online A/B); Table 4 (PRM step ablation with hierarchical recall); Figure 4 (test-time scaling of K+).
  - Source: Public: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T1; industrial: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T2; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T4; test-time scaling: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS5.p1.

### Related

- id: actionpiece; relation: competitor; note: ActionPiece is the strongest public baseline; it changes tokenization, whereas Promise keeps RQ-VAE SIDs and adds a process reward model to steer beam search.; where: Promise v1, generative baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.I2.i3.p1; Table 1 and Section 4.1.5: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04674v1#S4.SS1.SSS5.p2.

## PSI

- Page: pages/papers/psi.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Post-hoc RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: PSI assigns unique, semantic-preserving IDs by relaxing nearest-centroid selection with exhaustive candidate matching or recursive residual searching, instead of appending a non-semantic token to resolve conflicts.
- [Code](https://github.com/wangshanyw/PurelySemanticIndexing)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Sequential recommendation on Amazon Beauty (12,101 items / 22,363 users), Sports (18,357 / 35,598), and Toys (11,924 items), keeping users and items with at least 5 interactions, following LMIndexer. Also Amazon Product Search (same domains) and document retrieval on NQ320k and MS MARCO-1M.
  - Source: Recommendation data and LMIndexer protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p2; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T2; search and retrieval data: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx3.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T3.
- **Split**: Recommendation: per-user leave-one-out (last for test, second-to-last for validation, rest for training). Product search: the original train/test split. A cold-start test subset keeps targets that appear at most 0 or 1 time in training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p2; cold-start subset: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled evaluation candidates); generation over valid semantic IDs.
  - Source: Metrics and protocol follow LMIndexer; candidate set not restated: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Cold-start subset: targets appearing at most once in training, including items never seen by the generator; whether the RQ-VAE or clustering indexer was fit with these items: not reported.
  - Source: Cold-start subset with items that appear 0 or 1 time: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2; the indexer embeds all items including test-only ones.
- **SID**: Purely semantic IDs: conflicts are removed by assigning non-nearest centroids instead of appending a conflict token, via exhaustive candidate matching (ECM, global scoring of top-k combinations) or recursive residual search (RRS, greedy). Applied to RQ-VAE and hierarchical clustering indexers. The level study on Amazon product search compares three-level purely semantic IDs with two levels plus a conflict index (codebook size 256); the conflict-proportion study uses codebook sizes 512, 256, and 192. Levels and codebook sizes for the main tables: not reported.
  - Source: ECM and RRS conflict-free assignment over RQ-VAE or hierarchical clustering: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx1.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx3.SSx3.p1; codebook size 256 in the level study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx7.SSSx1.p1; codebook sizes 512, 256, 192 in the conflict-proportion study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx9.p1.
- **Inference budget**: T5-base generator initialized from the same checkpoint for all indexers; decoding method and beam width: not reported. All experiments on 2 NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: T5-base, hardware, training batch: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx2.p3; decoding settings not found.
- **Results from**: Table 5 (sequential recommendation on Beauty, Sports, Toys with RQ-VAE and HC indexers, 3 trials); Table 6 (product search); document-retrieval tables; Table 9 (candidate ranking ablation); Figure 5 (cold-start subset).
  - Source: Recommendation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T5; search: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T6; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T9; cold start: Figure 5 via https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p2.

### Related

- id: lmindexer; relation: predecessor; note: PSID follows LMIndexer's tasks, datasets, and setup, and replaces conflict tokens with conflict-free semantic assignment.; where: PSID v1, Section 4.1 follows Jin et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx1.p1; dataset tables: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.T3.
- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER appends a non-semantic conflict token to colliding IDs and uses a heuristic quota for cold-start items; PSID reassigns colliding items to non-nearest centroids so IDs stay fully semantic.; where: PSID v1, Section 1 on fallback tokens: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx1.p2; cold-start discussion citing Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p1.
- id: liger; relation: alternative; note: LIGER adds dense retrieval to recover cold-start items; PSID improves cold-start generation by removing unpredictable conflict tokens.; where: PSID v1, Section 4.10 cites Yang et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16446v1#Sx4.SSx10.p1.
- id: latte; relation: successor; note: Latte later uses PSID as its base model and its ESM conflict resolution, and adds latent prefix tokens.; where: Evidence is from the later Latte paper: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#S5.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.06331v1#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.

## PSRQ

- Page: pages/papers/psrq.md
- Venue: CIKM’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: Prog. RQ; Backbone: Encoder; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: PSRQ generates modality-specific and modality-joint Semantic IDs that preserve prefix semantic features and models music interests with multi-codebook cross-attention, to reduce semantic drift in residual quantization.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Baby (81,423 users / 33,652 items; ratings of 4 or more are positives), an industrial music-streaming dataset from one week of logs (4,926,656 users / 1,387,247 songs; collections are positives, played-but-not-collected are negatives), and Music4all (14,127 users / 99,596 songs; repeated plays are positives). Items with fewer than 30 interactions are marked cold-start. Further filtering: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and labels: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i3.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: not reported (sequences are built by timestamp and trained for one epoch, but the train/test division is not described). Online: A/B test in February 2025 on the music platform against a DLRM ranker.
  - Source: Timestamp-ordered sequences, no split rule: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.I2.i1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1; online test: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking candidates: evaluation is pointwise AUC and Logloss on labeled positive and negative samples; how negatives relate to user history is defined by the labels above.
  - Source: Pointwise AUC on labeled samples: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. 'Cold AUC' covers items with fewer than 30 interactions, which are low-frequency, not unseen.
  - Source: Cold-start = fewer than 30 interactions, not unseen: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.
- **SID**: Progressive Semantic Residual Quantization (PSRQ): layer-wise K-means over modality embeddings (text, image or audio) that preserves the prefix semantic feature, producing modal-specific and modal-joint semantic IDs; clusters per layer k = 64 (Amazon Baby), 256 (Industrial), 128 (Music4all), 3 layers. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Clusters k and layers l per dataset: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1; PSRQ name and modal-specific/modal-joint IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#abstract1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S4.SS1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: n/a for generation (SIDs feed a DIN-style ranker with cross-attention, MCCA). MLLM feature extractors run on NVIDIA A100 GPUs; ranker inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Discriminative ranker, hardware for feature extraction: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS1.SSS2.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (All AUC, Cold AUC, Logloss versus multimodal and quantization-based rankers); Table 3 (quantizers added to DIN with text only); Table 4 (MCCA ablation); Section 5.3 (online A/B: collect +2.81%, full play +0.95%).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T2; quantizers in DIN: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T4; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.SS3.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER introduced RQ-VAE semantic IDs for generative retrieval; PSRQ quantizes multimodal embeddings with progressive semantic residual K-means and uses the IDs as ranking features for cold-start items.; where: PSRQ v1, Section 1 and Section 2.2 cite Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1; RQ-VAE is a quantizer baseline in Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S5.T3.
- id: vq-rec; relation: alternative; note: VQ-Rec framed vector quantization for transferable recommenders; PSRQ adds modal-specific and modal-joint codebooks for multimodal cold-start ranking.; where: PSRQ v1, Section 1 and Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec uses residual K-means SIDs inside an end-to-end generator; PSRQ keeps a discriminative ranker and feeds it multimodal SID embeddings.; where: PSRQ v1, contribution list and Section 2.2 cite OneRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S1.I1.i2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2508.20359v1#S2.SS2.p1.

## Q-BERT4Rec

- Page: pages/papers/q-bert4rec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Img+CF; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Encoder (Non-AR); Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Masked; Inference: Non-AR
- TL;DR: Q-BERT4Rec fuses text, image, and structural features into item embeddings, quantizes them into Semantic ID tokens by residual vector quantization, and pre-trains a bidirectional encoder with several masking strategies.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018: pre-training on six source domains (Pet, Cell, Automotive, Tools, Toys, Sports) and fine-tuning on Musical Instruments, Arts Crafts and Sewing, Video Games (same statistics table as MQL4GRec). Filtering rules: not restated.
  - Source: Source and target domains: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p3; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out: most recent interaction for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **Candidates**: not reported explicitly; at inference the masked last position is filled with the most probable semantic ID over the item set (HR and NDCG at 1, 5, 10).
  - Source: Argmax over item semantic IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS6.p2; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Standard split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p4.
- **SID**: 4-level RQ-VAE x 256 codewords (dimension 32) over LLaMA text and CLIP-ViT image features fused by a cross-modal semantic injection module. Collisions are resolved by MQL4GRec's distance-based token reallocation.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32, MQL4GRec reallocation for collisions: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS4.p7.
- **Inference budget**: Bidirectional masked prediction of the last position (no beam search); 4-layer Transformer encoder. NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs (four for pre-training, one for fine-tuning). Table 6 reports per-sample inference latency of about 2.66-2.67 ms with under 6M parameters.
  - Source: Masked prediction at inference: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS6.p2; hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS1.p8; latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A2.T6.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (Instruments, Arts, Games versus traditional, Transformer, multimodal, prompt-LLM, and semantic-ID baselines); Tables 3-4 (modalities and pre-training strategies); Figures 3-5 (layers, mask ratio, dropout); Table 6 (complexity and latency).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.T4; sensitivity: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S4.SS4.p1; complexity: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A2.T6.

### Related

- id: mql4grec; relation: competitor; note: MQL4GRec generates multimodal quantitative language autoregressively; Q-BERT4Rec reuses its collision reallocation but fuses modalities before quantization and predicts masked SIDs bidirectionally.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, collision handling follows Zhai et al. (2025): https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.SS4.p7; Table 2 baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER decodes SIDs left to right with an encoder-decoder; Q-BERT4Rec uses a BERT-style encoder with multi-mask pre-training.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 semantic-ID baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; Appendix A baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A1.I5.i1.p1.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec uses product-quantized text codes for transfer; Q-BERT4Rec quantizes fused text-image features with RQ-VAE and pre-trains on six source domains.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 VQ/multimodal baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-CID uses collaborative IDs in a prompt-based LLM; Q-BERT4Rec uses multimodal semantic IDs in a small masked Transformer.; where: Q-BERT4Rec v2, Table 2 prompt-LLM baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#S3.T2; Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02474v2#A1.I4.i1.p1.

## QT-Mob

- Page: pages/papers/qt-mob.md
- Venue: KDD’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: QT-Mob tokenizes locations into compact semantic tokens and fine-tunes an LLM with complementary objectives that align the tokens with its representations, for next-location prediction and mobility recovery.
- [Code](https://github.com/shadowfall09/QT-Mob)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 1

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC/SG, April 2012-February 2013; Singapore cellular trajectories, November 2022, using 400m grids. Remove locations with <5 visits; group records into 24h trajectories and discard trajectories with <3 records.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user chronological trajectories: first 70% train, next 10% validation, last 20% test.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; the unseen-location experiment follows LLM-Move's zero-shot ranking setting without detailing its candidate pool.
  - Source: Section 5.1 and Appendix D.4 do not specify catalog enumeration or candidate sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.SS4.p1
- **Visibility**: Unseen-location probe: sample 100 test locations and remove all training trajectories containing them. Unseen by generator; whether unseen by tokenizer too: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix D.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.SS4.p1
- **SID**: 4 RQ-VAE levels x 256 codes, code dimension 32; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 15; Hit/NDCG@1/5/10. Inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported; four V100 GPUs are specified for training.
  - Source: Sections 5.1.3/5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/3: next-location prediction/mobility recovery; Table 10: unseen locations. Five-run averages; compared baselines use their papers' default parameter settings.
  - Source: Section 5.1.3/5.1.4 and Tables 2/3/10: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#A4.T10

### Related

- id: lc-rec; relation: predecessor; note: Its cited RQ-VAE tokenization approach informs QT-Mob's hierarchical location tokens.; where: QT-Mob v1, Section 4.2, citing Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S4.SS2.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11109v1#S4.SS2.p4.

## QuaSID

- Page: pages/papers/quasid.md
- Venue: KDD’26 ADS
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: QA-RQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam†
- TL;DR: QuaSID repels only qualified conflicting Semantic ID pairs with Hamming-scaled margins, masks benign overlaps, and adds a dual-tower contrastive objective, instead of treating all collisions equally.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2018 Beauty and Toys & Games, user/item 5-core; Kuaishou e-commerce industrial logs with multimodal item features.
  - Source: Section 5.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Public: leave-one-out train/validation/test, exact held-out positions not reported. Online A/B: 5 days, about 5% randomized treatment traffic covering >20M users.
  - Source: Sections 5.1.1/5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS4.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Sections 5.1.3/5.1.4 and Appendix A.2 do not specify candidate enumeration or sampling: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#A1.SS2
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Industrial cold-start subsets have <100 or <600 video views within the first 48h; strict generator/tokenizer unseen status not reported.
  - Source: Section 5.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS4.p1
- **SID**: Public: 3 x 256; industrial: 4 x 1024. HaMR repels qualified full/partial collisions; additional inference-time collision resolution not reported.
  - Source: Sections 4.2/5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.SS2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1
- **Inference budget**: Offline HitRate/NDCG@5/10; beam width, inference hardware, serving batch size and latency not reported. Appendix A.2 batches 256/1024 concern SID learning.
  - Source: Section 5.1.3 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#A1.SS2
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: matched-TIGER tokenizer comparison, five-seed means; Table 3: HaMR added to baselines; Table 4: online retrieval/ranking and low-view subsets.
  - Source: Tables 2/3/4 and Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: Supplies the shared downstream backbone for tokenizer comparisons.; where: QuaSID v1, Section 5.1.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S5.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- id: letter; relation: alternative; note: Assignment balancing contrasts with QuaSID's qualified, severity-scaled collision repulsion.; where: QuaSID v1, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00632v1#S2.SS2.p2.

## R3-VAE

- Page: pages/papers/r3-vae.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Ref.-RQ; Backbone: –; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: R3-VAE stabilizes residual quantization with a reference vector as semantic anchor and a dot-product rating mechanism, and uses two Semantic ID quality metrics as training regularizers.
- [Code](https://github.com/wwqq/R3-VAE)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Public: Amazon Beauty, Sports, Toys, Clothing, plus LastFM and ML1M. Industrial: Toutiao interaction logs. Filtering rules and corpus sizes: not reported in the body.
  - Source: Public datasets: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1; industrial Toutiao data: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.p1; no filtering rules or statistics found in the body.
- **Split**: not reported for the public datasets. Industrial: offline MRR plus online A/B tests for both the generative (OneRec framework) and CTR settings; test periods and traffic not reported.
  - Source: No split rule found; online tests: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Recall and NDCG at 10, 20, 30 on the generated top-K sequence; industrial generative MRR and CTR UAUC.
  - Source: Generated top-K sequences: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. The online CTR test reports cold-start click volume for existing and new users without defining item visibility.
  - Source: Online cold-start click volume for new users, no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS3.p1.
- **SID**: Reference-vector-guided residual quantization VAE: inputs are projected on a learned reference vector, each layer assigns soft top-K weights over codewords, and the SID takes the top-weighted index per layer; a metric loss maximizes semantic cohesion and preference discrimination. Industrial: 3 levels x 8,192. Public: the Beauty sensitivity study fixes L=3 and K=256; codebook sizes for the other public runs: not reported. Collision handling: not reported (collision rates are measured, e.g. Table 6).
  - Source: Reference-vector projection and weighted rating residual quantization: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS3.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS5.SSS1.p1; industrial codebooks 8192^3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; Beauty sensitivity study with L=3, K=256 fixed: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS6.SSS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Industrial generative setting follows OneRec: beam search generating 512 responses for DPO, on 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. CTR setting: SIDs replace item-ID embeddings in DIN, SIM, RankMixer (batch 2,048). Public decoding settings, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: OneRec framework with beam 512 responses and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; CTR setting: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS4.SSS1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Beauty, Sports, Toys) and Table 2 (LastFM, ML1M, Clothing) with SC/PD metrics; Table 3 (industrial generative MRR and online A/B); Tables 4-5 (CTR UAUC and online A/B); Table 6 (Beauty SID quality including collision rate and Gini).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T5, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T6.

### Related

- id: onerec; relation: competitor; note: OneRec's residual K-means is the main industrial baseline and the generation framework; R3-VAE adds a reference-vector projection, rating-weighted residual quantization, and SID-quality regularization.; where: R3-VAE v3, baselines and OneRec framework: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1; Tables 1, 3, 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4.
- id: tokenrec; relation: competitor; note: TokenRec's masked vector-quantized tokenizer (MQ) is a baseline; R3-VAE differs by reference-guided soft residual assignment.; where: R3-VAE v3, baseline MQ [26]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Tables 1 and 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4.
- id: vq-rec; relation: competitor; note: VQ-Rec's OPQ-style codes appear as the OPQ-KMeans baseline; R3-VAE uses residual rather than product quantization.; where: R3-VAE v3, baseline OPQ-KMeans [5, 7]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1.
- id: forge; relation: alternative; note: FORGE proposes Embedding HitRate and Gini to evaluate SIDs without full training; R3-VAE proposes semantic cohesion and preference discrimination for the same purpose.; where: R3-VAE v3, Section 3.4 draws on FORGE [4]: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.SS4.p1; Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S1.p3.

## RAGR

- Page: pages/papers/ragr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: Beam† / –
- TL;DR: RAGR interleaves item Semantic IDs and review Semantic IDs chronologically in the user sequence and uses DPO to favor item tokens at prediction positions, instead of modeling item-only sequences.
- [Code](https://github.com/Zhang-Yingyi/TKDE_RAGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games, with historical review text; remove users/items with fewer than five interactions; maximum history 20, truncating oldest interactions.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p3
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last interaction test, second last validation, remaining interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Experimental settings report top-K metrics but no candidate universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Historical reviews are retained; tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; #S4.SS4.p4
- **SID**: RQ-VAE: 4 x 256, 32-dimensional codewords, shared item/review token space. Default tokenizer fits item text only; collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p2 ; #S4.SS4.p4 ; #S4.SS5.p4
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive item-SID prediction; HIT/NDCG@5/10/20. Decoding algorithm/beam width, inference batch size and latency not reported. General experiment server: 8 RTX PRO 6000 96GB GPUs; inference-specific allocation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p5
- **Results from**: Original Table II: TIGER/LETTER with and without RAGR, means over seeds 42/43/44; all baselines trained/evaluated with the common split/protocol. Table III: ablations; Tables IV-V: tokenizer efficiency/collisions. No baseline-result reuse stated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 ; #S4.SS1.SSS4.p5

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: RAGR augments TIGER with interleaved review SIDs, review-generation supervision and DPO alignment toward item generation.; where: RAGR v1, Section IV-A and Table II: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2.
- id: letter; relation: predecessor; note: LETTER is the second backbone receiving the same review augmentation and item-centric DPO alignment.; where: RAGR v1, Section IV-A and Table II: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2605.17267v1#S4.T2.

## RecBase

- Page: pages/papers/recbase.md
- Venue: EMNLP’25
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Curr. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: RecBase pretrains a domain-agnostic foundation model on a cross-domain corpus with a unified tokenizer of hierarchical concept identifiers, for zero-shot recommendation instead of language-centric pretraining.
- [Code](https://github.com/reczoo/RecBase)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Pre-training on 15 datasets and testing on 8 unseen datasets from RecBench (MIND, MovieLens, MicroLens, Goodreads, Yelp, Steam, H&M, HotelRec as test sets). Totals: training 4,595,003 items / 35,047,682 users; fine-tuning 1,005,745 / 5,098,084; test 623,615 / 145,975. Length-based filtering: users with fewer than 15 interactions are removed (e.g. AmazonToys) and histories over 2,500 interactions are truncated (e.g. LastFM, PixelRec); thresholds for the other datasets: not reported.
  - Source: RecBench and dataset roles: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T2; length filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Split**: Dataset-level: pre-train on training datasets and evaluate zero-shot on held-out datasets; a fine-tuning study adds in-domain data for five test datasets. Within-dataset split rules: not reported.
  - Source: Dataset-level split between pre-training and zero-shot test: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1; fine-tuning study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T3.
- **Candidates**: n/a for ranking candidates: user-item pairs are scored and evaluated by AUC (RecBench protocol); how negative pairs are formed is not restated.
  - Source: User-item pair scoring with AUC: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p3.
- **Visibility**: Zero-shot: test datasets and their items are unseen by the generator; whether the CL-VAE tokenizer was trained on test-dataset items: not reported. Fine-tuned setting: warm.
  - Source: Test datasets are unseen in pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p3.
- **SID**: Concept IDs from a curriculum-learning RQ-VAE (CL-VAE) with 4 levels x 2,048 codes over NV-Embed-v2 text embeddings, with codebook reinitialization against collapse. Collisions are measured as a conflict rate (Figure 2) but a resolution rule is not reported.
  - Source: CL-VAE with 4 levels x 2048 over NV-Embed-v2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS2.p1; curriculum and reinitialization: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S3.SS2.p2; conflict rate study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.SS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Scores items from the logits over concept IDs (no beam search described); Qwen2-style decoder (Base: 24 layers, hidden 1,024; Large: 28 layers, hidden 1,536; vocabulary 20,000). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Logit-based ranking of concept IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS1.p2; model sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.SS2.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (zero-shot AUC on 8 datasets versus P5, RecGPT, and LLM baselines); Table 3 (zero-shot versus fine-tuned); Table 4 (ablations of CL-VAE components); Figure 2 (codebook size and levels).
  - Source: Zero-shot: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S3.T1; fine-tuning: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S4.T3; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.T4; codebook study: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S5.SS2.p1.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER builds RQ-VAE semantic IDs per dataset for next-item generation; RecBase pre-trains a recommendation foundation model over concept IDs shared across many domains.; where: RecBase v1, Section 2.2 cites Rajput et al. (2023): https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec adapts an existing LLM to one domain's item indices; RecBase pre-trains from scratch on recommendation corpora for zero-shot transfer.; where: RecBase v1, Section 2.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2509.03131v1#S2.SS2.p1.

## RecoChain

- Page: pages/papers/recochain.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Hybrid
- TL;DR: RecoChain generates candidates by hierarchical Semantic ID prediction and then ranks them with SIM-based click estimation in the same Transformer, to close the gap between generation and ranking.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: TAOBAO-MM: 8.79M users, 35.4M items, 99M interactions, histories up to 1,000 interactions, with 128-dimensional multimodal item embeddings; adapted from CTR to sequential recommendation by keeping interaction histories and discarding exposure labels. Further filtering: not reported.
  - Source: TAOBAO-MM and adaptation: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **Split**: The official TAOBAO-MM train/validation/test split, without further sequence-level partitioning.
  - Source: Official split: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); top-K comes from C beam candidates (beam size 20 by default) that are re-ranked by a click-probability head.
  - Source: Beam candidates re-ranked; metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: Official split with no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-Kmeans over the pretrained multimodal embeddings, plus a random fourth token s4 that makes the item-SID mapping one-to-one; codebook size per level: not reported.
  - Source: 3-level RQ-Kmeans plus a random fourth token: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Hierarchical beam search (default beam 20; 10 to 40 in Table 1) with KV cache, then for each candidate the top-10 most similar history items are appended and a rank head scores the candidate by continuing decoding. 2-layer decoder (hidden 1,024). Hardware, inference batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Generate-retrieve-rerank with KV reuse: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS3.SSS2.p4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.SS4.p2; defaults: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p4; model: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S3.p2.
- **Results from**: Tables 1-3 (Recall and NDCG at 5 and 10 before and after re-ranking, varying beam size, input sequence length, and retrieval length on TAOBAO-MM).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S2.T3.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: alternative; note: TIGER stops at beam-search retrieval; RecoChain appends retrieved history items to each beam candidate and re-ranks them in the same decoder.; where: RecoChain v1, Section 1 cites TIGER and OneRec as beam-search retrievers: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p4.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec unifies retrieval and ranking with preference alignment over sessions; RecoChain chains generation and a click-probability re-rank head with KV-cache reuse.; where: RecoChain v1, Section 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.25787v1#S1.p4.

## REGER

- Page: pages/papers/reger.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → (NTP + Aux.); Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: REGER pretrains a generator to produce semantic neighbors' Semantic IDs, combines global and ID-boundary local attention, and distills a discriminative teacher's next-token distributions along the target prefix path.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014 Beauty/Sports/Toys and 2023 Instruments/Scientific/Games; 5-core filtering and maximum history 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #A1.T6
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: latest interaction test, second latest validation, all earlier interactions training.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Evaluation settings give metrics and seeds but no evaluation universe: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1 ; #A1.SS1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. GSR semantic neighbors are drawn from the item catalog; tokenizer and frozen DuoRec teacher exposure to test items/interactions not explicitly separated.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p3 ; #S4.SS3.SSS2.p1 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE on Sentence-T5 embeddings reduced to 128 dimensions by PCA/whitening; semantic level count and codebook sizes not reported in paper. Extra token distinguishes identical semantic codes; suffix vocabulary size/assignment not reported. Dataset-specific SID mapping shared across recommender seeds.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S3.SS1.p1 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Unconstrained beam 20 for validation/test, without teacher; teacher ablation uses beam 50. Recall/NDCG@5/10. Table 4 efficiency probe on TIGER+HCPD: one L40, FP32, test batch 256, KV cache off, 16 s for full Beauty test set. REGER-specific absolute inference time and general inference batch/hardware not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#A1.SS3.p2 ; #A1.SS3.p4 ; #A1.T7 ; #S5.T4 ; #S5.SS4.p3
- **Results from**: Table 1: 2014 comparisons with reproduced baselines, three seeds 2024/2025/2026; Table 2: training objectives on TIGER; Table 3: REGER ablations. Table 6: 2023 results, with published baseline rows from Latte, OMEGA, DECOR and TopoTok papers.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.T1 ; #S5.T2 ; #S5.T3 ; #A1.T6 ; #A1.SS3.p2

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: REGER uses residual-quantized SID generation and additionally tests its HCPD training objective directly on TIGER.; where: REGER v1, Section 3.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S3.SS1.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: gflowgr; relation: competitor; note: GFlowGR supervises generation with collaborative rewards and flow balance; HCPD directly matches teacher conditional preferences over legal prefix branches, using the same DuoRec teacher.; where: REGER v1, Section 5.4 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS4.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: apao; relation: competitor; note: APAO-pointwise is a compared GR training objective; HCPD instead distills full conditional distributions over legal next tokens along observed target paths.; where: REGER v1, Sections 4.3.2/5.1 and Table 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p4; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.SS1.p3; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S5.T2.
- id: pctx; relation: predecessor; note: REGER follows Pctx in choosing DuoRec as its auxiliary recommender, but transfers collaborative preferences through distillation rather than personalized tokenization.; where: REGER v1, Section 4.3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37584v1#S4.SS3.SSS2.p1.

## ReRankID

- Page: pages/papers/rerankid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: R-KM†; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+Greedy
- TL;DR: ReRankID is a controlled testbed, not a new recommender: models reason over and rerank slates shown only as Semantic IDs, and the paper compares post-training methods for this task.
- [Code](https://github.com/lilv98/ReRankID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Kuaishou OpenOneRec-RecIF short-video release, 162074 source users; evaluation requires a renderable positive and >=256 items with both SID/caption histories.
  - Source: Section 3 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A5.p1
- **Split**: User-disjoint SFT/post-training/development/test partitions; 400 development and 400 test users, each balanced 200 explicit-engagement/200 long-view positives; histories precede targets.
  - Source: Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p1
- **Candidates**: sampled: 29 negatives plus one positive at anchor; slate sizes 10/20/30/50/100. Exposure-hard negatives plus uniform catalog fill; user-engaged items excluded. Exclusion of other historical exposures: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix A.2-A.3: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS3.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; evaluation release users/items were exposed during backbone pretraining, while post-training users are disjoint. Reranking supplied slates is a new task.
  - Source: Appendix A.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS4.p3
- **SID**: Released OpenOneRec three-code SIDs from quantized item-text embeddings; quantizer algorithm, codebook sizes and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Section 3 and Appendix A.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A1.SS1.p1
- **Inference budget**: SID: greedy reasoning 2048 tokens, fallback structured extraction 256 tokens from <=1200 reasoning characters; top-10 indices; A100/BF16. Text APIs: 8192-32768 output-token caps. Inference batch and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Appendix B.1, Table B.2 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A2.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A2.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A5.p2
- **Results from**: This testbed's paired evaluations: Table 1 initial models/references, Table 2 post-training, Table D.1 full metrics. Each post-training method compares its own initializer; invalid outputs score zero.
  - Source: Tables 1/2/D.1 and Section 5.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#A4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S5.SS1.p1

### Related

- id: onerec-think; relation: alternative; note: OneRec-Think reasons before catalog-item generation; ReRankID reasons over a supplied candidate slate.; where: ReRankID v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TIGER's SID-generation paradigm is the background contrasted with SID-only slate reranking.; where: ReRankID v1, Section 2: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.22797v1#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.

## ReSID

- Page: pages/papers/resid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Attr+CF; Tokenization: GAOQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: ReSID learns item representations from structured features with field-aware masked autoencoding and quantizes them with globally aligned orthogonal quantization, instead of LLM embeddings and generic quantizers.
- [Code](https://github.com/FuCongResearchSquad/ReSID)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon 2023: Musical Instruments, Video Games, Industrial/Scientific, Baby Products, Arts/Crafts/Sewing, Sports/Outdoors, Toys/Games, Health/Household, Beauty/Personal Care, Books. User/item 5-core; require store and three category-level fields.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **Split**: Chronological per-user last/penultimate interactions test/validation; sliding training windows, maximum length 32. Evaluation target items absent from training are added to the training set.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix E specify ranking metrics but no candidate protocol; 128 sampled negatives are a training objective: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p2
- **Visibility**: warm; evaluation target items absent from training are added to the training set.
  - Source: Appendix C explicitly inserts evaluation-only items into training: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A3.p1
- **SID**: GAOQ, 3 levels. Branching tuples: MI(32,40,19),VG(32,64,13),IS(24,80,14),BP(32,64,18),ACS(64,96,16),SO(128,128,11),TG(192,192,5),HH(50,512,8),BPC(96,192,11),Books(256,256,8). Global anchor-vocabulary sizes and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Table 7 and Algorithm 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.T7 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#alg1
- **Inference budget**: Beam 50; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Inference hardware, batch size, latency: not reported; batch 2048 is training.
  - Source: Section 4 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S4.p6 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p4
- **Results from**: Tables 1/4 aggregate/full main comparison; Tables 2/5 ablations; Table 3 quantization runtime, not inference latency. All SID methods use this study's common T5-style generator; tokenizer settings follow original methods.
  - Source: Tables 1-5 and Appendix E: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#S5.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A0.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A0.T5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.02338v1#A5.p3

### Related

## Retrieval-Grounded-Credit

- Page: pages/papers/retrieval-grounded-credit.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam

## ROS

- Page: pages/papers/ros.md
- Venue: ACL’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Geo; Tokenization: Geo-Prefix+RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+C-Beam
- TL;DR: ROS adds hierarchical spatial Semantic IDs, a mobility chain-of-thought with locality-informed pruning, and spatial-guided reinforcement learning to LLM-based next-POI generation.
- [Code](https://github.com/amap-cvlab/Reasoning-Over-Space)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY, Gowalla CA, prepared with the LLM4POI pipeline: users and POIs with fewer than 10 check-ins removed, trajectories segmented by a 24-hour time-gap threshold, and street-level addresses added by reverse geocoding. Sizes after preprocessing (users / POIs / check-ins): NYC 1,048 / 4,981 / 103,941; TKY 2,282 / 7,833 / 405,000; CA 3,957 / 9,690 / 238,369.
  - Source: Datasets and LLM4POI pipeline: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1; 24-hour gap and sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#A1.T10.
- **Split**: Temporal 80% / 10% / 10% train/validation/test split. Separate cross-city test: train on one city and evaluate on others.
  - Source: Temporal 80/10/10 split keeping test users and POIs observed: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1; cross-city: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T6.
- **Candidates**: n/a for candidate ranking: the model outputs exactly one POI per request and is scored by HR@1.
  - Source: One recommendation per request, HR@1: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; validation and test users and POIs are kept only if observed in training. The cross-city test (Table 6) uses POIs of another city; their tokenizer exposure is not reported.
  - Source: Test users and POIs observed in training: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Hierarchical spatial SID [g; s; u]: two S2-cell locality tokens (after removing the dataset-wide common prefix), two semantic tokens from a 2-level residual quantizer with 28 codes per level over Qwen-0.6B category embeddings, and a sequential suffix token within each (g, s) pair that makes IDs unique (at most 8 suffix values observed).
  - Source: HS-SID construction: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Generates a mobility chain-of-thought and then one POI SID per request (three inference runs averaged); decoding settings not reported. Qwen3-4B student on 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: One output per request, hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (HR@1 on NYC, TKY, CA versus traditional, neural, and LLM-based baselines); Tables 2-5 and Figure 3 (SID design, CoT stages, geographic cues, reward weights); Table 6 (cross-city generalization).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T1; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T5; RL weights: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.F3; cross-city: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T6.

### Related

- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID quantizes POI embeddings without explicit spatial structure; ROS builds S2-cell locality tokens plus semantic codes and adds mobility chain-of-thought and spatial RL.; where: ROS v2, LLM-based baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T1.
- id: spacetime-gr; relation: competitor; note: SpaceTime-GR also generates next POIs with an LLM; ROS adds hierarchical spatial SIDs and explicit reasoning before the recommendation.; where: ROS v2, LLM-based baselines (ST-GR): https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S3.T1.
- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc injects geography into the SID input and rewards; ROS encodes geography directly as S2-cell prefix tokens.; where: ROS v2, Section 1 cites OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S1.p3.
- id: lgsid; relation: alternative; note: LGSID aligns embeddings with geographic rewards before quantization; ROS separates geographic and semantic tokens inside the SID.; where: ROS v2, Section 1 cites LGSID: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.04562v2#S1.p3.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On NYC, ROS reports HR@1 of 0.4478 against 0.4027 for CoAST (+11.2%), and the paper reports gains of +11.0% on TKY and +15.7% on Gowalla-CA over the strongest LLM-based baselines (Table 1).
Limitation: A monotonic prior treats long moves within short intervals as unlikely, so ROS can underweight fast trips by metro rail or highway, especially near transit hubs (Limitations).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

LLM-based generative recommenders make limited use of geographic signals, which matter in mobility and local-service scenarios (Abstract). ROS models the next visit as a sequence of constrained decisions driven by time, intent, and geography (Sec. 2.3). It represents each POI with a hierarchical spatial Semantic ID (SID) that encodes locality and POI semantics (Abstract).

> "We present ROS, a generative next POI recommendation framework that treats geography as an explicit decision variable." (Sec. 5)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Check-ins") --> B["Spatial SID: S2 prefix + anchor + suffix"]:::key
    B --> C["SID grounding + sequence pretraining"]
    C --> D["Mobility CoT"]
    D --> E["Spatial-guided GRPO"]
    L1{{"Haversine + SID match + format"}} -.-> E
    E --> F("Next POI")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Hierarchical Spatial SID

Each POI SID has a geospatial prefix, a semantic anchor, and a discriminative suffix (Sec. 2.2.1). The prefix takes the POI's S2 Cell ID, written as hexadecimal digits, removes the prefix shared by all POIs, and groups the remaining digits into tokens. The semantic anchor embeds the POI's category description with Qwen-0.6B and quantizes it with an RQ-VAE.

#### SID Grounding

Bidirectional alignment trains the model to predict the SID from text and to generate text from the SID (Sec. 2.2.2).

> "This bidirectional alignment grounds SID tokens in functional semantics and fine-grained neighborhood cues." (Sec. 2.2.2)

Sequence pretraining then trains next-POI prediction on SID sequences, where the model learns recency, category repetition, and neighborhood continuity.

#### Mobility Chain-of-Thought

The model reasons in three deterministic stages: it profiles the user, builds an intent-aligned candidate space, and prunes candidates (Sec. 2.3). Pruning uses temporal consistency, semantic fit, and spatial feasibility from street addresses and transition distances.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    U["Profile the user"] --> C["Build intent-aligned candidates"] --> P["Prune: time, semantics, space"] --> A("Answer")
```

#### Spatial-Guided RL

GRPO optimizes a unified reward (Sec. 2.4.3). The reward combines the Haversine distance between the predicted and true POI (Sec. 2.4.1), a hierarchical SID match with a bonus for an exact match (Sec. 2.4.2), and a format term.

### 3. Experimental Findings

- CoT stages: the best result needs all three stages together (Sec. 3.3, Table 3).
- Cross-city transfer: trained on one city and applied to two unseen cities, ROS achieves the best transfer results against LLM4POI and GA-LLM (Sec. 3.4, Table 6).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- GNPR-SID quantizes POI features with a plain `RQ-VAE`; ROS puts an explicit S2-cell prefix before the semantic codes (`Geo-Prefix+RQ-VAE`).
- SpaceTime-GR uses geographic indices only (`Geo`, `Geo-Idx`); ROS adds category semantics to the SID and reasons before decoding (`CoT+C-Beam`).

## RPG

- Page: pages/papers/rpg.md

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: RPG compares its parallel OPQ-token prediction and graph-constrained decoding with TIGER's autoregressive RQ-VAE-token generation.; where: RPG v1, Section 2.1.1 describes OPQ: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS1.SSS1.p1; Section 2.4.2 explicitly contrasts TIGER: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.SS4.SSS2.p1; Section 3.1 names the TIGER baseline and Table 2 compares results: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S3.SS1.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05781v1#S2.T2.
