## Think2Go

- Page: pages/papers/think2go.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Attr+Geo+CF†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: CoT+Beam
- TL;DR: Think2Go unifies supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning reasoning for next-POI generation, weighting advantages by prompt epistemic uncertainty and normalized rewards, to deepen the LLM's understanding of Semantic IDs.
- [Code](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18206701)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Foursquare NYC and TKY (April 2012-February 2013) and Gowalla CA (February 2009-October 2010), preprocessed as in GNPR-SID: POIs with fewer than 10 interactions and users with fewer than 10 check-ins removed. Sizes (users / POIs): NYC 1,083 / 5,135; TKY 2,293 / 7,873; CA 6,592 / 14,027.
  - Source: Datasets and GNPR preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T1.
- **Split**: Records sorted chronologically and split 80% / 10% / 10% for training, validation, and test; for each user the last check-in is the answer. Separate cross-city transfer test (Table 5).
  - Source: Temporal 80/10/10 with last check-in as answer: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; cross-domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Acc@1, 5, 10 and MRR over the predicted top-K POIs.
  - Source: Acc@K and MRR over predicted lists: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; users and POIs that do not appear in training are removed from the test set. The cross-city transfer (Table 5) tests POIs of another city; their tokenizer exposure is not reported.
  - Source: Test users and POIs absent from training removed: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: Listwise semantic IDs built with RQ-VAE, which the paper contrasts with the pointwise semantic IDs of GNPR; numerical levels, codebook sizes, and collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Listwise semantic IDs whose correlations are learned through RQ-VAE, contrasted with GNPR's pointwise IDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS5.p2; numerical settings not found.
- **Inference budget**: Reasoning generated with vLLM (max length 1,024, temperature 1.3, 4 rollouts, beam search width 10) before the POI SID; LLaMA3.1-8B with LoRA. Five NVIDIA L40s GPUs (four for training, one for rollout inference); latency: not reported.
  - Source: Rollout and decoding settings, hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#A1.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (NYC, TKY, CA versus traditional, sequence, GCN, LLM, and reasoning baselines); Table 3 (ablations); Table 4 (SID category prediction versus GNPR); Table 5 (cross-city generalization).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T3; SID understanding: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T4; cross-domain: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.

### Related

- id: gnpr-sid; relation: competitor; note: GNPR-SID trains SID knowledge by SFT alone; Think2Go adds reasoning tokens and advantage-calibrated GRPO over the same kind of POI semantic IDs and generalizes better across cities.; where: Think2Go v1, LLM-based baselines and preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS2.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.SS1.p1; Tables 2, 4, 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S5.T5.
- id: onerec-think; relation: alternative; note: OneRec-Think adds reasoning to industrial video recommendation; Think2Go applies RL-trained reasoning to next-POI prediction with SIDs.; where: Think2Go v1, Section 2.2 cites OneRec-Think: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S2.SS2.p1.
- id: oneloc; relation: alternative; note: OneLoc is a geo-aware generative recommender trained without explicit reasoning; Think2Go relies on reasoning to use spatial context.; where: Think2Go v1, Section 1 cites OneLoc: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28997v1#S1.p4.

### Notes

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Next-POI recommendation learns from sparse and complex mobility patterns (Abstract). The authors argue that non-reasoning models lack the capacity to capture deep intent from them, and that LLMs understand Semantic IDs (SIDs) poorly when the SIDs are trained separately from the model (Abstract, Sec. 5.8). Think2Go lets an LLM reason before it recommends, and trains memorization and reasoning in one architecture instead of running SFT and RL one after the other (Sec. 4, Sec. 4.1).

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("SID history + time") --> B("Think")
    B --> C("Go: first prediction")
    C --> D("Self-correct prompt")
    D --> E("Answer")
    B -.-> L1{{"RL: progressive reward"}}
    E -.-> L2{{"SFT"}}
    L1 -.-> P["Policy"]
    L2 -.-> P
    W["STEU + DRG advantage weights"]:::key -.-> L1
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Unified SFT and RL

The model input contains SIDs and temporal information only (Appendix E). During training, the model reasons and makes a first prediction, then a fixed self-correct prompt is appended, followed by the correct answer (Sec. 4.1, Table 7).

> "This forms a Think–>Go–>Self–correct–>Answer structure, where tokens from the reasoning trace are used for RL, and tokens from the appended answer are used for SFT." (Sec. 4.1)

#### Progressive Reward

The reward first favors well-formatted responses and then semantically correct answers (Sec. 4.2.2). Correctness is scored on the decomposed SID units.

#### Calibrated Advantage

Standard group advantages give the same update weight to easy and hard samples (Sec. 4.2.3). Think2Go adds two weights. Kernel density estimation measures how well the query matches the user's spatial-temporal history, and this epistemic uncertainty changes the update size (Sec. 4.2.1, Sec. 6).

> "challenging samples with high epistemic uncertainty and correct predictions receive larger updates to encourage exploration, while incorrect predictions are updated conservatively to ensure robustness." (Sec. 4.2.1)

The second weight rescales the group advantage by the reward relative to the maximum reward, so that the absolute performance signal is kept (Sec. 4.2.4, Eq. 9). The authors describe the combination as an implicit curriculum.

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Ablation: Table 3 removes the reasoning tokens, the epistemic-uncertainty weight (STEU), the reward-informed weight (DRG), and a token entropy bonus (Sec. 5.5).
- Entropy: the reward-informed scaling keeps the entropy of reasoning tokens high during training (Sec. 4.2.4, Sec. 5.6, Fig. 3).

  > "Through comparative experiments, we further observe that it effectively alleviates entropy collapse by maintaining a high entropy level for the reasoning tokens, which implies greater exploration capacity." (Sec. 4.2.4)

- SID understanding: given a SID and ten candidate categories, the model identifies the correct category, compared against GNPR (Sec. 5.7, Table 4). The prompt for this task includes one example (Appendix C.2, Table 8).
- Out-of-domain: Think2Go degrades less than the other methods on out-of-domain datasets (Sec. 5.8, Table 5).
- Efficiency: against Refine-POI trained on NYC, the paper reports training time per epoch, test time, and memory (Appendix E, Table 10).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- GNPR-SID trains on `RQ-VAE` POI SIDs with `NTP` only and has no reported inference strategy (`–`); Think2Go adds an RL stage (`NTP → RL`) and reasons before decoding (`CoT+Beam`).
- ROS also reasons before decoding (`CoT+C-Beam`) but puts geography into the SID itself (`Geo-Prefix+RQ-VAE`); Think2Go keeps a plain `RQ-VAE` SID and models space through the advantage weights.

## TIGER

- Page: pages/papers/tiger.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’23
- Problem: Paradigms, Systems and Benchmarks
- Stage: No single stage
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: TIGER encodes item text into RQ-VAE Semantic IDs and trains a Transformer encoder-decoder to decode the next item's ID, instead of retrieving items by approximate nearest neighbor search.
- [Code (third-party)](https://github.com/baiyimeng/TIGER)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Product Reviews (May 1996-July 2014): Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games. Users with fewer than 5 reviews are filtered; an item-frequency filter is not reported. Retained item counts: 12,101 / 18,357 / 11,924, respectively.
  - Source: Dataset/date range and user-only filtering: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1; corpus sizes: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.T6.
- **Split**: Chronological per-user leave-one-out: last interaction for test, penultimate for validation, earlier interactions for training; training histories contain at most 20 items. Separate Beauty cold-start experiment: remove 5% of test items from the training split.
  - Source: Chronological ordering, exact leave-one-out allocation, and training-history cap: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. The separate Beauty cold-start manipulation removes 5% of test items from the training split: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **Candidates**: Main evaluation: full catalog versus sampled candidates not reported. Cold-start retrieval adds unseen items sharing the first three codes with a generated SID to the matching seen item; epsilon caps the proportion of unseen items in the returned top-K list (epsilon=0.1 in Fig. 5a).
  - Source: Full-catalog versus sampled-negative evaluation is not specified in Methods/Experiments or Appendices A-E; the evaluation description is https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1. Cold-start candidate construction and unseen-item quota: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p4; epsilon=0.1 comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p5.
- **Visibility**: Main leave-one-out evaluation: per-target generator/tokenizer training visibility not reported. Beauty cold-start experiment: unseen by tokenizer too; the selected items are removed from the training split, both RQ-VAE and the generator are trained on that split, and unseen-item SIDs are produced afterward.
  - Source: Main preprocessing defines interaction holdouts without explicitly enumerating item-level training visibility: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. For the cold-start experiment both RQ-VAE and the sequence-to-sequence model are trained on the reduced training split; unseen items are encoded afterward: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS3.p3.
- **SID**: Main configuration: 3 residual-quantization levels x 256 codewords (32-dimensional code embeddings), plus a fourth collision-disambiguation token, giving 4 tokens per item. Colliding three-code tuples receive different fourth tokens; non-colliding tuples receive 0. The generator uses 4 x 256 item-token entries.
  - Source: Main RQ levels, codebook cardinality, latent dimension, and collision suffix including zero for a unique tuple: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4. Four position-specific 256-token vocabularies: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p5; one-time collision lookup: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S3.SS1.p8.
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive beam search; numerical beam width not reported. Main evaluation: Recall and NDCG at K=5 and 10. Cold-start Fig. 5a varies K at epsilon=0.1; Fig. 5b evaluates Recall@10 while varying epsilon. Hardware, inference batch size, and measured latency: not reported.
  - Source: Autoregressive beam search: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.p3; main metric cutoffs: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p2; cold-start cutoffs/quota experiment: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. No numerical beam width, inference hardware, inference batch size, or latency is specified after checking Methods/Experiments and Appendices A-E; https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.p6 give training batches only.
- **Results from**: Original paper Table 1 (main sequential recommendation); Appendix E, Table 9 (three-seed means and standard errors); Fig. 5 (Beauty cold start). Table 1 combines the authors' TIGER results, previously published S3-Rec benchmark results for baselines other than P5, and P5 rerun with modified preprocessing.
  - Source: Original main comparison: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.T1; separate three-seed mean/standard-error table: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A5.T9; cold-start: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.F5. Baselines except P5 were taken from S3-Rec's published results; P5 was rerun with modified preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#S4.SS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2305.05065v3#A4.p2.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Key Findings: On Amazon Beauty, TIGER reports Recall@5 of 0.0454 against 0.0387 for SASRec, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs outperform LSH and random IDs (Tables 1 and 2).
Limitation: The authors state that beam search can make TIGER more expensive than ANN-based retrieval at inference (Appendix E).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

Large-scale recommenders usually embed users and items in one space and select candidates by approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search (Abstract). The authors describe TIGER as the first Semantic ID-based generative model for recommendation (Sec. 2). Many later papers in this list keep this Semantic ID (SID) pipeline and change one of its stages.

> "We propose a new paradigm of building generative retrieval models for sequential recommendation." (Sec. 1)

### 2. How It Works

#### Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("Item text") --> B["Sentence-T5: 768-dim"]
    B --> C["DNN encoder: 32-dim"]
    C --> D["RQ-VAE, 3 levels × 256"]:::key
    D --> E("SID + collision token")
    E --> F["Enc-Dec generator"]
    L1{{"NTP over 4 tokens"}} -.-> F
    F --> G["Beam search"]
    G --> H("Items via lookup table")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Step 1: Item Text to a Latent Vector

TIGER builds a sentence from each item's title, price, brand, and category, and the pre-trained Sentence-T5 model encodes it into a 768-dimensional embedding $`\mathbf{x}`$ (Sec. 4). A DNN encoder $`E`$ with intermediate layers of size 512, 256, and 128 and ReLU activations maps $`\mathbf{x}`$ to a 32-dimensional latent vector $`\mathbf{z} = E(\mathbf{x})`$ (Sec. 4).

#### Step 2: Residual Quantization into Codes

RQ-VAE quantizes the residual left by the previous level, so each level refines the code of the level before it.

> "Residual-Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (RQ-VAE) [40] is a multi-level vector quantizer that applies quantization on residuals to generate a tuple of codewords (aka Semantic IDs)." (Sec. 3.1)

TIGER uses $`M = 3`$ levels, each with a codebook of $`K = 256`$ codewords of dimension 32 (Sec. 4). At level $`m`$:

```math
\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{z}, \qquad c_m = \arg\min_{k \in \{0, \dots, K-1\}} \left\| \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_k^{(m)} \right\|_2^2, \qquad \mathbf{r}_{m+1} = \mathbf{r}_m - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{r}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{32}`$ is the residual that enters level $`m`$;
- $`\mathbf{e}_k^{(m)}`$ is codeword $`k`$ of the level-$`m`$ codebook;
- $`c_m`$ is the code chosen at level $`m`$.

```python
import torch

def rqvae_quantize(z, codebooks, beta=0.25):
    """
    z:         [B, 32] latent vectors from the encoder E(x)
    codebooks: list of M tensors, each [K, 32] (M = 3, K = 256)
    """
    r = z
    z_hat = torch.zeros_like(z)
    codes, vq_loss = [], 0.0
    for E_m in codebooks:
        # nearest codeword at this level
        c_m = torch.cdist(r, E_m).pow(2).argmin(dim=-1)                     # [B]
        e_m = E_m[c_m]                                                       # [B, 32]
        # codebook and commitment terms of the quantization loss
        vq_loss = vq_loss + (e_m - r.detach()).pow(2).mean() + beta * (r - e_m.detach()).pow(2).mean()
        # straight-through estimate, then the residual for the next level
        z_hat = z_hat + r + (e_m - r).detach()
        r = r - e_m.detach()
        codes.append(c_m)
    return torch.stack(codes, dim=-1), z_hat, vq_loss                        # [B, M], [B, 32], scalar
```

Simplifications: The code shows only the quantization loop and the quantization loss. It omits the DNN encoder and decoder, the reconstruction loss, and the k-means codebook initialization.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Z("z") --> L1["Level 1: nearest codeword c1"]
    L1 --> R2("r2 = z - e(c1)")
    R2 --> L2["Level 2: nearest codeword c2"]
    L2 --> R3("r3 = r2 - e(c2)")
    R3 --> L3["Level 3: nearest codeword c3"]
    L3 --> S("(c1, c2, c3)"):::key
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Step 3: Tokenizer Training

A decoder $`D`$ reconstructs $`\hat{\mathbf{x}} = D(\hat{\mathbf{z}})`$ from the sum of the selected codewords $`\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \sum_{m=1}^{M} \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}`$. RQ-VAE trains the encoder, decoder, and codebooks with a reconstruction loss and a quantization loss:

```math
\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x}) = \|\mathbf{x} - \hat{\mathbf{x}}\|_2^2 + \sum_{m=1}^{M} \left( \left\|\mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{r}_m] - \mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}\right\|_2^2 + \beta \left\|\mathbf{r}_m - \mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{e}_{c_m}^{(m)}]\right\|_2^2 \right)
```

where:
- $`\mathrm{sg}[\cdot]`$ is the stop-gradient operator;
- $`\beta = 0.25`$ weights the commitment term (Sec. 4).

To prevent codebook collapse, TIGER runs k-means on the first training batch and uses the centroids to initialize the codebooks (Sec. 3.1).

#### Step 4: Collision Token

Several items can receive the same three codes. TIGER appends a fourth token so that every item has a unique SID: two items that share (12, 24, 52) become (12, 24, 52, 0) and (12, 24, 52, 1) (Sec. 3.1).

> "To remove the collisions, we append an extra token at the end of the ordered semantic codes to make them unique." (Sec. 3.1)

```python
from collections import defaultdict

def append_collision_token(code_tuples):
    """code_tuples: list of (c1, c2, c3), one per item."""
    seen = defaultdict(int)
    sids = []
    for t in code_tuples:
        sids.append((*t, seen[t]))   # 0 for the first item with this tuple, 1 for the second, ...
        seen[t] += 1
    return sids
```

The code assigns the fourth token in input order. The table that maps SIDs to items is built once after the tokenizer is trained and then frozen (Appendix E).

#### Step 5: Sequence-to-Sequence Generation

TIGER flattens a user's history into SID tokens and puts one user token in front. The raw user ID is hashed into one of 2,000 user tokens (Sec. 4). The generator is a Transformer encoder-decoder built with the T5X framework, with 4 layers each in the encoder and the decoder and 6 self-attention heads of dimension 64 (Sec. 4).

> "Given Semantic IDs for items in a user session, a Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence model is trained to predict the Semantic ID of the next item that the user will interact with." (Abstract)

The generator is trained with next-token prediction over the four tokens of the target SID:

```math
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{NTP}} = -\sum_{m=1}^{4} \log P_\theta\left(c_{t,m} \mid \mathbf{c}_{1:t-1},\, c_{t,1:m-1}\right)
```

where:
- $`\mathbf{c}_{1:t-1}`$ is the SID token sequence of the history items;
- $`c_{t,m}`$ is the $`m`$-th token of the target item's SID.

At inference, TIGER decodes SIDs with autoregressive beam search and maps each generated SID to an item through the frozen lookup table (Appendix E).

### 3. Experimental Findings

The three entries below compare TIGER with SASRec. S3-Rec is the strongest baseline in all four Sports and Outdoors columns (Table 1). It is also the strongest in Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on Beauty and on Toys and Games.

- Beauty: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0454, NDCG@5 = 0.0321, Recall@10 = 0.0648, and NDCG@10 = 0.0384, against 0.0387, 0.0249, 0.0605, and 0.0318 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Sports and Outdoors: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0264, NDCG@5 = 0.0181, Recall@10 = 0.0400, and NDCG@10 = 0.0225, against 0.0233, 0.0154, 0.0350, and 0.0192 for SASRec (Table 1).
- Toys and Games: TIGER reports Recall@5 = 0.0521, NDCG@5 = 0.0371, Recall@10 = 0.0712, and NDCG@10 = 0.0432, against 0.0463, 0.0306, 0.0675, and 0.0374 for SASRec (Table 1).
- ID ablation: Table 2 compares random IDs, LSH Semantic IDs, and RQ-VAE Semantic IDs. RQ-VAE IDs score highest and random IDs lowest in all twelve metric columns (Table 2).

  > "Our results show that RQ-VAE consistently outperforms LSH." (Sec. 4.2)

- Invalid IDs: for top-10 predictions, 0.1%–1.6% of generated IDs map to no item across the three datasets (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 6).
- Cold start: the authors state that SIDs improve retrieval of items with no prior interaction history (Abstract, Fig. 5).
- Diversity: temperature-based sampling during decoding controls the diversity of predictions (Sec. 4.3).
- ID length and codebook size: the authors also tried other settings, such as 6 codewords from codebooks of size 64 (Appendix E).

  > "We noticed that the recommendation metrics for TIGER were robust to these changes." (Appendix E)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Stated by the authors.**

> "we note that our model can be more computationally expensive than ANN-based models during inference due to the use of beam search for autoregressive decoding." (Appendix E)

**Our analysis.**

- TIGER's representation uses item text only (`Text`). LETTER uses text and collaborative signals (`Text+CF`) with a learnable RQ tokenizer (`Learn. RQ`).
- The tokenizer is fixed before the generator trains (`Fixed`). ETEGRec updates the tokenizer and the generator in turns (`Altern.`).
- Unconstrained beam search can produce IDs that map to no item (Sec. 4.5). LETTER decodes with constrained beam search (`C-Beam`).
- Beam search runs one generator step per SID token. RPG predicts all tokens of an SID in parallel (`Non-AR`) and decodes over a graph of valid IDs (`Graph`).

- Problem: I. Informativeness

## TokenRec

- Page: pages/papers/tokenrec.md
- Venue: TKDE’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: CF; Tokenization: Masked VQ; Backbone: Encoder; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Discrim.; Inference: Scoring
- TL;DR: TokenRec quantizes masked collaborative user and item representations into discrete tokens and retrieves top-K items without autoregressive decoding or beam search, to generalize to new users and items.
- [Code](https://github.com/Quhaoh233/TokenRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: LastFM (1,090 users / 3,646 items), MovieLens-1M (6,040 / 3,416), Amazon Beauty (22,363 / 12,101), Amazon Clothing (23,033 / 39,387 as printed); histories capped at 100 items. Filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Datasets and statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Leave-one-out: all but the last observation for training; histories are randomly shuffled to give non-chronological lists (to match collaborative-filtering baselines). Separate study on Beauty and LastFM: the 5% of users with the least history are removed from training as unseen users, and all items they interacted with are excluded from training too.
  - Source: Leave-one-out with shuffled histories: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1; unseen-user split: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS3.p2.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (scores all items in the item base and retrieves top-K). Training uses 1:1 negatives drawn at random from un-interacted items.
  - Source: Scores over all items for top-K retrieval; training negatives 1:1: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S2.SS4.SSS3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Unseen-user study: held-out users and every item they interacted with are excluded from the training split, so those items are unseen by the generator and the MQ-Tokenizer training (tokens for them are produced afterwards from their representations).
  - Source: Unseen-user study excludes those users' items from training: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS3.p2.
- **SID**: Masked vector-quantized tokenizer (MQ-Tokenizer) for both users and items: K parallel sub-encoders, each quantized against its own sub-codebook of L codes (K searched in 1-5, L in 128-1,024; prompt example uses K=3), over masked collaborative representations. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: K-way masked vector-quantized tokenizer, ranges: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S2.SS3.SSS3.p2, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S2.SS3.SSS3.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: No beam search: the T5 output is projected and all items are scored for top-K. Table 5: average top-20 inference time per user of 5.76-8.43 ms versus 76-102 ms for P5, POD, CID, and TIGER; hardware and batch size: not reported.
  - Source: Generative retrieval by scoring instead of beam decoding: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S2.SS4.SSS3.p3; timing: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T5.
- **Results from**: Tables 2-3 (LastFM, ML1M, Beauty, Clothing versus CF, sequential, and LLM-based baselines); Table 4 (seen versus unseen users); Table 5 (inference time); Table 6 (ablations).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T3; unseen users: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T4; time: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T5; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T6.

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER decodes RQ-VAE item IDs by beam search; TokenRec tokenizes users and items with a masked K-way quantizer and scores all items directly, about ten times faster.; where: TokenRec v3, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1; Tables 2-5: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T5.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: CID builds collaborative indices for P5-style text generation; TokenRec builds collaborative tokens for users and items and retrieves without decoding.; where: TokenRec v3, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.I2.i4.p1; Tables 2-5: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S3.T5.
- id: lc-rec; relation: alternative; note: LC-Rec decodes item indices autoregressively, which TokenRec avoids for speed and to limit hallucinated items.; where: TokenRec v3, Section 2.4.3 cites Zheng et al. (2024): https://arxiv.org/html/2406.10450v3#S2.SS4.SSS3.p1.
- id: r3-vae; relation: alternative; note: R3-VAE later evaluates TokenRec's masked quantizer (MQ) as a tokenizer baseline and proposes reference-guided residual quantization.; where: Evidence is from the later R3-VAE paper: baselines and Tables 1, 4: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.11440v3#S4.T4.

### Notes

## At a Glance

Limitation: New users and items need a retrained collaborative filtering model to produce their representations; only the tokenizer and the LLM stay frozen (Sec. II-E.2).

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

LLM-based recommenders need user and item tokens that the LLM can read (Abstract). One token per user or item expands the LLM vocabulary with the number of users and items (Sec. I). The authors also name two further gaps: existing tokens do not capture high-order collaborative knowledge, and they generalize poorly to users or items outside the training data (Abstract). TokenRec tokenizes users and items from collaborative representations and replaces autoregressive decoding with retrieval.

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("GNN CF representations") --> B["Random mask"]
    B --> C["K encoders + K codebooks"]:::key
    C --> D("User and item tokens")
    C --> E["Average codewords + MLP decoder"]
    E -.-> L1{{"Reconstruction loss"}}
    D --> F["LLM query encoder"]
    F --> G["3-layer MLP projection"]
    G --> H["Cosine vs GNN item representations"]:::key
    H --> I("Top-K items")
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### MQ-Tokenizer

A GNN-based collaborative filtering model learns user and item representations, which are stored in a vector database (Sec. II-C.2).

> "Specifically, our MQ-Tokenizer assigns each user and item a small number of discrete tokens generated by quantizing the GNN-based representations." (Sec. II-C.1)

The tokenizer randomly masks the representation, encodes it with K separate encoders, and quantizes each output against its own codebook (Sec. II-C.2, Sec. II-C.3). The decoder averages the K codewords and reconstructs the collaborative representation with an MLP (Sec. II-C.4, Eq. 9). User and item tokenizers are trained separately.

> "we propose to randomly mask these representations to create a challenging task that enables the tokenizer to build a comprehensive understanding and generalize well." (Sec. II-C.2)

#### Generative Retrieval

The LLM reads a prompt with the user's tokens and, optionally, the tokens of interacted items, which are shuffled during training rather than kept in time order (Sec. II-D.2). The LLM acts as a query encoder. A three-layer MLP projects its hidden state, and cosine similarity against the GNN item representations scores all items for top-K retrieval (Sec. II-D.3, Eqs. 17–19).

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Main comparison: TokenRec outperforms both traditional and LLM-based recommenders on the four datasets (Abstract, Tables 2 and 3).
- Inference time: the authors attribute the speed to retrieval instead of decoding.

  > "This can be attributed to our generative retrieval paradigm, bypassing the most time-consuming auto-regressive decoding and beam search processes of LLMs [ 29 ] ." (Sec. III-D)

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- TIGER decodes text-based `RQ-VAE` IDs with `Beam`; TokenRec builds tokens from collaborative signals only (`CF`) and ranks by `Scoring`, so it never generates an ID.
- CID also tokenizes collaborative signals (`CF`) but with `Spectral Clus.` and decodes with `C-Beam`; TokenRec uses `Masked VQ` and an `Encoder`.

## TopoGR

- Page: pages/papers/topogr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: BDQ; Backbone: Non-AR; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: MTP + Aux.; Inference: Scoring+Rerank
- TL;DR: TopoGR learns bit-decomposable binary Semantic IDs and uses their Hamming geometry in input features, soft training targets, and reranking, instead of treating Semantic ID tokens as independent symbols.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Review Sports & Outdoors, Beauty, Toys & Games, CDs & Vinyl; reviews treated as chronological interactions. Filtering and maximum history length not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #A1.T3
- **Split**: Leave-one-out with checkpoint selection by validation performance; exact train/validation/test holdout allocation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S5.SS1.p3
- **Candidates**: full catalog scored through vectorized SID-probability gathering, followed by top-1000 reranking; consumed-item exclusion not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S4.SS5.p1 ; #A1.SS4.p4
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S5.SS1.p1 ; #S5.SS1.p3 ; #S4.SS1.p8
- **SID**: BDQ/LFQ: 64 positions x 8 bits, each position mapping to 256 integer codes; implicit fixed binary vertices, not learned centroid codebooks. Reported full-SID collapse ratio <0.003; collision disambiguation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#A1.T4 ; #A1.SS3.p2 ; #A1.SS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: Parallel prediction of all 64 SID positions, full-corpus gather scoring and Hamming reranking of 1000 items; no beam search; Recall/NDCG@5/10. One H20 96GB is used for experiments; Figure 8 plots approximately 9 ms inference time on Beauty. Inference batch size and timing aggregation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S4.SS3.p3 ; #S4.SS5 ; #S5.SS1.p4 ; #A1.F8
- **Results from**: Table 1: four-dataset comparison; some baseline numbers adopted from Rajput et al. (2023), remaining datasets/models reproduced with official implementations or RecBole; exact reused rows not specified. Table 6: ablations; Figure 8: inference efficiency.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.25216v1#S5.T1 ; #S5.SS1.p4 ; #A2.T6 ; #A1.F8

## TRACER

- Page: pages/papers/tracer.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Soft Reassign. RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only / Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Joint; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: TRACER removes sensitive concepts from a generative recommender by reassigning concept-related items to alternative Semantic ID tokens with a coherence regularizer, instead of suppressing tokens shared with retained items.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

  - Source: Sec.4 models/baselines and Appendix D.1/D.2/D.4: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07688v1#S4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07688v1#S4.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07688v1#A4.SS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07688v1#A4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2606.07688v1#A4.SS4.p1

## TransRec

- Page: pages/papers/transrec.md
- Venue: KDD’24
- Problem: II. Uniqueness and Validity
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: Multi-Facet ID; Backbone: Enc-Dec / Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: FM-Index+Agg.
- TL;DR: TransRec indexes items with multi-facet identifiers combining ID, title, and attributes, constrains generation with FM-index substring indexing, and aggregates generated identifiers to rank catalog items.
- [Code](https://github.com/Linxyhaha/TransRec/)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty and Toys, plus Yelp. Release year and filtering thresholds: not reported. Items use random unique numeric IDs, titles and categories.
  - Source: Sec.4.1 Datasets and Appendix Table9: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#A1.T9
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: last item test, penultimate validation, remainder training. Full training uses all training users; few-shot selects 1024/2048 users. Discard oldest history items until input fits 1024 tokens (BART) or 512 (LLaMA).
  - Source: Sec.4.1 Datasets/Implementation and Sec.4.3.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported: full-catalog versus sampled evaluation and history-item exclusion are unspecified. Generated facet identifiers are aggregated into scores for in-corpus items.
  - Source: Sec.3.2 aggregated grounding and Sec.4.1 evaluation: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS2.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS2.SSS2.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2
- **Visibility**: Full-training item-level visibility: not reported. Few-shot tests the N training users plus N unseen users; warm requires both user and item warm, otherwise cold. Cold items are unseen by generator training, but the cold subset also includes unseen-user cases. Identifier construction reportedly uses only warm items; learned SID tokenizer n/a for manual facets. Cold-item exposure through the FM-index is not reported.
  - Source: Sec.4.2 and Sec.4.3.1 explicitly distinguish warm/cold users and items: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS3.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS3.SSS1.p2
- **SID**: Three separate facets: unique random numeric ID, title and categories. Variable text-token lengths; codebook size n/a. Numeric IDs provide uniqueness while titles/attributes can be shared. Training samples five title substrings per sequence and uses each category separately; this is not a quantized SID.
  - Source: Sec.3.1.1-3.1.2 and Appendix A.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS1.SSS1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS1.SSS1.p5 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS1.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#A1.SS2.p1
- **Inference budget**: FM-index-constrained beam20 for TransRec and LLM baselines; generate each facet, then aggregate grounding scores. Recall/NDCG@5/10. Table3 reports 218.43s grounding per 5000 Beauty users, not end-to-end request latency. Inference batch, hardware and generated-length cap: not reported; four RTX A5000 GPUs are explicitly the training setup.
  - Source: Sec.3.2 generation, Sec.4.1 implementation/evaluation and Table3: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S3.SS2.SSS1.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.T3
- **Results from**: This paper's Table1 full-training BART comparison, Table2 Beauty few-shot warm/cold comparison, Table3 grounding ablation, and appendix analyses. P5 is explicitly trained on sequential tasks with randomized IDs; Appendix A.3 implements indexing baselines and TransRec with the same T5-small backbone/single prompt. Borrowed-score attribution and run/seed counts: not reported.
  - Source: Tables1-3 and Appendix A.3/A.6: https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#A1.SS3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06491v2#A1.SS6.p1

## TriAlignGR

- Page: pages/papers/trialigngr.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+Img; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: Multi-task NTP; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: TriAlignGR adds visual content and LLM-mined user intents to Semantic ID construction and trains several generation tasks linking Semantic IDs, text, and images under one autoregressive loss.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 5

## TrieRec

- Page: pages/papers/trierec.md
- Venue: NeurIPS’26
- Problem: III. SID–Model Alignment
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed†; Objective: NTP†; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: TrieRec adds a trie-aware absolute positional encoding and a topology-aware relative positional encoding to Transformer generators, so attention reflects the Semantic ID prefix tree instead of a flat token stream.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Beauty, Toys, Food; MovieLens-1M. Standard 5-core filtering, histories retain the most recent 20 interactions.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Split**: Per-user most recent interaction test, penultimate validation, earlier interactions training.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1
- **Candidates**: Traditional models: full catalog; generative candidate universe not explicitly reported beyond a valid-item trie.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer/collaborative encoder exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1 defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1
- **SID**: Sentence-T5-base text features; RQ-VAE: 3 semantic levels x 256 codes, dimension 32, plus a fourth collision token. Select lowest-collision tokenizer checkpoint before appending the uniqueness digit; collision-token vocabulary size not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.4 and Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#A1.p1
- **Inference budget**: Constrained beam 10; Recall/NDCG@5/10. Hardware and inference batch size not reported. Figure 3 plots inference time on Beauty/Toy, but the inference panel lacks explicit units and numeric bar labels.
  - Source: Sections 4.1.2/4.4 and Figure 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.F3
- **Results from**: Original Tables 2/4: TrieRec on TIGER, CoST, LETTER and competing positional/structure encodings. Table 3: LETTER-based ablations.
  - Source: Section 4.2, Tables 2/4: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.T2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.T4 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.T3

### Related

- id: tiger; relation: predecessor; note: TrieRec adds trie-aware positional encodings to TIGER.; where: TrieRec v1, Sections 1/4.1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S1.p5; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- id: cost; relation: predecessor; note: CoST is the contrastive-tokenization backbone augmented by TrieRec.; where: TrieRec v1, Section 4.2 and Related Work: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S4.SS2.p2; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.21677v1#S5.p3.

## UGR

- Page: pages/papers/ugr.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → (RL + Rank); Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: UGR adds uncertainty to preference optimization through an uncertainty-weighted reward, difficulty-aware optimization, and explicit confidence alignment, instead of rewards based only on binary outcome correctness.
- [Code](https://github.com/cxfann/UGR)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Office (2016.10-2018.11), Industrial and Scientific (1996.10-2018.11), Yelp (2018.05-2018.11); user/item 5-core filtering, histories capped at 10.
  - Source: Appendix A/Table 5: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A1.p2 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A1.T5
- **Split**: Chronological 8:1:1 train/validation/test split; finer per-user allocation details not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1.1/Appendix A: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A1.p2
- **Candidates**: not reported; training rollout group size 16 is not an evaluation negative count.
  - Source: Section 4.1.2/Appendix C describes beam lists without full-catalog/sampled-negative evaluation specification: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS1.SSS2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A3.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Tokenizer exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: Section 4.1/Appendix A defines no unseen-item holdout: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A1
- **SID**: RQ-VAE on Qwen3-Embedding-4B item embeddings; 4 layers. Codebook sizes and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: Appendix C: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Qwen3-8B; beam 10; confidence computed post-generation. Experiments use 8 A100 GPUs; inference device allocation/batch size not reported. Office: 37.0 ms/query versus SFT/GRPO 32.9 ms; training rollout beam/group 16 is separate.
  - Source: Section 4.1.4/Appendix C/Table 6: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A3.p3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A3.T6
- **Results from**: Original Table 1: main comparisons, baselines reproduced from official repositories using best validation checkpoints; Table 2: staged ablations. Table 3: optional confidence reranking on Office, separate from main comparison.
  - Source: Table 1/Appendix B/Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#A2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.T3 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S3.T2

### Related

- id: minionerec; relation: competitor; note: UGR and MiniOneRec share the backbone; UGR adds uncertainty-aware optimization.; where: UGR v2, Section 4.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS2.p2.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER supplies the standard SID-based baseline for UGR's uncertainty-aware alignment.; where: UGR v2, Section 4.1.3 and Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S4.SS1.SSS3.p1; https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11719v2#S3.T1.

## UNGER

- Page: pages/papers/unger.md
- Venue: TOIS’25
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Representation
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: R-KM; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Ctr.; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: UNGER learns one integrated semantic-collaborative embedding through cross-modality alignment and next-item prediction, quantizes it into a unified code, and adds intra-modality distillation, instead of separate codes per modality.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2014: Beauty, Sports and Outdoors, Toys and Games; user/item 5-core.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.SS1.SSS1.p1 ; Table 2.
- **Split**: Per-user chronological leave-one-out: last item test, penultimate validation, earlier items training; training history capped at 20 items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3
- **Candidates**: not reported; full-catalog versus sampled evaluation and history exclusion are unspecified.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.SS1.SSS2 ; evaluation reports Recall/NDCG@10/20 but no candidate-pool protocol.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.SS1.SSS2.p3
- **SID**: DIN collaborative and Llama2-7b textual representations are integrated before fixed hierarchical k-means residual quantization; 4 levels, 256 clusters per level; item-code lookup table; main-tokenizer collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S3.SS3.SSS5 ; Algorithm 1; https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.T4
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive beam search, width 100; lookup and confidence ranking for top-k. Beauty speed comparison separately uses top-5 and beam 100; inference hardware and batch size not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S3.SS5.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.T4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S1.F4.fig1
- **Results from**: UNGER experiments averaged over 5 runs (seeds 2020–2024), with standard errors in Table 3; unstarred baseline scores copied from Zhou et al. (2020) and Wang et al. (2024c), starred TIGER and ColaRec scores reimplemented for missing statistics.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.SS2.SSS2.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S4.T3

### Related

- id: eager; relation: predecessor; note: Its dual-code design motivates UNGER's unified code.; where: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.06269v3#S1.p3 ; §3.3.5 follows its quantization approach; §4.2 baseline.

## UniRec

- Page: pages/papers/unirec.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+CF; Tokenization: RQ; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → DPO; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: UniRec prefixes each Semantic ID with category, seller, and brand tokens through Chain-of-Attribute, to recover the item-side feature crossing of discriminative models, and adds capacity-constrained quantization.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Shopee main-feed production logs over 9 consecutive days, billions of interactions (impressions, clicks, add-to-cart, purchases). Filtering and catalog size: not reported.
  - Source: Shopee production logs: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.
- **Split**: not reported (the 9-day window is described, but not how training and test are divided). Online A/B test in feed and landing scenarios (Table 5); duration and traffic: not reported.
  - Source: No train/test division stated; online A/B: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T5.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); Hit Ratio at 50, 100, 200 on all samples and on purchase samples.
  - Source: Hit Ratio on all and order samples: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.
- **SID**: Capacity-constrained residual K-means SIDs with 3 layers x 4,000 codes, using exposure-weighted capacity penalties (tolerance 1.05) instead of equal item counts; Chain-of-Attribute prefixes each SID with category tokens (L2, L3) decoded first. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: Capacity-constrained SIDs, 3 layers x 4000, tau=1.05; CoA attribute prefix: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.
- **Inference budget**: Autoregressive decoding of attribute tokens then SID tokens; beam width not reported. Online end-to-end latency 110 ms versus 266 ms for the traditional pipeline; hardware and batch size: not reported. Decoder-only model with cross-attention (d_model 256, 3 layers).
  - Source: End-to-end latency: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1; model size: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (HR on all and order samples versus SASRec, TIGER, OneRec-V2); Table 2 (CoA configurations); Table 3 (SID construction, ablation, scaling); Table 4 (multi-scene task-conditioned BOS); Table 5 (online A/B: orders +4.76%, GMV +5.60%).
  - Source: Results: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T4, https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T5.

### Related

- id: onerec-v2; relation: competitor; note: OneRec-V2 decodes SIDs with a decoder-only model over user context; UniRec first decodes coarse item attributes, uses exposure-capacity-constrained SIDs, and aligns to GMV with RFT and DPO.; where: UniRec v5, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.I2.i3.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER generates RQ-VAE IDs without any item-side attribute conditioning, which UniRec adds through Chain-of-Attribute.; where: UniRec v5, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.I2.i2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.T1.
- id: onerec; relation: predecessor; note: UniRec starts from OneRec's balanced quantization and replaces equal item counts with exposure-weighted capacity limits.; where: UniRec v5, Section 3.2: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S3.SS2.p1; RQ-KMeans ablation in Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12234v5#S4.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.
- id: capsid; relation: alternative; note: CapsID later compares against a UniRec-style Chain-of-Attribute patch and argues that a variable-length SID can avoid extra attribute decoding.; where: Evidence is from the later CapsID paper: baselines and Table 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2605.05096v1#S4.T3.

## UniSGR-V2

- Page: pages/papers/unisgr-v2.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Backbone
- Representation: –; Tokenization: –; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: –; Objective: NTP + Rank; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: UniSGR-V2 anticipates a continuous target-side feature vector before each codeword and crosses it with the semantic prefix and user behavior inside the decoder, using it for generation and ranking.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 3

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Lazada recommendation logs with impression, click, add-to-cart and pay behaviors; training: 2.42 billion samples, 6.46 million users, 7.53 million items.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p1
- **Split**: Chronological: first 30 days training, following day testing; validation split not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: not reported; full-catalog versus sampled retrieval evaluation and history exclusion are unspecified; ranking sample construction not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p3 ; HR@100/500 are output cutoffs, not a stated evaluation pool.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p1 ; Appendix A's cold-start prediction refers to the initial anticipation slot.
- **SID**: 3-level semantic IDs with 2,048 codewords per level; tokenizer inputs, quantization algorithm, training visibility and collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p4
- **Inference budget**: Beam search width not reported; paired prediction/code execution uses 3 sequential decoder calls; maximum history 1,024. Full TacGR: 701 QPS, mean latency 75.6 ms, P99 83.8 ms under matched production hardware/load; hardware specification, batch size and numerical memory-funnel schedule not reported; anchoring tower is training-only.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S3.SS5.SSS4.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p4 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#A2.T5 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S3.SS4.SSS2.p3 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S3.SS7.SSS2
- **Results from**: Own Lazada offline comparison, ablations and serving benchmarks; Table 1 averages 5 seeds. UniRec CoA reproduced on the same backbone; other baseline implementation provenance not reported. Own 40-day online A/B test on 10% traffic replaces UniSGR in one retrieval channel: IPV +0.79%, Order +5.55%, GMV +3.09%; other channels and downstream ranking retained.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.T1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS5.p1 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#A2.p1

- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: Semantic-ID generative retrieval baseline in Table 1.; where: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.SS1.p2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16132v2#S4.T1

## UniSID

- Page: pages/papers/unisid.md
- Venue: arXiv’26
- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text+Img+Attr; Tokenization: Direct SID Heads; Backbone: –; Tokenizer: –; Objective: –; Inference: –
- TL;DR: UniSID optimizes embeddings and Semantic IDs end to end from raw advertising data with multi-granularity contrastive learning and summary-based reconstruction, instead of embedding first and quantizing afterwards.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 2

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Tencent Ad-60W and Ad-100W multimodal advertising datasets, plus Amazon Beauty. Filtering rules not reported; public preprocessing is described only as standard practice.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.T1
- **Split**: Table 1 train/test counts: Ad-60W 500K/100K, Ad-100W 1M/1M, Beauty 12101/12101. Split procedure, count granularity and validation allocation not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.T1 ; #S4.SS1.p1
- **Candidates**: Embedding retrieval sampled: 1000 total (one positive plus 999 negatives); negative sampling distribution and history exclusion not reported. Next-ad and Beauty recommendation candidate protocols not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.SS1.p3
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. SID-model fitting exposure to test items not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.SS1.p1 ; #S4.SS1.p3 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **SID**: Three direct categorical SID heads x 2048 entries, using per-layer argmax on Qwen2.5-VL-3B outputs rather than residual quantization. Collision handling not reported.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S3.SS2.p3 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **Inference budget**: Beauty replaces the TIGER tokenizer with UniSID; industrial next-ad predictor details not reported. Metrics at K=1/5/10/20. Downstream decoding/beam, inference hardware, batch size and latency not reported; tokenizer training batch 512 is not an inference setting.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.SS1.p3 ; #S4.SS2.p5 ; #A1.SS3.p1
- **Results from**: Original Table 2: SID quality/next-ad prediction; Table 3: embedding retrieval; Table 5: ablations. Table 4: UniSID in TIGER on Beauty, with baseline results explicitly taken from LETTER.
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10445v3#S4.T2 ; #S4.T3 ; #S4.T4 ; #S4.T5 ; #S4.SS2.p5

## UniTok

- Page: pages/papers/unitok.md
- Venue: AAAI’26
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Multi-Dom; Tokenization: TokenMoE; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam†
- TL;DR: UniTok tokenizes items from multiple domains with a shared encoder, domain-specific and shared experts, and codebooks, calibrating mutual information across domains, instead of one tokenizer per domain.
- [Code](https://github.com/jackfrost168/UniTok)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Ten domains: Amazon Beauty, Cellphones, Grocery, Instruments, Office, Pet Supplies, Tools, Toys, Games, and Yelp, with title, category, and feature metadata; zero-shot targets Clothing, Health, and Sports. Sizes are in Appendix Table 6 (e.g. Beauty 22,363 users / 12,101 items; Yelp 30,431 / 20,033); filtering rules: not reported.
  - Source: Ten domains: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx1.p1; zero-shot targets: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx4.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#A4.SSx1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#A4.T6.
- **Split**: not reported in the main text (full-ranking evaluation per dataset; the train/test division is not restated). Zero-shot study: the tokenizer is trained on the ten source datasets and tested on three unseen domains.
  - Source: Split not restated in the extracted text.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (all non-interacted items are ranked for each user, so user history items are excluded).
  - Source: Full ranking over all non-interacted items: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx3.p1.
- **Visibility**: Main: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined. Zero-shot: items of the three target domains are unseen by the UniTok tokenizer; whether the T5 recommender saw them: not reported.
  - Source: Zero-shot domains unseen by the tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx4.p1.
- **SID**: 4-level residual quantization x 256 codes (dimension 32) inside each expert of a TokenMoE: one shared expert plus 10 domain experts (top-N routing, N = 1 or 2) over 2,048-dimensional language-model embeddings, with mutual-information calibration. Collision handling: not reported.
  - Source: 4 levels x 256 x 32 per expert, TokenMoE with shared and domain experts: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx4.p1, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#A4.SSx4.p3, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.SSx3.SSSx2.p3.
- **Inference budget**: Recommendation uses TIGER's T5 generator; beam width not reported. Experiments on two NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported. Table 2 compares trainable parameters (9.11M versus 87.78M accumulated for per-dataset tokenizers).
  - Source: TIGER T5 recommender and hardware: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#A4.SSx4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (ten datasets versus CF and tokenization-aided baselines); Table 2 (trainable parameters); Table 3 (competitors trained jointly across domains); Table 4 (zero-shot on unseen domains); Table 5 and later (ablations).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.T1; parameters: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.T2; unified training: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.T3; zero-shot and ablation in later tables.

### Related

- id: letter; relation: competitor; note: LETTER trains one regularized RQ-VAE tokenizer per dataset; UniTok shares one tokenizer across ten domains with a mixture of quantization experts.; where: UniTok v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p1; Tables 1-3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.T1, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.T3.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER is both a tokenizer baseline and the downstream T5 recommender; UniTok replaces per-domain RQ codebooks with routed experts.; where: UniTok v1, baselines and backbone: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#A4.SSx4.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec aligns an LLM to per-domain indices; UniTok targets one tokenizer for many domains.; where: UniTok v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p1; Tables 1 and 3: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.T1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.T3.
- id: cid; relation: competitor; note: P5-TID and P5-SemID (Hua et al., 2023) use titles or categories as IDs; UniTok learns codebook IDs.; where: UniTok v1, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx4.SSx1.SSSx2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.12922v1#Sx3.T1.

## UTGRec

- Page: pages/papers/utgrec.md
- Venue: arXiv’25
- Problem: VI. Generalization
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Multi-Dom; Tokenization: Tree; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP; Inference: Beam
- TL;DR: UTGRec builds a universal item tokenizer from a multimodal LLM with tree-structured codebooks, text and image reconstruction, and co-occurrence alignment, and pre-trains a generator that transfers across domains.
- [Code](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/UTGRec)
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023 with 5-core filtering. Pre-training on five domains (Arts Crafts and Sewing, Baby Products, CDs and Vinyl, Cell Phones and Accessories, Software; 999,334 users / 344,412 items in total); downstream on Musical Instruments (57,439 / 24,587), Industrial and Scientific (50,985 / 25,848), Video Games (94,762 / 25,612), Office Products (223,308 / 77,551).
  - Source: Pre-training and downstream domains, 5-core: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1; statistics: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.T1.
- **Split**: Per-user leave-one-out: latest item for test, second most recent for validation, the rest for training; the tokenizer and recommender are pre-trained on the five source domains and fine-tuned on each downstream domain.
  - Source: Leave-one-out allocation: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: full catalog (full-ranking evaluation over the entire item set).
  - Source: Full ranking and beam 50: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined (downstream items are seen during fine-tuning of both tokenizer and recommender).
  - Source: Downstream domains are fine-tuned on, no unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **SID**: Universal item tokenizer on Qwen2-VL-2B (LoRA) with tree-structured codebooks: root codebook 256 and leaf codebook 512, identifier length 3, shared across domains. Conflicts are resolved by reassigning the last-level code to the second-nearest or a farther code instead of appending an extra code.
  - Source: Tree-structured codebooks (root 256, leaf 512), L=3, last-level reassignment for conflicts: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S2.SS4.SSS1.p2; MLLM tokenizer: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Beam size 50 for all generative recommenders; tokenizer pre-training on 16 GPUs (batch 16 per GPU). Inference hardware, batch size, and latency: not reported.
  - Source: Beam size 50: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS3.p1; GPUs for tokenizer pre-training: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.SS1.SSS4.p1.
- **Results from**: Table 2 (four downstream domains versus traditional, content-based, and generative baselines including TIGER, LETTER, TIGER-M); Table 3 (ablations); later figures (analyses).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.T2; ablation: https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04405v3#S3.T3.

## V-STAR

- Page: pages/papers/v-star.md
- Venue: KDD’26
- Problem: IV. Utility
- Stage: Training
- Representation: Text†; Tokenization: RQ-VAE; Backbone: Dec-Only; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP → RL; Inference: C-Beam
- TL;DR: V-STAR deepens high-value prefixes with value-guided decoding during reinforcement learning sampling and computes sibling-relative advantages with Sibling-GRPO, instead of likelihood-driven beam search.
- Setup card: yes
- Relations: 4

### Setup card

- **Datasets**: Amazon Reviews 2023 Industrial and Scientific and Office Products, preprocessed following MiniOneRec (Kong et al., 2025b); online: WeChat Channels advertising traffic. Filtering and sizes: not restated.
  - Source: Datasets and MiniOneRec preprocessing: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1.
- **Split**: Chronological next-item prediction following MiniOneRec's preprocessing (allocation not restated). Online: 5-day A/B test on 5% of live requests, against beam search plus GRPO.
  - Source: Chronological next-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1; online A/B: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS3.p1.
- **Candidates**: not reported (full catalog versus sampled); generation is restricted to valid catalog SIDs, with HR and NDCG at 3, 5, 10.
  - Source: Valid-SID constraint and metrics: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1.
- **Visibility**: warm; no unseen-item protocol is defined.
  - Source: No unseen-item protocol: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1.
- **SID**: 3-level RQ-VAE semantic IDs (citing TIGER); the paper states each item is represented by a unique fixed-length SID. Codebook size and the mechanism that ensures uniqueness: not reported.
  - Source: 3-level RQ-VAE SIDs: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1; each item has a unique fixed-length SID: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S3.SS1.p1.
- **Inference budget**: Training rollouts use value-guided decoding (VED) with 16 candidates per query and an 8-wide beam to initialize the prefix tree; at inference, standard beam search is the default decoder (width not reported). Qwen2.5-1.5B on 8 GPUs; inference batch size and latency: not reported.
  - Source: VED budget, beam settings, inference decoder: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p2.
- **Results from**: Table 1 (Industrial and Office versus sequential, generative, and RL baselines including MiniOneRec); Tables 2-4 (decoding, expansion rules, training objective); Table 6 (candidate diversity and max reward); Section 5.3 (online GMV +1.23%).
  - Source: Main: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S4.T1; ablations: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.T2, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.T3, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.T4; diversity: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.T6; online: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS3.p1.

### Related

- id: minionerec; relation: competitor; note: MiniOneRec samples RL candidates by beam search and applies GRPO; V-STAR replaces candidate construction with value-guided prefix expansion and uses sibling-group advantages, while keeping MiniOneRec's preprocessing.; where: V-STAR v2, preprocessing follows Kong et al. (2025b): https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS1.p1; strongest RL baseline: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S4.T1.
- id: tiger; relation: competitor; note: TIGER's SIDs and beam search are the base; V-STAR targets the pruning of high-reward low-probability prefixes during RL sampling.; where: V-STAR v2, SID-based baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S4.T1.
- id: lc-rec; relation: competitor; note: LC-Rec is an SID-based LLM recommender without RL; V-STAR adds value-guided RL on top of SFT.; where: V-STAR v2, baselines: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S5.SS2.p1; Table 1: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S4.T1.
- id: onerec; relation: alternative; note: OneRec applies preference alignment with beam-sampled responses; V-STAR argues that probability-based beam sampling under-explores high-reward items.; where: V-STAR v2, Sections 1 and 2.3 cite OneRec: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S1.p1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10699v2#S2.SS3.p1.

### Notes

### 1. Why This Paper Matters

RL fine-tuning of generative recommenders samples candidates with likelihood-driven decoding such as beam search (Abstract). The authors name two failures of this setup. High-reward items in low-probability branches are pruned early, and candidates that share a high-probability prefix receive correlated rewards, which weakens the comparison signal for RL. A larger beam does not fix this, because it spends most extra compute on redundant high-probability candidates (Sec. 1). V-STAR changes how RL candidates are built and how their advantages are computed.

> "Our V-STAR primarily focuses on training-time improvement." (Sec. 4.4)

### 2. How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A("User context") --> B["Policy"]
    B --> C["Prefix tree from probability beam"]
    V["Value head"]:::key --> D
    C --> D["VED: expand nodes above depth-average priority"]:::key
    D --> E("Candidate set")
    E --> F{{"Sibling-GRPO"}}:::key
    F -.-> B
    classDef key fill:#eaf2fb,stroke:#6b8fc7
```

#### Value Head

A value head reads the policy's hidden state for each Semantic ID (SID) prefix and predicts its value (Sec. 4.1). Dense semantic returns for its training come from item embeddings computed by a frozen text encoder.

#### Value-Guided Efficient Decoding

VED treats SID decoding as building a candidate set on the prefix tree under a fixed compute budget (Sec. 4.2). A probability-guided beam initializes the tree. Each node's priority combines its predicted value with the policy entropy, and a node whose priority exceeds the average at its depth receives one new child (Eq. 11). The child is sampled from the unexpanded valid children by normalized policy probability.

> "We develop Value-Guided Efficient Decoding (VED) for budgeted candidate construction by allocating decoding compute to high-value and high-ambiguity nodes." (Sec. 1)

#### Sibling-GRPO

Sibling-GRPO groups the children of each parent prefix (Sec. 4.3). Each child's score is the mean reward of its descendant candidates, and advantages are normalized among siblings (Eq. 17).

> "We introduce Sibling-GRPO, a tree-structured objective that uses sibling groups to mitigate advantage compression under correlated candidates." (Sec. 1)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P("Parent prefix") --> A("Child a: mean reward of its candidates")
    P --> B("Child b: mean reward of its candidates")
    P --> C("Child c: mean reward of its candidates")
    A --> N{{"Normalize advantages among siblings"}}
    B --> N
    C --> N
```

### 3. Experimental Findings

- Decoding budget: under matched training-time decoding budgets, VED outperforms beam search on the tested metrics (Sec. 5.5, Fig. 4). The budget counts model-evaluated tokens during candidate construction, not end-to-end latency.
- Training objective: combining GRPO with Sibling-GRPO gives the highest NDCG and HR among the tested objectives (Sec. 5.4, Table 4).

### 4. Limitations & Critical Analysis

**Our analysis.**

- MiniOneRec uses the same `RQ-VAE` SIDs, `Dec-Only` generator, and `NTP → RL` training; V-STAR changes only how RL candidates are sampled and how advantages are computed.

## VarLenRec (TIGER)

- Page: pages/papers/varlenrec-tiger.md

- Problem: I. Informativeness
- Stage: Tokenization
- Representation: Text; Tokenization: HARQ; Backbone: Enc-Dec; Tokenizer: Fixed; Objective: NTP + Aux.; Inference: C-Beam
